PROS: Great design in all aspects; gorgeous world, always something to do, interesting challenges and puzzles, interesting abilities, nice OST, yadda yadda.
A lot of people are disappointed by the game, saying it's just a cheap Banjo Kazooie throwback, but I disagree. While many features are straight copied from BK, I find they either add to the immersion, gameplay, or fun factor in some way. Overall, the game is quite different from BK and builds upon its legacy in a great way. And it's not like you can't skip the dialogue if the voiceover annoys you...
I want to suggest that the grave disappointment is partly fueled by overly optimistic expectations and partly by the ~2 decades of gaming that have passed since then, and have made us more sensitive to the flaws in some games, depending on which genres we played the most or which aspects of game design we value most.
This game is definitely a very good platformer that can stand by itself. Don't approach it thinking it is the return of platforming Christ. It's just a really good game.
HOWEVER, there are some VERY big problem with the game, and they almost made me give the thumbs down: configurability is a hot mess, and it's not well optimised at all, plagued by technical shortcomings.
You have one linear scale by which to change the overall graphics quality of the game; this creates the very awkward situation where you either have to play with a gorgeous landscape and bad framerates, or an overall nice landscape with fine framerates, but shadows popping into existence maybe 3 meters in front of you, which is extremely jarring. There is no inbetween, no picking the graphical features most important to you, it behaves like a very bad port in this way.
However, it's still better than a highly configurable but utterly catastrophically performing port, such as Deus Ex: Mankind Divided.
The most jarring issue is the dramatic fps drop in the overworld though. You may have workable framerates at the highest graphical settings in the levels, but when you drop back into the tower, it starts to stutter like a senile grandma on Parkinson and you have to reduce the quality by two levels to get usable framerates. What the heck? At least it still looks fine.
Also, I can't use my Steam Controller with the game. I can't navigate the menues or the gameworld at all, regardless of my PC and Steam recognising and working with the controller flawlessly. This is a very sore disappointment, as I was looking forward to playing it on the TV per Steam Link. Controls in general are not configurable, full stop.
It's easily worth the ~25€ I paid for it during a sale, but I would've had some stomach aches if I had paid full price, though I'd still have enjoyed the game. My suggestion is to wait until it's on sale again and then grab it immediately.

An amazing game, it's definitely an improvement altogether from the very start of the series.  I really love the overall feeling while playing these games, they really capture the emotion (or lack thereof) of being an assassin travelling to the most diverse places in the world.  Being able to plan missions out with particular disguises, weapons, and tools beforehand is a nice option in gameplay.  Finding creative ways to assassinate your target is one of the best things about this game and offers such high replayability on every level.
The only major problem with HITMAN is that I have to wait for the new episodes to come out.  Call me impatient, but if I buy a 60 dollar game, I should be able to play it entirely at my own speed.  I understand if you are wanting to stretch out the game as much as possible to have players stay interested, but releasing each episode one at a time leaves me (and probably a few thousand others) frustrated.  This does NOT take away from the game itself, I blame whoever greenlit staggering the content releases month to month.  That is a TERRIBLE idea.  You are not creating anticipation but rather leaving yourself open to having players put this game on the backburner while waiting for episodes to come out.  That's exactly why these reviews went from 'Overwhelmingly Positive' to 'Mixed' after a month.
The option to pick your hit and try to take on other's challenging targets is very nice.  Some offer a bit of thinking and trial and error before figuring out the best route.  Some are nearly impossible to complete which is humbling and impressive to show off what some players are capable of doing.  The reward system is nice as well, unlocking more and more tools to help you in your profession as you fulfill each level's objectives.
All in all, the controls are smooth and comfortable, your standard Hitman controls with some changes.  The detail is impressive along with level setup and character design.  8/10 because I just want to play more of this game and they won't let me!

This game was very hyped up as being incredibly queer-friendly and enjoyable, and it turned out to be more than disappointing. I found the representation to be sub-par, as the words "gay," "queer," or even the outdated term "homosexual" were not used, which, in some cases can be positive, as it implies a future where we no longer need to label a dad who dates other dads a gay dad, but in this case, I did not care for. There was a transgender character, who was dealt with pretty well, but again, he was not explicitly labled as trans, it was implied and later confirmed. This representation is good, but it has caused a lot of transphobic/ignorant responses from people making fun of the character as effimate, as they do not realize he is trans and that they are being insensitive. Perhaps a clearer scene of him coming out could help. Given that this is a dating sim, I expected romance, scenes of actual sexual encounters, or at the very least, the dads being intimate with each other. I didn't need to see it, just know that it happened, and it was never explicitly stated. Also, there is a secret ending in which you learn that one of the dads is using the love between all of the other dads to power a demon, or for occult purposes, the idea of using gay love to power something insidious is really cool in theory, but in this game, has no place.
Very disappointing on many levels, bad, unimaginative gameplay, short game, not worth the money, poor queer representation. Basically bad Yaoi in a video game format.

To the former issue, it's fine. The game is basically done and only really needs a release to throw down 'chieves, pokemon cards, and all the other heavy-handed fanfare that accompanies even the most bizarre and unwarranted of steam releases. The most I can say is that the music is a bit finicky, going back and forth between desolate silence and ZOMG COMBAT!!! mode at points where one or the other would be more applicable. It almost brings up the question of why the game is even on Early Access at all. It seems like the developer genuinely seems to want quick feedback from players to help polish the final copy before release rather than doing a quick cash grab to make everyone pay 40 to 80 bucks for a glorified wireframe alpha build like everybody else does these days.
But there I go being cynical again. Now then, on to the gameplay.
The gameplay is standard rogue-likey stuff except the combat isn't total floaty garbage. It has a few glaring issues, but for the most part is quite solid. You fire your gun, your bullets the size of soda cans hit your enemies in the soft gubbins, and then they explode in one hit. Enemies actually take a bit to bring you down since you get a pretty generous healthbar for a roguelike, able to take six hits from most regular mobs until dying. Non-boss enemies die in one hit, as stated, but some of them will only do so if you hit them in a particular weak spot, like the power generator for turrets a-la-Receiver. After firing your coffee-can-sized rounds from your Ruger 2.00 caliber Velociraptor, you can pick your bullets back up again like firing a nerf gun and then OCD-ingly making sure you picked up all the foam darts even though you have three more in your pocket because losing them will haunt you for the rest of your days. This adds a surprisingly fun and compelling ammo dynamic where you always have very little ammo and yet paradoxically more ammo then you'd ever need.
In the first half of the game, there are three enemy types: snakes, chompers, and turrets. Interestingly, these enemies represent the best, average, and worst aspects of the combat respectively. Snakes lie in bushes almost perfectly camoflauged and strike at you out of nowhere, more than once causing me to jump out of my chair and scream random expletives. They can also poison you, which sucks just about as much as getting poisoned has since Final Fantasy One and Pokemon Red and Blue. As much as I would typically throw these off as "cheap" or "unfair", the ammo dynamic meant that I really didn't have any excuse not to throw a bunch of gigantic bullets into the bushes before I went exploring for health potions, so they actually helped endear me to the game.
The chompers are typical videogame fair. They charge at you mindlessly, bite you when they get up close, and die in one hit. Nothing special, but they get the job done. Later on in the game they "spice it up" by throwing spider chompers, flying chompers, or that eternal unwanted scourge of all shooters that is apparently as easy to shake off as Zaire-strain Ebola and just as entertaining, the Kamikaze chomper. SSDD really, but nothing wrong with mindless mooks in a shooter. If anything, they make the encounters with snakes all that more epic.
The turrets however are somewhat of a pain. To kill them, you have to hit them in their power generator, which can often be placed behind them when you enter the room. Often you'll have to thread your shots to hit their core, which would be easier if your bullets weren't the size of goddamn coelocanths. Often, you'll attempt to thread a shot only to have your enormous rounds ping ineffectually off the turret's impenetrable hide. The turrets however are bound by no such restraint, as the most common ones fire lasers, which will ALWAYS hit you if you're not moving and will usually hit you if you are. Luckily, they can be easily evaded by jumping over them which has the slight downside of a jump button NOT EXISTING IN THE GAME.
Which brings me to my main gripe about the combat. The combat is essentially a modified version of an InstaGib Railgun match in Quake or Unreal Tourney, and as such it is ABSOLUTELY INEXCUSABLE to not have a jump button. In addition, this would add to the dynamism of combat by allowing you to jump away from those evil snakes or jump over and around a horde of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. If anything should be added, I think this should be prioritised.
As to the rest of the game, it's a standard roguelike affair with upgrades, cash, and permadeath. Worth noting though is that the game has a rogue-lite banking system that allows you to store money for future runs, store valuable items, and even allow you to keep your items, upgrades, and a percentage of your unbanked money on death for a modest fee.
The problem with this aspect is that most of the upgrades just aren't worth their salt. Speed can be upgraded, but you already move like a crackhead. You can upgrade reload so that you mash in more bullets with each button press, but you can already reload as fast as you can push the button anyway. You can upgrade Bullet Magnet, but there's an item that does the same thing as having maximum rank in that stat, and it's pretty easy to find on each playthrough. The inventory system is a bit daft too, in that there really isn't one. You get to hold one item. That's it. This sounds pretty good in theory, especially for a roguelike, but in practice it means that you'll be ignoring just about every consumable you find because you found one item with a passive ability on it that turns you into a bullet god. Sure, you can upgrade your backpack to hold more items, but good luck saving up the 100 coins needed for that one, or having two items you want to store in the first place. In fact, why have a Bulletgod Relic and 3 consumable rockets when you could just have 2 Bulletgod Relics?
Really though, the game's actually pretty decent and it's worth a pickup if you enjoy roguelikes and other stuff like Receiver or Tower of Guns, though it lacks the intricate gameplay setup of the former and the depth and complexity of the other. If you're not into that kind of thing, it's still probably worth kicking about whenever it goes on sale. It's fun, but flawed, and that's honestly not half bad.
And it gets mad props for not using Early Access to act like a money-hoarding ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

The moment I start Heavy Bullets I'm assaulted with a minimal bright neon colored title-screen and a trippy melody with hazy vocals blaring over the glitched sounds of the menu like I've stumbled upon some kind of Philip K. Dickian Hotline Miami. I instantly think to myself "Yep this feels like something Devolver Digital would publish." This is of course a very good feeling.
This exceeds any rogue-like FPS before it in every way, and ups the ante by having very well-thought out and carefully planned gameplay. The action and combat are more than solid, intense and the atmosphere is engaging; with enemies that can pop out of bushes killing you in a heartbeat, the panic of realizing you haven't loaded all those bullets you picked up, all powered by a pulsing electronic soundtrack that creeps up on you as you come closer to dangerous areas.
The roguelike elements here work *very* well. You are placed into the thralls of a glitched neon world with harsh and bright hallways randomly generated everytime, the goal is to reach the end of each floor and eventually make it to the 8th floor where you're tasked with resetting a malfunctioning mainframe. Sounds simple, but equipped with only your 6-shot revolver this will prove to be a true test in frustration as there are monsters, turrets, and worms hiding around every corner to whittle away at your already very limited life. The floors are randomly littered with items to help with this, and you'll find banks where if you're playing smart enough you can buy life insurance or deposit money that carry over into your next playthroughs, making things slightly easier each time.
Seriously if you like roguelikes at all buy this game. If you like first person shooters at all, buy this game. If you like crazy artsy games with insanely stylish visuals and trippy sound design, buy this game!

As far as sports simulations go, this game is really fun to play but is also unbelievably unstable.  I've logged 23 hours according to Steam and so far I've had the game lock up to the point where I had to restart my PC, straight up crash, and have had my save file corrupted after completing my first season.  The stability issues are really unfortunate because I'm having so much fun with the game so far.
--Pros--

--Cons--

All together, I think I've gotten my $20 worth. I would pay $40-$50 for a new version of the game that addressed many of the stability issues and rounded out some of the rough edges.  If you want to tough through the stability issues by frequently saving and backing up your file, it's a fun game to play. However, those crashese are definitely coming. You've been warned.

If you had asked me in 2001 what I thought of Max Payne, you would have gotten an incredibly enthusiastic, positive answer. I freakin loved Max Payne, everything about it at the time was mindblowing, it was the first game to have competently done slo-mo, the storyline (at the time) was not only fairly dark and compelling, but also funny and self-aware, in a way much more subtle and enjoyable than something like Duke Nukem 3D. Visually mindblowing, with intensely cool effects like bullets being modelled, shell casings being modelled (dropping to the floor as you filled enemies with lead) and real world locations with explosive set-pieces and action.
At the time, it was absolutely mindblowing.
But now, it is pap. It is infuriatingly dated, it's like your grandpa who won't shut up about Vietnam or the Korean War or whatever and at first it was cool when you're a kid but now you're just depressed at his psychological devesation at the death of his friends, what? Nothing, nevermind.
Anyway, the root of the problem is that Max Payne's level design is absolutely donkey dongs, the AI behavior is entirely scripted so basically every moment of the game can be memorized, and you'll HAVE to memorize the more difficult segments, as they are difficult for exclusively arbitrary and crap reasons.
Since Max takes locational damage like any other enemies, your dives should almost exclusively be backwards with his feet facing forward, since diving forward is welcoming Max's instantaneous, welcomed release from his hellish torment of a life as bullets pile-drive his face and you get to watch in glee like you're some kind of kid from a special needs program who absolutely loves WWE.
But this mechanic is the biggest reason why this game is so frustrating, an enemy sprays you in the chest? Fine, you'll like lose most of your healthbar, but you'll live, a single shot in the head? Instadead. Max lies down with a look like his bunger screamed flaming diarrheatic doodoo in his moment of death.
Now this wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for a few things, one, this game loves deathtraps, and they aren't just environmental hazards like a door exploding or whatever, they'll be enemies that are scripted to run around a corner immediately, throwing a grenade down stairs (which there is only ever one correct direction to run away from, anything else gets you killed) and since the enemies' reactions are absolutely pearl beyond belief, you end up getting a face full of buckshot while they mug at you goofily with their weird rictus grins of stupidity.
So you basically quick-save nonstop, running into an area, hoping you don't get riddled with really slow moving bullets (the physics in this game are weird) try to kill the enemies through a combination of manual bullet-time and shoot dodges (by the way, manual bullet-time is not set by default, make sure to go into the key bindings and set a key for it) without having a stray bullet slap you in the noggin.
If you die, quick load, if you don't, move to the next door, quick-save, then repeat endlessly until the end of the game.
Mooks also take about a dozen bullets to kill, and since weapons spray in indiscernible trajectories most of the time, you can't consistently land headshots, even with the most accurate weapons in the game, like the Desert Eagle or Colt Commando, the only gun that always lands its shot is the Sniper Rifle, and that gun sucks crap in most of the game's areas and prevents you from shoot dodging.
Oh, and speaking of shoot dodging, it's almost always a bad idea, it looks cool, but you're pretty much better off only using manual bullet-time, running around, instead of shoot dodge, since shoot dodge only allows you a very limited amount of shots before you're prevented from firing anymore as you lie on the ground, giving enemies plenty of time to kill you murderously or run over and pee in your mouth or a host of other possibilities.
It's just annoying constantly hearing "HEYA" and having your brain squished out of your skull. Enemies will literally wait around corners and without hesitation pound you to death as soon as you turn the corner, even shoot-dodging won't save you most of the time.
There's also just a ton of annoying segments in the game that force you to do platforming or climb up pillars or etc. and Max's movement is so stiff and unnatural, his jump so iffy and weird, that oftentimes you'll fall to your death or stumble around like a drunken ape as you shuffle on pipes and other pieces of junk.
At least the level design is straight forward enough that you never get lost, which is saying something for a game from this era, old school shooters used to think sending you into a monochromatic labyrinth of banality was amazing level design (see Unreal/Daikatana/etc.)
I still love the story, it's unapolagetically ridiculous and the writing has a lot of character and personality to it, Max's character arch is interesting and well developed, and there's a lot of funny dialogue between idling enemies. The comic book segments are well done and feature a lot of beautiful to look at grimaces and weird faces from Sam Lake.
Ambient sound is great, the music is fantastic, the guns sound wonderful, basically, the production values of this game have held up well, they're not stunning like they used to be, but for the most part the presentation of this game is acceptable and doesn't hold the game back by modern standards.
But it's just such a frustrating slog to play, there's very little rhyme or reason to it, you can be a great FPS gamer and yet most of your encounters are just down to luck, like that idiot Leprechaun from those crap Leprechaun movies, where he's murdering people in really dumb ways and saying completely stupid crap, I hate those movies and I hate that idiot Leprechaun. Just like I hate the encounter design of this game.
Hell, even Max says it himself at one point, as you assault a mob boss's mansion, it has nothing to do with skill, or playing your cards right, it's all chaos and luck.
That's a very apt thing to say Max, you sexy boy.
Max Payne 2 and 3 are fortunately, much much better games, and I highly recommend them, but I can't really recommend MP1 as its gameplay design is archaic and frustrating. It's a shame, and I haven't even said anything about the dead baby dungeon and Twizzler tight ropes and Max's wife screaming at him because she burnt the roast or something.
Anyway, I wish I could still like Max Payne 1 like I did back in the day, but unfortunately I have to sensually whip off my rose-colored glasses and call it as it is. This game is straight doodie.

The game WILL NOT run out of the box; there are two things you need to personally do, and a third if the nuance bothers you.
1. Google 'max payne sound fix' and run the script/installer. Just follow the instructions. The game WILL NOT have working sound without this fix.
2. Manually turn on compatibility mode. Run it in Windows 98 / ME Compatibility Mode. The game will refuse to start unless you do this.

The Battle of Stalingrad (23 August 1942 – 2 February 1943) was a major confrontation of World War II in which Nazi Germany and its allies fought the Soviet Union for control of the city of Stalingrad (now Volgograd) in Southern Russia.
Marked by fierce close quarters combat and direct assaults on civilians in air raids, it is often regarded as one of the single largest (nearly 2.2 million personnel) and bloodiest (1.7–2 million killed, wounded or captured) battles in the history of warfare. It was an extremely costly defeat for German forces, and the Army High Command had to withdraw vast military forces from the West to replace their losses.
The German offensive to capture Stalingrad began in August 1942, using the 6th Army and elements of the 4th Panzer Army. The attack was supported by intensive Luftwaffe bombing that reduced much of the city to rubble. The fighting degenerated into house-to-house fighting; both sides poured reinforcements into the city. By mid-November 1942, the Germans had pushed the Soviet defenders back at great cost into narrow zones along the west bank of the Volga River.
On 19 November 1942, the Red Army launched Operation Uranus, a two-pronged attack targeting the weaker Romanian and Hungarian armies protecting the German 6th Army's flanks. The Axis forces on the flanks were overrun and the 6th Army was cut off and surrounded in the Stalingrad area. Adolf Hitler ordered that the army stay in Stalingrad and make no attempt to break out; instead, attempts were made to supply the army by air and to break the encirclement from the outside. Heavy fighting continued for another two months. By the beginning of February 1943, the Axis forces in Stalingrad had exhausted their ammunition and food. The remaining units of the 6th Army surrendered. The battle lasted five months, one week and three days.

I didn't think I was going to like it this much. It's hilarious! Art is gorgeous. It also manages to be heartwarming, especially when the dads talk about/with their kids. This has become one of my all time favourite games.
Inclusive, incredibly witty, fantastic art, and much deeper than it may appear at first.
I enjoyed every route immensely and have experienced a whirlwind of emotions, all in all I HIGHLY recommend that you buy this game!

Character Design: Each dad feels like a new person, they’re all fleshed out and feel real. They have distinct personalities and although they all fall into a stereotype, they do break out of those boxes and gain more character depth. Each character is likable and I honestly can’t think of a single character I hate. Yes, that includes Mary.
Sprite Design: The anatomy on the sprites is great and the physical designs of the characters are aesthetically pleasing. The designers really know how to use color well. That might sound like a small thing to praise but really it adds to experience and the bright aesthetics.
Voice Acting: The voice actors did an excellent job on delivering their lines (or lack thereof but I’ll get to that) and all voices really fit the character.
Music: I personally believe the music is fantastic especially whatever the track is that plays in the bar and concert venue.
Representation: This game has amazing LGBT+ representation. There are gay, bi, and even trans dads which is great! You’re even given the option to wear a binder at the start and you can choose if Amanda had a mom or another dad.
Writing: It’s clever, witty, and sometimes just nonsensical in all the right ways. This game has given me a few good laughs which is something I expected since Game Grumps is tied so closely to it.
Glitches: If you haven’t heard already, the way the game is makes it impossible to acquire certain achievements
and also random character sound effects will play when you change scenes
Price: As much as I enjoy this game it is not worth $15, maybe more like $10
Protagonist: Sometimes I feel like he acts more like a teenager than an adult. I suppose that’s to keep it accurate to the demographic but still. We understand that he’s supposed to be a fish out of water and nervous about meeting dads but sometimes I think the game takes it too far.
It would be nice if you could choose how you react more. I know lots of people hate the illusion of choice, and don’t get me wrong, so do I, but I would rather do that than be frustrated with my characters actions because he can’t send a text.
Voice Acting: Okay so I know I praised the voice acting before but there’s some downsides. It’s not fully voiced which wouldn’t be an issue if there was so little audio clips for them to use. Because there’s only a few snippets, there’s plenty of times where clips are played at inappropriate times with dialogue that doesn’t fit. Also a few characters have not so great audio quality due to their mics.
Minigames: Most minigames aren’t explained and so you’re left to fumble around with the controls until you figure it out.
Romance Aspect: It doesn’t feel like the dates are dates. There’s not a lot of romance for a dating sim and most of the time it doesn’t feel like you’re flirting at all. Well that’s not entirely true, it’s just that the romance hits HARD on the third dates usually. There’s not a smooth transition and it doesn’t make the attachment feel genuine.
Routes and Endings: The routes are all more or less the same. Sure, the dates are different, but nothing in between changes. Also, there’s not a lot of variation in the endings either and there’s quite a few dads who you can’t even get good endings with, only bittersweet or horrible ones.If you’ve read any other reviews or have any knowledge of the fandom, you’ll know exactly which dads I’m talking about.
Even though there’s a lot of cons I’m still going to recommend this game. Overall it’s a good game that has good characters and funny interactions. However, don’t expect to play it more than once or twice unless if you like to collect achievements (but even that might not be satisfying considering that a few are unavailable to collect). My advice is to wait for it to go on sale or play it with a group of friends. It’s a fun game that’s full of laughs and it’s more fun to share the experience.

My first impression while playing this game is that they took what everyone loved about the first 4 games (Codename 47, Silent Assassin, Contracts, & Blood Money) and took the few good ideas from Absolution (Controls, PART of the instinct system, contracts mode, etc) and have fused them together for a proper sequel.

Really it all comes down to this, if you enjoyed the previous Hitman games, you will enjoy this. Nothing is missing, and everything is improved. Don't listen to all the people causing problems because they hate waiting for new content. No matter how you slice it, the 60$ get's you a full game.
The only differance is you can get it AS content is ready and being updated.
OR you can wait till it's all on one disc.

I'm a huge CFB so I was thrilled when I came across this game, but, despite making every effort to love the game, I just don't.
The main issue for me is the instability; the game crashes at least a couple of times in each session (which, tbf, is normally 3+ hours) and sometimes even deletes your saved game for no apparent reason. As you can imagine, this is extremely frustrating.
The UI isn't always particularly user-friendly either; I spend most of my time during the recruiting section of the game flicking back and forth between my (in-game) emails and the recruiting screen to follow advice which is in said emails, making an otherwise enjoyable aspect of the game tedious and grindy. Simply populating the player info screen with suggested recruit pitches after scouting, rather than slowly growing adding to them week on week, would be a quick fix here. Similarly, full information on player injuries isn't available in your depth chart, so you have to flick back and forth between emails and depth chart to update the position of players who are fit to play but haven't fully recovered. If you could get the medical staff report either in the player info screen or simply by hovering over their name in the depth chart I would save a fair bit of time. There's more on this but I won't drone on.
Finally, calling the plays in a game can be very hollow and frustrating at times, not because this is a text-based sim, but because there is no kind of play-by-play feedback or general analysis to explain why a certain play is/isn't working, making play-calling fairly arbitary as long as you stay within the confines of common sense. A simple pop-up from the relevant co-ordinator explaining in more detail what happened on each play would help give a clearer picture of why a play succeeded/failed and help to make more informed decisions later on.
There are things I do love about the game, like the subject matter and the fact that it even exists. I've had some really enjoyable moments when playing and there's a real sense of satisfaction from building your team's prestige and attracting better recruits as the seasons wear on. Unfortunately that just isn't enough to keep me coming back for more agonising crashes and motonous offfseason tabbing. While it would be foolish to expect the kind of polish you would expect from a game like Football Manager, given the difference in budget and price, I would have hoped for a slicker overall product. If the issues I mentioned above are fixed then I will come back to this game in a heartbeat, but until then I'll just content myself with watching CFB.

4 hours in:
Just started playing so I'll update the review once I finish, but off to a great start.
Playing this toook me back to the old CRPG days of when I was back in highschool. TTON definitely feels like a solid successor to the original Torment.  The game has the same mystery, detail and story as the original and it feels so right.
If you're not interested in a long literaly journey - DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.  There is a lot of reading and if you don't want to invest the time to read it through, you'll miss out on the whole point of this game.
If you're a fan of CRPGs and want to expereince a great story - you MUST BUY THIS GAME.
- Every NPC so far has been a great experience.
- The items have all been interesting.
- The decisions have all given me pause, just what impact will this have down the line???
The polish on the game is solid as well, very smooth feeling and it's just a goregous game.
===========
9 Hours in
Wow - this just gets better.  I ended up completing several quest chains in 2 new area maps during my next playthrough.  The NPCs continue to be very deep and engaging and boy am i sweating my decisions.  I actually failed at a quest I really wanted to succeed at, however I recall Colin McComb saying that failing in this game has sometimes more interesting consequences, so I'm letting my failures ride!
Also, ended up at a bar for psycics and spent probably 2 housrs in there alone.  Ran into an NPC from Torment, very cool, and also had to do a few very interesting things with the NPCs in there.  I have to tell you, this bar, so far, is my favorite part of the game.   The folks in here were so amazing and the detail written for each made me care and worry about each one of them.  So great.
===========
18 Hours in
Main Quest: Alright, so i'm making headway on the main quests now.  I have to say that i'm finding it quite interesting but also i'm getting very curious to see what role my character is going to play here.  The sheer amount of castoffs i'm running into is making me feel far  "less special' that I did at the start.  I think it's interesting to talk to the others but we seem to be a dime a dozen - which could be the point - The Changing God apparently changed bodies every 10-20 years.  Just not sure if i totally dig this aspect of the main story.  I wanna be SPECIAL DAMNIT!
Bugs: As for bugs, I've noticed that long conversations bog down the game.  Some conversations with so many responses are the problem.  But this is easily fixed by stoppiong the dialog and starting again.
Environments: They continue to be quite engaging and some of the NPCs are seriously funny.
Items and quests:  So great.  Everything is interesting and the quests have lots of depth.  They definiteyl spent a lot of time making these both meaningful.
Consequences: Definitely continue to feel i'm making an impact and i'm leaving a trail of broken situations i will need to see the counter-conclusions to in my NEXT play through.
===========
25 Hours in
Main Story: Progressing through the main story - still quite interesting.  Making little progress on it though, so many fun side quests!  I have made some seriously f'd up decisions but that's how it goes in a Torment game : )  next play through I'll switch things up and see how things turn out on the flipside.
Environments: I'm in the bloom now - what a great environment.  It's like a mix between the alien nest in Aliens and The Thing.  It's truely unique and the quests and the items and the interations that are possible in such a wild blend of environemtns make for such a great experience.  My favorite zone so far - just so much depth it's great.
Special call out to the Doctors in the bloom - very funny dialog.
Items and quests: The items i'm obtaining and the things I've been able to do with dropped items have been so fun.  So many unique itemts to use and figure out.  Dependant on your skills, you're able to use unique items by fiddling with them.  Hope I keep finding them, they're so interesting.
Bugs: No bugs
Next up - the Ascention!
Highly recommended so far, more to come.

I'm giving this a thumb down with really a heavy heart.
And this be a high(ish) tier KS backer bleeding heart, for that matter. And that's the crux of the problem, I think.
By no means is Numenera an objectively bad game, but I think it unfortunate that the KS campaign is probably the best excecuted area of the whole project. I admit I could not manage my expectations because PS:T is forever a favourite. Someone coming to this game with lesser vested interest will probably really like it.
The writing is quite good, with interesting and even touching little destinies. I mean: why did I feel so sad for a "stillborn" robot, for example?? The story is a definate highlight. I also think visually the game is pleasing.
But I really, really hate the combat.
It's not particularly good as far as turn based go, IMO - and because the emphasis more or less has to be on "social" skills and checks to get the most out of the gameworld, I've found myself quite on the plain side as far as fighting prowess go.
Here the promised but not delivered death labyrinths would have been handy, to add a silver lining to the fumbling combat.
I find the turn based solution poor and inorganic - not to mention that BG-style pausable tactical combat could be played as turn based by enabing auto-pause. Why not deliver both worlds, when this has been the case in the classics of the genre inXile is paying homage to?
Do I regret backing? Not exactly.
I did not get what I hoped for, but at least inXile got my good-will when it needed it the most. I wish to be optimistic that this title will serve a basis from which inXile can improve many a tantalising idea that did not get the depth it would have deserved. But I doubt that I would pre-pay them on faith again.

Hard to recommend this overdue nostalgia-bait to people at anything other than a deep discount.
If they had named it something else it - rightly - wouldn't have existed today. It rides almost exclusively on the hype of PS:T, but fails to deliver anything remotely close to its namesake. It even goes out of its way to spit in your face by constantly referencing PS:T itself in-game, in situations that make so little sense it's outright offensive.
Now, I could complain about a lot of things. I could complain about it being incredibly overdue. I could complain about the broken promises. I could complain about the terrible sound design. I could complain about the user interface. I could complain about the absolutely atrocious combat (some of the worst you will encounter in any cRPG). But I won't because a lot of those things were pretty bad in the original as well... though that's hardly a point in this game's favour, at least it means it doesn't have anything to live up to. Except maybe in the sound design. PS:Ts music was often very good. T:ToN's music is... does it even have music? I don't know. All I can remember from its sound design is having to CONSTANTLY LISTEN TO SOME ENDLESSLY LOOPING HIGH PITCHED BACKGROUND NOISE AS I TRY TO READ A SCENE--- but I digress.
But I could probably overlook its many flaws and recommend it as a still fairly-decent more-of-a-book-than-a-game-kind of game (which it sometimes is, seemingly depending on what writer wrote the scene you're in; some are utter trash; some are alright) if it wasn't for THE COMPANIONS. My god. The companions. Every time I encountered a new one, I was amazed by how this awful character was the worst-written, most cringe-inducing thing I'd encountered in the game up to that point. Then I'd encounter another one and have the same experience all over again.
The absolute low must've been when I came across Rhin. Now, I had just encountered Erretis - a horribly written deadpool expy complete with obnoxious oh-so-quirky yellowtext in every conversation you have with him - so my standards were pretty low.
Then comes Rhin. Probably the most offensively poorly written companion I've ever come across in any cRPG. It's like you took all the most overused, boring, bland, predictable, subversion-worthy tropes of 'a helpeless little girl who tries her best and need you to protect her and is oh so awkward and almost cries and don't you just want to protect her' and wrapped them all up into one. I was absolutely convinced that it was impossible that this character wasn't a subversion, but as far as I can tell (I dumped her almost right away), she wasn't. She was a genuine true-to-life Little Match Girl, presented with absolute zero irony or self-awareness by the author.
Now... maybe if this game was just some generic RPG I could've let this slide. Standards are pretty low these days, after all. But this game dresses itself in the cloth of PS:T, and standing in its shadow it looks like nothing so much as a perversion. Fukken any of the companions in PS:T by themselves were more interesting than all of the ones I've encountered in T:ToN put together thus far, and even some of them were fairly banal at times - though at least they tried. Y'know, they tried♥♥♥♥♥♥like taking a succubus and turning her into an intellectual who disawovs sex. Not exactly the most radical♥♥♥♥♥♥ever, but man if T:ToN had a similar companion Fall-from-Grace would just be a normal succubus. Nordom would just be a mindless automaton. Vhailor would probably be a golem, and I'm sure he'd have been presented as evil as well. It's weird because some of the ranom NPCs you encounter are actually pretty interesting (I can only attribute this to different authors; apparently their good ones didn't end up writing any companions - at least not that I've come across thus far). But the companions... the most important NPCs you encounter... decidedly are not.
The whole experience is just... very disappointing, and I regret having been baited into backing it way back when they claimed they were going to deliver it in december 2014.

Following on from Jedi Knights Outcast, comes a game I enjoyed a little more.  I played this game a long time ago, so knew what to expect, but after recently playing Outcast, I prefer this game a little more.
The story follows on the story in Outcast, where someone you've fought was left alive, and now she's back.  This time however, you play as a young Jedi in training, working along side, Kyle Katarn.
You can choose your species and gender before starting, and as the game progresses, can choose your lightsaber, fighting style and force powers, whereas in Outcast, you were on a set path.  The game also has light and dark endings, which gives it a little more replay value.  The missions are not linear in a sence of following a strict timeline, so you can even mix it up that way.
Combat wise, its basically the same as Outcast.  Gun play is fine, although you learn why everyone is such a terrible shot.  Not as many Stormtroopers as Outcast, so see a variety of different species, which makes things different.
Lightsaber duels are a little better I found than Outcast.  But that's maybe just down to a different move set you can have over the standard Katarn one; I'm not sure.  Like Outcast, and because I'm terrible, playing on Easy Mode was a mix bag for me.  100 health, and can fight for ages and never deal damage, then die with one swing from the AI.  Othertimes, one swing and a jump from me and they go down.  Not much feedback on dealing damage I found.
Levels are SO much simpler to work out than Outcast.  I had a terrible time figuring out where to go, and what to do, with some backtracking required.  Academy though is a lot more condensed, and a lot more linear, which for this type of single player story, is a lot easier to work with.
Overall, a good enough game.  Recommend it, and I'm sure you can pick it up with Outcast in a Star Wars bundle.

I really enjoyed this game, so I just can't bring myself to say that I don't recommend it. However, I do have a few criticisms, and felt a slight twinge of dissapointment from this game.
Firstly, let me start with the goods.
- The artistry on the dads? Gorgeous. I absolutely love the style that all the dads are drawn in. It's incredibly attractive.
- I absolutely love the choice you are given at the beginning with Amanda. You can choose whether you are her biological dad or adoptive dad, and whether her other parent is male or female.
- The dialogue is very funny and captivating. You can tell the writers really know their target audience's sense of humour (well, at least they knew MINE...)
- I love the fact that I was torn between who to date. All the dads are so different and yet so desirable, that it was hard for me to choose who I would go on that first third date with.
- As a member of the LGBT community and an activist for more representation, the inclusion is revolutionary. 4 men of colour, a trans man who's storyline does not revolve around his gender, a fat man who isn't treated like a joke and the choice to make your own dad gay, bi and trans is honestly a huge step in the right direction.
Now, the things I was dissapointed with
- Creating my dadsona. The artstyle in this part is just so different to the other dads that it looks rushed. There's not really a lot of choices to go with, and a lot of the options were jokey (e.g. anime sparkley eyes/jokey mouths making up a good portion of the choices, no option of stubble, etc.). I think I might have actually preferred to just have a set look for this main dad character, which ties in with my next point
- The final dates seem so.... unfulfilling? The text is all you get to describe the romantic scenes. I think, if there was a set dad look, some cute drawings of the dads together (not neccessarily anything smutty!) would have been a really great addition to the final scene with your chosen dad.
- Some of the voice acting really ground on me (*cough* Hugo *cough*). It sounded as if it was recorded through a cheap webcam at some points, and really breaks the chill mood that the cute background music brings at times. I also think that some dad's voices should have been swapped, mainly Mat and Robert as I think Danny's voice would have matched better with Mat's character.
So, all in all, I'd still recommend you give this game a try. It's cute and definately gets you invested.

Alright, I've got around 8hrs clocked in and have finished all the routes once so I think I'm ready for my verdict on the game.
I did like several parts of Dream Daddy, the writting is charming and the art (though your "dadsona" looks very out of place comparied to everyone else's avatars, which can be very comical) is really really nice, some of the gallery photos are stunning. As a transgender man myself it warmed my heart learning one of the characters is too. I was also sobbing away several times before the dates began because of the moments with Amanda. I'd never had the chance to see myself as a possible parent before, and the Dream Daddy team got me right in the heart with the prologue.
Onto the dating, some of the storylines are very enjoyable and interesting to go along. Though even with the storylines that I really enjoyed, they feel very rushed with how the writting lays out the content of the dates. That plus the sublte time skip between second and third dates can make the emotional jumps the characters make odd for the player.
For replayabiliy, I noticed (I think because I played multiple routes at once) that some dialogue seems influenced because I played other routes.
Example; At the end of Hugo's route talking to Ernest at the party, he referenced when I ran into him during Robert's route. This doesn't seem like enough of a difference that I'd want to play any route again, but it was an intersting touch.
One of the biggest problems is the price. $17 (CAD) is way more than I'd pay for any visual novel this buggy, and this short.
Sprites appearing in scenes they dont belong in (had this happen with Joseph's twins, Amanda, and Brian's daughter) Characters making noise when they aren't supposed to or aren't even in the current scene. During Damien's third date everytime he spoke two (DIFFERENT) pieces of his audio would play. With the audio problems it makes me wish not only the music could be turned off but the voices too. (And Hugo's audio quality... oh boy)
I believe it's the save and load features that makes the audio and sprite problem worse! (Or at least I believe the glitch is tied to that) As if I loaded a scene while playing the game there would be absolutely no music until the next piece of music/bg noise was to come in. (or I'd have to reload 6-10 times or restart the game to get the audio back in that part.)
All in all, I did enjoy Dream Daddy. Their team did an overall great job for their first game, I followed along them pushing back the date and struggling to get the game up.
I'm also not implying this is a bad game, but at the moment I wouldn't reccomend the game as it is. I'd say wait for a sale or for them to work out all the bugs the game currently has. I'm gonna go try to play some of the infuriating minigames to wrap up my Dream Daddy experience!

Most of the negative reviews of this game appear to be down to both the always online DRM and the episodic format.
Which is a shame because aside from this the game itself is incredibly fun, and a welcome return to the sandbox style silent assassin fun of the old Hitman games, which used to make me cackle like a witch at a halloween party.
If anything I'd like a better map (like the ones in Blood Money) because the levels are so huge it's easy to get lost, but the new opportunities system is a very fun addition - with the odd little sly remark from Diana added in.

I kind of have to recommend this game. The gameplay is nothing short of brilliant. Yeah, it has some flaws here and there, but no game is litterally perfect. As a Hitman game, this is pretty damn close though. As much as I liked Absolution for what it was, this is what Hitman is supposed to be like. It takes everything good from Absolution and Blood Money and then combines them together. You're presented with a large map and the objectives. Then you go to work aby way you like. Shoot everything that moves? Sure, you can do that. Sneak in and steath-kill only the targets? Yes, you can do that too. What about killing only those in your way to get to the targets? of course, it's a Hitman game! You can even make it look like accidents.
There is, however, one problem. It's not with the gameplay, it's not with the graphics. It's the content. This game has one level, well, if you don't count the tutorial. It was supposed to be one map, then one months after another one would come up. The problem is that the game was released on March 11th, and teh next map, well it doesn't come out untill today, which is April 26th. That's way too long. A map every two weeks or so would be great. Well, not better than just having everything released on the date the game came out, but the age of complete games upon launch is sadly long gone. Anyone else miss that? And then getting an expansion alomost the size of the original game a few months later? Yeah, those were the days. No I'm not here to complain and bicker about how the gaming industry has become and yadda, yadda. But if you do get hung up on this sort of stuff, do not even think about buying this game, yet. When everything is out and the game is complete, which at this pace will be in a couple of years, the game will be fantastic.
So stick around for the full game, as this game is gonna be great when it's actuall done.

I was hesitant to try the game because of all the negativity surrounding its release.
But the game itself (not the business model) might be the best Hitman game ever.
I went in with low expectations. The tutorial does a good job in conveying what Hitman is all about. The 'opportunities' (creative ways to kill targets) interface can be fully turned off, but is very nice feature for new players.
And then the Paris level completely blew me away. The scale is massive. It's probably 4x+ the size of your average level from 'Blood Money'. And it ran very well and still looked amazing even though I'm on an older system.
The amount of things to explore in this single level is insane. It's like levels inside of the level (levelception?). There's the 'infiltrate the auction as a guest' level, there's the sharpshooter assassin level and many more.
I've played through the Paris destination three times and I'm not even close to seeing everything and doing everything.
Admittedly you have to be more of a completionist and a tinkerer (a typical Hitman player) to get a lot of time out of it. The story is not really a thing and if you play your levels once and then you're done you're probably not gonna like it that much.
However, if you loved 'Blood Money' or if you're willing to view this experience as more of a puzzle game than a story driven adventure you're gonna have a blast.

First let me say I am huge fan of many "text based" sims -- from OOTP series to FM Manager.  This game doesn't have nearly the bells and whistles of a AAA title like OOTP or FM series but it compares favorably in many ways and in some ways falls quite a bit short.
The biggest annoyance by far is the frequent crashing and lack of hyperlink based navigation.  The game seems to have a memory leak and will freeze every other season or so.  This would be a huge deal if it had auto save feature and/or didn't require a entire system reboot in order to come back.   Luckily I have learned to frequently save and the game does always load after a reboot -- haven't lost a single save yet (knock on wood).
The navigation is clunky at best and the game won't scale fullscreen as well.  These are two huge "quality of life" issues and I really hope with the increased scrutiny and money from Steam sales they fix this.  I would love to be able to play this game in 1440p and to have hyperlinks for players, conferences, etc.
Those annoyances aside -- I pretty much lost last weekend to this game, it's that compelling.  Following recruiting is as addictive as real life (can I can get that 5 star???) and quite realistic as well.  If you don't spend the $$$, time and have a high enough prestige you'll often have to settle for 3 star prospects or offer few 4 stars at a few understocked positions while enticing them with immediate playing time, which the AI seems to do a good job recognizing from what I can tell;   I offered a 5 star RB with only middling prestige and when I offered him playing time (I had zero good back on the roster after graduating my two seniors) he ended up committing.
But go after too many very hightly touted recruits as a middling school and you'll just end up with a handful of walk on levels players after everyone leaves you hanging.
That said, if you recruit 3 stars into your team that excel at areas you want to play them (say  athlete QB on an option team) you can build a program -- more slowly, but you can.
I don't personally get too deep into the game plan besides occasionly stepping in on a big down and guiding the way, but from what I've read you can spend hours just setting up the weekly strategy.  I don't prefer that level of micromanagent but if you do the option is there.
But as far as gameplay and replay value this game is just as addictive as the FM Series or OOTP.  The simulation is usually solid (hey, these things are hard, you will occssionaly see the absurd like 7 fumbles in one game from one team) and the gameplay is solid all around from the simulation engine itself to the big picture stuff like choosing your coaches and gameplan and recruiting.
I recommend this game but it is with some hesitation as for some on smaller monitors (I have a 27" 1440p on my main gaming rig) the text is unreadable and the constant crashing is a pretty major annoyance as well.
But given that this game is only, $15, if you have a large monitor and enjoy sports sims, pick it up now you'll consider it money well spent.

When playing through the franchise modes of a modern sport game like NBA 2K or, to a lesser extent, Madden, it’s hard to believe that there was a time when the only place you could find the multi-season GM-like experience of these titles was the world of text simulations. The trade-off with these text sims was that they there were usually a one-man operation, with 99% of the time and effort spent trying to replicate accurate stats and finances of the sports they were simulating, and the remaining 1% spent quickly hobbling together a GUI to present all the information.
Bowl Bound College Football was one of the first among the new breed of text sims. By moving away from the ‘one-man operation’ model to employ others specialising in areas such as 2D graphics and UIs, BBCF attempted  to merge the strengths of text sims – the multi-season experience, and statistical accuracy – with a GUI that also didn’t look like an excel spreadsheet. It succeeded. Despite the fact that the game has been out for some time now, the UI is still clean and modern looking, and little touches like player portraits for the generated players was years ahead of the 3D-based sporting titles. Even the BBCF simulation screen foreshadows the type of display we expect to see today in ‘quicksim’ screens in these 3D titles.
Graphics aside though, BBCF alse does the kind a great job simulating the kind o fcollege football experience – recruiting, strategy, statistical accuracy – that you expect from any text sim worth its salt. In any sports game, be it text sim or graphical, my favourite aspect is rebuilding a team into a winner, and the college world of sports is perfect for this given the continual overhaul needed to replace graduated players. Even after all these years – ignore my Steam stats, I’ve had this title on my PC for close to a decade - I fire it up from time-to-time and embark on yet another career.
With no other college football game around or even on the horizon, BBCF is a fine option to satisfy your college football hunger. Hopefully one day we see the long-rumoured Pro football version released!

WARNING: This review contains spoilers for the anime "The Adventures of Garfield" as well as the TV movie of the same name. DO NOT READ IF YOU ARE NOT CAUGHT UP!
In the vast world of anime, many heroes are ingrained in our collective conscience. Cory Baxter, Gary Oak and Tesco's Own Great Value Bleach spring to mind. Every good anime hero is only as good as their villains, however. Hillary Clinton, The Allied Powers and the Suicide Hotline may be the most villainous villains, but I think that the tragic villains are the best characters. Robbie Rotten, for example, has to resort to trickery to stop the communists from taking over Lazytown. My favourite villain, though, is a bit more obscure.
You have all probably heard of the classic Miasaki anime Garfield. It is, in a villain sense, the Batman of anime. The scheming Nermal makes most top 10 lists, but I find the tragedy of Jon Arbuckle to be one of the best anime stories of all time. Jon was thought to be the chosen one and his parents were killed when the Order of the Lasagne tried to kidnap him. We all know that Garfield is the true chosen one. He attempted to rescue Jon, but was too late.
After the Order lobotomised Jon, they left him in a house with the confidence that they had defeated the chosen one. Garfield's attempts to try and help Jon have been met with failure. In the event of another chosen one rising, the Order left an agent called Odie to guard Jon. His idea that Odie is innocent merely stems from his Order brainwashing, which causes him to interrupt the classic Garfield fight scenes more often than not.
As we all know, Jon's arc closes in the series finale. He is able to overcome his brainwashing and sacrifices himself to allow Garfield to reclaim the sacred Lasagne. This is a beautiful end for an amazing character. This character is so good because his villainous acts come from a place of a genuine feeling that he is doing the right thing. His Order brainwashing makes him think that Garfield is a villain. I think that the writers of this amazing anime did a great job making a believable character whilst still giving him a threatening stature.
To conclude, I highly recommend that anyone who enjoys good, story based anime checks out Garfield. As for what version: if you must watch a dub then I suggest the Australian dub due to it's superior voice acting, otherwise, go for the original Japanese version with subtitles.  I must warn you that the American movie adaptation of the classic Jim Davis manga is atrocious. The best piece of Garfield merchandise you can play is the "♥♥♥♥♥♥ic experience" known as Garfield Kart, available on PC, 3DS and mobile devices.

Despite what many of the top reviews are saying right now, this game is fantastic. The negative reviews are mainly for a mismanaged Kickstarter. So long as you aren't part of that, then this outrage doesn't effect you.
The actual game itself is a very well written spiritual successor to Planescape Torment. However, there is even less of an emphasis on combat, so if you prefer more combat heavy RPGs like Baldur's Gate than this may not be for you.
The RPG mechanical elements themselves are pretty light. There are 3 "effort" skills you can spend to pass checks, which can only be recharged by items and sleeping. The combat is also based on spending these skills to use abilities.
The main alluring part of this RPG is the top quality writing and all of the different choices that can be made during quests and even outside of quests. For example, in many quests, you have the ability to learn deep secrets from people. After finishing the quest, you could always go and trade those secrets away for another secret, perhaps one that can save people, or perhaps one that you can use to your advantage. Is this something you want to do?
Torment: Tides of Numenara is all about these kinds of choices. If this sounds appealing to you, then I highly recommend the game!

Hello all,
I am early in the game and from what I could see, the game is good, but not good at the same time.
I am really hesitating between recommanding and not recommanding the game at the same time.
First, the game is gorgeous, you can't say they didn't make a great work there, the pillars of eternity engine is certainly great (though I would have liked some coop like baldur's gate).
Then the story, the story is certainly worth it, it is really well written, intriguing and you really want to go deeper into it.
The narrative is certainly the strongest point of the game with some stuff I could argue about like the change of scenery coming out of nowhere which in game is only a story, you take a couple minute to get into and by the time you're into it, you're back in reality... Some game effects could have been added to make more immersion.
Music and narration goes along with it, all pleasant and makes you want to hear more.
The the mechanics, the gameplay, the combat system... Well, let's start by saying that turn based combat isn't bad, I personnaly like turn based when it is well made such as fallout 1,2 or more recently divinity original sin!
BUT WHY OH WHY CHANGING THE MECHANICS SO MUCH??? The first torment was a blast combat wise... This one is really a deception... They threw away the D&D mechanics relative to the Torment universe to create a really poor system with 3 stats (might, speed and intellect) which form a "pool" from which you can drain points to perform successful actions or having a chance to fail them... Meaning, if you make a warrior, you will have high might and most likely succeed your might test all the time until your might goes down to 0 ! (example if you have 9 in might, you make an action and decide to spend 3 points to succeed it, you will have 6 left in might until you can replenish it)
The system is horribly bad, just like the cyphers which are kind of like a one time use magic object.
Going away from the classic D&D rule set is the biggest mistake they made, they should have conserved it even if it would cost more to have the right to use them!
Which also did cost them the class system which is down to the nano (the mage/mechanic), the jack (jack of all trade, master of none, kind of rogue) and the warrior, well, what's more to say about it? Master of weapons and armors.
Heck, even taking the pillars of eternity system would have been better! It was their engine so why not take their combat system instead of this horrible pool system!
Even by beeing a warrior with everything in might, if you empty your pool, you can fail a test... Same with the nano I am playing with right now.
Finally, the interface is really blend and I would have appreciated to see the portrait of NPC you're talking to avoid confusion while reading a dialog between more than 2 characters because this ask you to be really attentive to each name popping during a conversation.
The dialog window could have been made better to avoid the need to scroll down when making a choice.
Appart from that, the game, the animations of the decor, the story, everything is great and is the reason why I would recommend the brilliant writing of the scenario... Don't play Tides of Numenera hoping to get a deep RPG system... The RPG is all about the story and what it will make you discover althought many already state the story feels short.
Fort a 50$ game, this is quite a let down! I am finally glad I didn't back the game.
The world while seeming quite alien is lacking of mystical creatures and npc like the modrone, the black knight, morte, Anna, Ignis... And all the fun, weird, original and deep characters which could travel alongside with you in the original game. They made us go back to something classic.

There are plenty of other reviews out there for the game on various platforms, but only the PC version was developed directly by Playtonic, as far as I know--the rest having been developed by groups the fine people at Team17 put together for porting. This leads to inconsistencies and platform-specific issues between reviews that aren't really issues in the PC version. For this review, I'm focusing specifically on aspects of the PC version.
- Specs -
Intel i7 6700K @ 4.4 GHz
16 GB RAM
NVIDIA GTX 980ti (6GB VRAM)
Installed on 7.2k RPM HDD
Run at 2560x1440 locked at 72 FPS (half of the display's refresh rate)
This game supports widescreen, ultra-widescreen, and 4k display modes in windowed, borderless fullscreen, or exclusive fullscreen modes. Anisotropic filtering can be forced via the NVIDIA control panel or whatever AMD's equivalent is called (Catalyst Control Center?), but is not present in the game's video options. The game features always on post-process anti-aliasing and depth of field effects. They can be disabled via a third-party program, but I left them on for the entirety of my playthrough. There is a vertical sync option present within the game's options that allows you to sync the frame rate to your display's refresh rate, as well as a half refresh rate (i.e. if you have a 60 Hz display, you can cap it at 30 FPS). Finally, the game supports frame rates above 120 FPS. That said, the physics engine seems to top out at 60 FPS, leading to some "stuttering"  of moving objects if you're playing the game at more than 60 FPS.
The game should do a good job of scaling to your PC, regardless of hardware. The minimum requirements include an Intel E7300 (which came out in the Fall of 2008--a nearly decade-old processor) and an Nvidia GTS 450, a now seven-year-old GPU. On the other hand, if you have a crazy, high-end PC with the latest and greatest hardware companies have to offer, you should still be able to utilize a lot of that horsepower to push the game well beyond what is capable on other platforms. Even just meeting the minimum requirements to play, I can't imagine anyone would be better off playing it on a console.

The Arkham series has been setting the bar for melee combat for some years now.  So Origins has big shoes to fill.   Fans have gotten used to an unbelievable experience AND a serious evolution in gaming style each time a batman is released.  So it’s understandable why Origins has gotten poor reviews especially from fanboys.  What Origin actually turned out to be was an excellent game cut in the same mold of Arkham City, but without any evolution in gameplay. Putting the fanboyism aside the game is not a money grab by copy and pasting City.  It’s just a solid game in the series and well worth anyone’s time.
To be fair however Origins has some serious problems that are odd considering their nature.  Having basic bugs still in core gameplay mechanics months after release is a huge bone for fans to pick.  Especially since we didn’t see those bugs in the two previous games and this new developer had Rocksteady’s work to build on.  The worst problem still unresolved is what I call a hitbox (I am sure it has a real name) basically when the cursor is placed over an object the command will flash and allow you to use the key.  In Origin I frequently had near game breaking problems with the hitbox.  Trying to quickly go from perch to perch was nearly impossible in this game.  I could put my cursor over the location and it just refused to allow me to go there.  Sometimes it would just be a delay of a second but other times it would never register.  This ruined a key part of a batman game and got me killed countless times.
I would rate the Plot and theme done by this developer a B or B-, it’s not something I found interesting but it was enjoyable.  I think the bottom line with Origins is that you have to take it for what it is; it’s another 20 hours or so in Arkham City with some new twists that will marginally intrigue you.  Is it a true successor to the Arkahm family no, but it’s worth 50-60% of full price.   My Score  75/100

Overall I have to say I liked the game. It definitely has some oddities and issues but it's not overly bad. Not perfect though either.
Pros
1) It's a neat romp through being a jedi.
2) Some interesting missions where you meet classic Star Wars characters like Chewbacca, Wedge Antilles, and Boba Fett.
3) Some other missions that are just interesting, in and of themselves, just from setting an circumstance.
4)No live action cutscenes like the awful ones in Dark Forces II.
5)Chewbacca is listed in the credits as having voiced himself.
6) A large array of weapons to choose from like Wookie Bowcasters, and this one weapons that shoots a blue beam and wrecks anyone who even stands near it.
7) You can use Jedi Mind Trick to makes any enemy that's not a dark jedi join your side and attack their friends, and it is the most useful ability right next to heal in just how OP it is.
8) The story is, well it's not the most wonderful story ever written in the Star Wars Universe, but it's okay. It's not dog doo like some unfortunate SW things we don't ever speak of. If you don't mind a story that has you fighting a cult that apparently has more dark jedi than there are actual jedi and a Sith Lord's Force Ghost(Sorta, he's a bit Skeleton-ish) then you should be fine.
9) I came across the boss battle for Hoth and won it in about 3 seconds by jumping on her head, then stabbing her with the lightsaber while she was on the ground. So yeah, that's a pretty effective strategy. I suggest jumping on people's heads as much as possible.
Cons
1)It's major failing is that it did the same mistake that earlier games also made(Such as Dark Forces II). And that is that the Lightsaber blocks automatically. It ♥♥♥♥s you over. Because then you end up getting shot and you don't really have any control over the 1 line of defense you have. Games like Battlefront II and Force Unleashed fixed that by giving you a block button. This doesn't have that and it makes lightsaber combat so much more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t than it could have been. Also it's kind of unclear how fighting works when you fight someone who also uses a lightsaber. You just kind of jump around and keep swinging until they go down, and running away to heal if that doesn't work out. Once your combat level goes up this gets easier against weak dark jedi but remains an issue.
2) You will probably have to remap the controls, because they were seemingly chosen randomly.
3) Remember how I said there was an awesome array of weapons like missile launchers, trip mines, and that blue beam one that wrecks shop? Yeah they don't do♥♥♥♥♥♥to dark jedi. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. You have to use your lightsaber, or else they just deflect it back to you regardless of what it is. Not just blaster bolts. Mines and grenades will fly in your direction, missiles will come soaring into your face, and that awesome blue concussion gun that's a one hit KO for anyone not in a super heavy armor suit and should not be deflectable by some no name, just got his lightsaber, weak♥♥♥♥♥dark jedi? Yeah that becomes a 1-hit KO for you as it comes back to bite you. Blaster bolts I could understand. Giving boss Dark Jedi and the more powerful ones it I could understand. But the way it's thrown in here basically makes every weapon that's not your lightsaber nearly useless once you reach a certain point.
4) The character customization is, well not really all that much there. You have the choices of Human Male, Human Female, Zabrak Female, Twi'lek Female, Rodian Male, Kel Dor Male. You cannot change anything about the models they give you besides clothes and the color of the clothes(On the Twi'lek it changes skin color rather than clothes color.) I find this game very hard to rate, on one hand when I first started playing it was a whole lot of fun, but about halfway through I started to wish it was over. The main problem I had is with how repetitive everything got, taking over camps, races (which I hated and only did the ones it forced me to) side missions, etc. everything started to feel like the same.
Let's start off with the combat, if you enjoy fighting in any of the recent batman games you should like the combat here, it is damn near a copy paste. If you're on the other end of that and you hated the batman combat, well I hate to tell you that you're not going to be too fond of what you find here. There are upgrades you can unlock to Max's armor, fists, counters and special skills (which I really stopped investing in early on) but the basic combat never changes, one on screen prompt for dodge, one to counter and then you mash the LMB until everything is dead. I actually enjoyed the combat anyways though, trying to get higher and higher multipliers and some of the moves, especially the shiv finishers are brutal and satisfying to watch.
The driving has some issues, the handling, no matter how you build the car, is rubbish. You wouldn't think this is too big a problem as you're mostly driving around a giant wasteland but as soon as you veer off road a little bit your top speed becomes about 23 mph. Also, forget trying to make it through any tunnels or holes in the wall without crashing as the slightest bump sends you bouncing all over. This is mainly the reason I hated the racing. Now maybe I am just terrible at the driving in the game and really it is great, but I find that hard to believe.
This is also the only game to ever make me feel physically ill, only when looking through the binocs in an air balloon (how you scope out the areas a la towers in assassins creed) I'm not sure if it was the blur or what but every time I dreaded going in a baloon as it made me nauseous.
The cars sound good, and the voice acting is really well done, but I was hoping for a killer soundtrack akin to Fury Road while I was driving around, but there was no such thing, only chumbucket yelling in my ear.
The game runs well, 4k maxed out and it held a solid 60fps throughout, but there isn't really a lot going on, all the areas look pretty similar and there is a very drab color pallet, I understand it is Mad Max, but a bit more variety wouldn't have killed them, maybe I should have just played in "Black and Chrome." Other than the bland landscapes the skies were really well done, the storms looked awesome and the characters all looked good. My only other complaint is having the gamma on the recommended setting made some areas pitch black and your flashlight is a complete pile of poo.
So, the story starts off pretty strong, maybe an hour or two it held me and I was excited for what was going on. Then for about 23 hours of gameplay I didn't give a flying F what was going on, the villan was weak, I really didn't know what I was doing or why and it all felt blah. Then for the last 3-5 hours it got good again, I felt for the characters, I thought Max was a♥♥♥♥♥♥ There was a strange and unexplained new villan who felt right and I found myself engrossed in the story again, but I don't think that made up for the rest of the "go here, shoot a flare" aspect of the game.
On a scale of 1-10 I would give this a 6, which is just enough to give it a thumbs up and a recommended purchase, but ONLY if it is on sale $15 USD or below seems about right.

I love this game. It's my BIG FAVORITE (that was a game reference there)! Some people are saying that the puzzles aren't that hard, but puzzles were never even a big part of the game. This game is focussed on the story mainly, with puzzles and random battles in between.
Of course, it doesn't have much to it graphics-wise, but I think it's nice. It doesn't have to have fancy graphics to be good!
Something that I love about this game is the story, the characters, and the message it brings. The characters may just be a few pixels, but they feel and act so real. You can build relationships with them, become friends with them, and even kill them (which I do not reccomend). The story of this game is hard to explain, but it can make you laugh, cry, and it can also make you get angry. It's just so heartfelt, well, when you are a pacifist. I love how you're choices can shape the game as a whole. Choices that you make in past playthroughs can change what happens in future ones, so be careful. A few of the characters are aware that there is someone behind the screen playing the game, so if you make a bad choice, you yourself will face the consequences.
Another thing that I like about this game is the unanswered questions it has, which sounds weird, but it leaves room for fans to make theories with each other. There are some strange things that can happen in the game, and I won't go into specifics because the last thing I want to do is spoil it for you, but notice I said the word can instead of will. There are chances of easter eggs, special characters, and secret rooms popping up throughout the game, which makes it super special.
The biggest thing that makes this game different and amazing is that you have the power to do what you want. You can spare or kill monsters, the choice is in your hands, and depending on the choice you make, you will either be rewarded or punished, and the punishment won't go away by simply resetting the game, it stays, forever, even in future playthroughs, as I said before. You don't have to kill in this game, but you can, and you, not your character, but YOU are held accountable, so be careful and think before you act, because once you do something, it's done, unless if you mess with the game files, of course. I also want to mention its great soundtrack! The songs are so good! Anyways, I highly reccomend this game! It really isn't expensive, so that's even better! I hope that you found this review helpful!
