is the tie-in game that was associated with and released a few months after the blockbuster movie Mad Max: Fury Road. Despite this, it shares almost nothing with the movie, the main similarities being thematic style and a main character who is modeled and voiced to resemble Tom Hardy.
The game follows Max, a lone survivor haunted by the guilt-induced specters of his deceased family, through a postapocalyptic desert wasteland on the less-than-epic mission to get his car back and hoard enough supplies to make an attempt to reach a possibly mythical land of slightly less wasted desert.
As far as overall design goes, the game very clearly shares its heritage with
. Instead of a lone, spirit-possessed ranger aiding fellow survivors, bringing down war chiefs, and murdering bands of marauding Uruks, while being guided by a seemingly subhuman creature with uncertain motivations; the player is a lone, guilt-ridden man aiding fellow survivors, bringing down war chiefs, and murdering bands of marauding ... post-apocalyptic mutant people, while being guided by a seemingly subhuman creature with uncertain motivations. There's a near-identical world map divided into regions, with fast travel between regions available once key areas of each region has been reached via slow travel. Quests, challenges, and caches of greater and lesser worth are marked on the map once discovered, once again giving achievement-oriented players plenty of grist for the grinder.
In terms of gameplay, there are three basic mechanics: driving, punching, and upgrading. The driving portion is well-done, and includes exploring the landscape, raiding enemy warbands, destroying symbols of enemy chiefs' power, hijacking enemy convoys, participating in deathraces, and even catching sick air from terrain features. The player can capture enemy vehicles and add them to her garage, giving her the ability to drive them whenever she wants, but only the main vehicle can be customized and upgraded. In addition to the basic driving combat arsenal of ramming and shooting out of the window, the player can equip a harpoon to grapple with enemy vehicles and tear down structures, pull out a rocket launcher for extra kick, or even park and practice extreme-range sniping from the back.
While driving occupies approximately 50% of gameplay time, the other 50% is spent infiltrating hostile camps, raiding groups of near-defenseless outcasts for their meager hoards of scrap, and taking down war chiefs. This is unfortunate, because the vast majority of these missions, as well as the hand-to-hand combat itself, are extremely tedious. Although there are nominally a variety of different tasks and objectives, they all boil down to: follow linear path through enemy-populated area, get rushed by a group of enemies in every open space, punch everything that bleeds, and blow up everything that doesn't.
Because the games are superficially so similar, I again can't help making the comparison here with Middle-Earth: Shadow of Mordor. In M-E:SoM, there was an extensive and carefully-integrated stealth mechanic, giving the player multiple options for low-conflict sneaking, quiet assassination, or chaotic bloodbath. Additionally, there were three completely separate combat trees: ranged, standard melee, and ultra-close; each one of these had a variety of special attack upgrades that could be learned in order to enhance the combat experience.
In Mad Max, you have shooting and punching. However, shooting is slow, and Max can only carry a few shells at a time. On top of that, there is no stealth option - on a good day, you can take out one or two before the group sees you, but there's no way to use cover or terrain to your advantage, let alone achieve sneak attacks or avoid combat altogether. And then there's the punching. In his arsenal, Max has Punch, Slow Punch, and Parry. All combats basically consist of parrying and counterpunching until Max is the last one standing. In boss fights, substitute dodging for parrying, since bosses tend to have unblockable attacks.
The payoff for all of this driving and punching is scrap and experience, both of which can be used to purchase upgrades in order to improve your driving and punching, as well as Max's beard, which accounts for something like 20% of his personal upgrade tree.
The environments were well-done, with lots of little details that reinforced the theme and enhanced immersion. For example, during one challenge mission,
. In another,
. The characters are varied and interesting, with the sadly notable exceptions of
and the beyond-laughably cliché damsel.
Despite its lack of meaningful connection with Fury Road and its unavoidable yet inadequate similarity to Shadow of Mordor, Mad Max is a solid game. I spent 30 hours playing it, and if they ship an expansion, I'll probably play that as well.
OK, final recommendation time: if you haven't played Middle-Earth: Shadow of Mordor, go play that.
If it leaves you wanting more, or if you just want to slap some armor onto the Black on Black and go wardriving, then Mad Max is for you.

Protip: I recommend you focus on the main storyline and secondary (blue) quests, don't get overly obsessed with doing every single sidequest else it will get too grindy and you might get bored. + The game is pretty damn gorgeous, with probably the best environmental effects and terrain i have possible ever seen in a game thus far. To the extent where i died several times from suddenly admiring an astounding sunset/vista...

+ Mad Max lore - ever wondered who those buzzard guys in the movie were? How about how Max got his PTSD? Or wanted to know more about Gastown? Or why the world is a desert? Or how the whole apocalypse went done. All in the game, which is a big plus.
+ Combat is smooth and similar to the Batman Arkham series. Similarly, the driving mechanics and combat are quite ok as well.

Do NOT miss out on this game. This is just as good as the other Arkham games. Warner Bros did not disappoint. You'll notice that the enemies are far more realistic this time around, partly due to the fact that this story takes place closer to the start of Batman's beginnings (hence the name...) Don't worry about being stuck in an updated Arkham City again, because that's not what this game is. Sure the original arkham area from the last game is accessible in this game, but almost every mission takes place in a completely new area. The overall map is twice as big as Arkham City, featuring an entire new section called "The Diamond District" which features much taller buildings. It FINALLY feels like you're in Gotham City. One of the coolest parts of this game is that it takes place on a snowy Christmas eve, and all the rooftops are covered in a dynamic foot of snow. Enemies will leave permanent tracks in the snow, and once you're done having a huge fight on the rooftop, you can see a drastic change in the snow cover which is pretty impressive. Again, DO NOT skip this game. This is a fantastic game and does a great job exploring the origin story of the Dark Knight.

The most important question you have to ask yourself, when considering whether or not to purchase Batman Arkham Origins, is "what do I want from a sequel?". If you want innovation, you will be disappointed. If you want the same content that you've previously enjoyed, you will be satisfied.
I personally fall into the second category. I could name several games whose sequels have alienated their existing fanbase by changing too much, so I won't criticise Origins for sticking with a successful formula.
Origins is almost identical to City, in terms of gameplay mechanics and mission structure. We still have the small scale open world of Gotham, which allows us to take on secondary missions against the lower profile villains in any order. We still have the story missions, which are more linear, require the use of gadgets to bypass obstacles, contain a mixture of direct and stealth combat, and finish with a boss fight against one of the more high profile villains. And we still have the mild puzzle element provided by the Riddler trophies.
Combat is as fluid and tactical as always, combining attacks, counters, dodges, gadgets and takedowns, along with a variety of enemy types, some of which require specific moves to penetrate their defences. There are a few new gadgets/abilities, but nothing really revolutionary. I quite like the shock gloves though, which charge up as you hit people, and when activated will add electricity damage to Batman's punches.
The story is okay, but it suffers from the same problem that every prequel will in my eyes. I already know what happens later, so I know certain events cannot possibly happen. For example, when certain characters are in life or death situations, but I know they are alive in Asylum or City, I know they cannot possibly die in Origins, which makes those scenes lack the tension they should have. However, I did like that a few different villains were worked in, which allowed me to expand my knowledge of the Batman universe.
Origins is very good from a technical point of view. The graphics are fantastic, although maybe there's more of a wow factor for me because I played the previous two games on my Xbox 360. The level of detail in the backgrounds, such as shop signs and wall posters, really brings Gotham to life. However I did have to turn off some PhysX smoke effects to get a consistent framerate. Voice acting is pretty good. I was worried about the changes to key roles, especially losing Kevin Conroy and Mark Hamill, but this wasn't a problem and their replacements did a good job.
I played with a 360 pad because that's what I'm familiar with for this series, and it worked perfectly on this PC version. I didn't notice any bugs at all. Length depends on how interested you are in hunting down all the Riddler stuff, but I've gone over 20 hours and still have things to do, so value for money is great.

I really love these clicker idle games. And Voodoo Garden was great... until you realize that to get all the achievements you have to actually click thousands of snakes, frogs, dragon flys, snails, and lizards. I enjoyed the game until it became a grind for the achievements. So if you're just looking to click around and you think the art is cool, by all means buy this game. But if you like to complete games and go for all the achievements, maybe save yourself the headache on this one.

.Gameplay.
*Click, click, click*
Typical of the clicker genre, the majority of Voodoo Garden is played via clicking with your mouse. You can also use WASD or the directional keys to pan the camera, but you can use your mouse for that if you simply move it to the edge of the screen.
You’ll gather ingredients yourself by clicking. If your inventory fills up, don’t worry! Every ingredient over your ingredient threshold adds one gold coin to your coffers. Ingredients can be gathered from most every creature that scurries through your garden—except for bats. These crafty little buggers will swoop down and fly away with ingredients unless you click them to shoo them away.
Crocodiles and Skulls will occasionally float in the river along the bottom of the screen. There will be an audio cue—a watery sound—every time one surfaces and clicking on it will reward you with an amount of gold that increases every time you click a new one.
You can access the plants available to you by pressing the coin icon in the top right corner. Select your greenery and plant it by clicking one of the green circles in your garden. There are three categories of plant: herb, shrub, and tree. Each can only be planted in their corresponding row (herbs in the front most row, shrubs in the middle, and trees in the furthest row).
You can also purchase upgrades for your plants once their planted by clicking the window beneath the plant in the store. Each upgrade increases the rate at which the plant grows.
The store also offers animals, totems, and upgrades for your utilities. I’ll break them down below.
Animals: Each animal eats a specific plant that grows in your garden. Once it’s fat enough, you can sacrifice it to create a spirit that will help you harvest plants. They also cause the plants they ate while alive to flourish. Spirits can only be placed in specific spots between columns formed by herb, shrub, and tree and will only harvest from the columns closest to them.
Like plants, these can be upgraded to work more efficiently.
Totems: Totems attract specific critters to your garden in greater number. These are invaluable for the faster creatures like lizards, which will stop and stare at the totem, allowing you to click them and gather their tails.
They can also be upgraded to increase their effectiveness.
Utilities: These include upgrades to what your spirits can pick up and how many ingredients you can carry. They’re quite costly, but well worth the investment.
Spirits will gather ingredients for you as long as it’s not raining. When it is raining, your spirits disappear and additional critters won’t dart about amongst your plants. Creatures that are already in your garden before the weather changes will remain. There’s a quiet ambiance when it rains, which is nice.
Ingredients are used to produce potions, which are sold for gold and net you experience. You can set priority for what is created by assigning numbers to each recipe via the menu accessed by clicking your level in the top left corner. The little hut at the center of your garden will continue to churn out potions as long as you have enough ingredients.
Your level increases once you have enough experience and increasing it gives you a greater variety of plants, animals, upgrades, and potion recipes.
.Atmosphere.
The music in Voodoo Garden is serene and peaceful. It features a lot of wind instruments and a drum, which fit nicely into the theme. The music continues on an infinite loop, but it’s so charming that you don’t even notice.
The graphics are bright and cutesy, stylized in such a way that they look hand-painted.
.Longevity.
I've been achievement hunting, so I'm already 12 hours in. I forsee another couple of hours before I get all of them. For those who aren't as dedicated to getting achievements, longevity depends highly on your willingness to keep on clicking.
.Pros.
.Cons.
.Bottom Line.
Voodoo Garden is an inexpensive and relaxing way to pass the time. If you’re a completionist, you’ll be able to collect the achievements simply by playing the game. If you enjoy casual clicker games like Plantera, you’ll be right at home here.
Either way, the game will definitely be something you’ll turn to when you’re tired of slaying and struggling to survive in the other titles in your library.

In short: plant plants, collect fruits, leaves, flowers from them, mix it with animal parts (if required) to make voodoo items. You can also buy pets that can be sacrificed to be a helping spirit who boost certain plant products around themselves and help collecting. Craft enough items to level up to unlock more options.  The problem is that the game's product to item to money (to level up) ratio is just bonkers.
The very first recipe requires 5 pieces of item to make it, that's 5 click. And even in mid-levels, you require dozens or hundreds of items to level up. And your helping spirits are really slow, and only working if the game is running, not to mention that they don't kill animals - there's only 3 recipe out of the 12 that has only plants in it, one being the very first.
You can not reliably make items because the priorities you can set up is not coded to effect stockpiling, but crafting order - if you miss one single item out of your #1 priority item, it will eventually still use up the other resources to lower priority recipes, so when you miss the first ingredient, you'll make other items, then because of that you'll lack the second ingredient and so on... there's a mid-game recipe that barely can be made because it needs four different animal's parts to it, multiple of each, and the system will use up the already collected ones while you hunt for the remaining.
And the problem? The game has a rain mechanic to it that makes the spirits and animals disappear, and (I think) makes the plants grow faster.  So during the rain your automatic helpers are not present, no animals can be collected, and the plants will get used up for no-animal-recipes instead of actually stocking so you'll have a nice inventory to use.
So far we have bad crafting system, absolutely no ecosystem or monetary choices to speak about. (Plant only AFK-farm is slow and rain ruins it, and building around recipes that require animals is hard as rain ruins it. See the problem?) Also way, WAY to much clicking and absurd prices. A higher leveled tree costs well above 100k, while the top item at highest multiplier gives around 3.5-4k gold, and needs to balance 4 or 5 resources, including animal parts that are inconsistant. All items above the inventory limit are sold for ONE gold, no workaround / alternative to the crafting, you can only sell crafted items.
Also the leveling takes ages - after seeing how much I would need to click, I downloaded an autoclicker for my mouse's and hand's sake. WIth autoclicker (spams clicks) I needed almost a full hour with everything maxed out to get from 28 to 29. It's horrible - the game can not work well as an idler, even when left open -and absolutely not while closed -  but at the same time it requires precision, attention to collect products while absolutely nothing happening - demanding attention while being boring is a criminally bad concept. Sometimes a skull or crocodile surfaces from the river and clicking on them gives miniscule amount of money (10-12k when average product of mine cost ~2k, every few seconds)
So, to sum it up: Voodoo garden has a charming art style, a gameplay that will make you stare at that beautiful art style for hours while barely doing anything, rewarded with slow, meaningless progress. It's a game equivalent of a class with a beatiful landscape with the world's most boring teacher who constantly tells you to pay attention, and the only thing you can motivate yourself is that once it will end. Sorry dev, make it less tedious and a literal timewaster, and I'll edit, potentially even change the review, but literally, finishing Adventure Capitalst and Bad Rats Show were both a less tedious and mind-numbing experience.

Voodoo Garden is a relaxing point and click game with cute music and vibrant colors. You plant trees, shrubs, as well as other greenery. Occasionally you sacrifice animals to use their spirits to guard and harvest produce from your plants.
The only feature that I can see being an issue for some is the clicking. There is a lot of clicking involved. You harvest a combination of plants to craft potions which are then sold, giving you more money to purchase more plants. Repeat, repeat, repeat. Click, Click, Click....
It's kinda like a Facebook game but it doesn't include the stressful time sensitive events, micro transactions or constantly being asked for money. I'd recommend it.
This game is very adorable. It has a learning curve, but it's easy to figure out so that's not such a big deal. It's very much about clicking.

Have you never had a Repetitive Strain Injury?
Have you never blown up a mouse from mashing the LMB forcefully and rapidly?
Have you never raged because bats were stealing all of your stuff?
Have you never overfed a cute animal until it become obese enough to kill for a voodoo ritual?
If you answered "YES!" to these questions,-
Okay, seriously...
The game is very well made, and plays very well. The graphics are a good fit for the game, rather simplistic, cute, and colorful. It's an easy game to play, not a ton of real thought needed. Sound quality is good, and sound effects are good, if a bit boring and repetative. Ran very well on a toaster. Probably better on a cell phone or tablet, but not hard on a low end rig.
Cute game, will take forever to grind out some of the achievements, because you have to click the same thing 1000 tines to get them. Very casual, good time waster for long car or bus rides (where you are not the driver), or sitting and waiting for something or someone (great for sitting in a waiting room at the doctor's office).
Not a "must have" by any means, but still fun, and oddly addictive. In spite of the fact that you know your mouse and clicking finger will regret it later. Not recommended to play while sitting in church or letting your boss catch you wasting time at work (you'll be thrown out on your rump in either case...). But worth it if you get it on a good sale and are looking for mindless clicking to kill some time. And some chickens, rabbits, pigs, and other cute animals. NOT recommended if you have an unnatural fear of sneaky, thieving bats.  :D
7/10 overall

As of version 0.1.2:
InXile has truly created a spiritual successor to PS:T with this game; the world is overflowing with story, depth of character, intrigue, excitement, and choice. That said, what exists now is VERY similar to PS:T and I hope there is a significant directional change as the story progresses further and deeper into Numenera's 9th World.
As an early beta, it is undeniably riddled with bugs, balance, and user interface issues; all of this is to be expected of course. Thus, I don't mind so far and am eager to see the game become more painted, polished and perfected. I have seen FAR worse betas. Many, many, much worse.
My two greatest likes about T:ToN: the beautifully painted areas, and the wonderfully scripted text/dialogue. In this InXile has shone.
What I hope to see more development in: For it's otherwise gorgeous artwork, the user interface (menus, gui/hud, etc) is lacking in the artistic department; it is unfortunately drab and plain. It doesn't reflect the beauty of the world it overlays. There also seems to be a significant amount of interface lag when attempting actions, dialogue, or navigating menus. As noted elsewhere, the game itself seems to suffer from slow transitional load times. Im fairly confident, however, that these problems will be addressed before final release.
In summary: This may be the game I am most excited to play in a very, very long time.

I just finished this game, I wrote an early access review a long time ago but didn't want to write a real review until I beat the game after final release. First off I must say the people complaining about this game aren't really rpg fans, they can't be. I have read some of the ridiculous reviews bad mouthing this game over the dumbest stuff like the developer making changes to the combat system. Who cares, they changed it to turn based combat(it plays great this way) and I see no issue with it affecting the game. The combat doesn't have to be a big part of the game anyway if you don't like the system don't get into combat, you don't lose out on XP either as most of the large gains are from the text options you choose. This lets you play anyway you want and you still can enjoy the story which is fantastic.

Now to get to the actual review. To me it is one of the best rpgs I have ever played and an instant classic, to be honest it is better than Planescape and I loved that game. This game to me hangs with all the classic rpgs from the late 90s and early 2000s like Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dales, Arcanum and the REAL Fallout games. The story is great and a breath of fresh air  because it is new and original enough to make it so you want to see what is going to happen next and don't mind reading all the dialog(this coming from someone who hates to read). I can't recommend this game enough to not only rpg fans but to any person who loves a good story and having their choices that affect the game world, their choices  actually changing what happens in the end game. Not really a spoiler but your choices do show up in the ending of the game, and unlike a game like Mass Effect(which I also loved) which promised to make your choices count and didn't come through, this game does.
I also loved how this game lets you play any way you want. As I stated above, you don't have to fight more than a few times if you don't want too, you can talk your way through 90% of this game easily and get everything with dialog and abilities you could gain with a blade. This game really doesn't punish for roleplaying any type of character, not all rpgs can say that. The XP gains also feel well paced but depending how you play, you can exploit some of the game with abilities at higher levels and make the last parts of the game pretty easy but it doesn't take anything away from the overall experience imo.
So to sum up this review if you skipped my novel above:
Buy this game, it is well worth full price and a steal if you buy it on a sale. This game is for real rpg fans and gamers looking for a very story rich/text heavy game with the freedom to make choices that affect the end game and let you play any style you like with out punishment. I give this game a 9.5/10.

I didn't expect much of this spiritual successor to one of the best RPGs of all time. You know how it is, sequels never live up to your expectiations, if you loved the original (Not because they aren't good, but because the memories of bright things always shine brighter in your mind than they were in reality).
But with Torment: ToN it is different. Because it is not really a sequel. It is filled with creativity, humor, philosophy and weirdness, without being pulled down by having to resort to reliving things that have already been written, worlds that are already known. Everything feels fresh and new, the characters are deep and intriguing and incredibly well written.
But that may be the reason why you may not enjoy it: it is all written. And that is a lot of reading. If you want to see action and don't enjoy reading in games, then you may want to stay away from this one, but if you want to experience history in the making, then you should go ahead and dive in the single most innovative and best written game I have ever played.
This is it. The game RPG fans will talk about for years to come.

At their best, video games are interactive stories. They allow us to participate and meaningfully change things, not just observe the narrative. Some games rise above the rest in this regard.
Torment: Tides of Numenera may be the best I've ever seen.
Some of you like running and gunning FPS titles. This isn't one. If you're an MMO player who follows the map arrows and never reads why you're tasked to do what you're doing, this game may not be for you.
If you love a well written story and want to immerse yourself - and immerse is the right word - in a mysterious world with exquisitely written, branching choices with real impact? You have come to the right place. Where careful reading of the text matters. Where there are no map arrows telling you where to go or what to do with a linear, chain of breadcrumbs quest. Instead, you're rewarded for paying attention. From logic puzzles to not even a single "kill X, pick up Y" quest to the stupendous writing that draws you further and further into the Ninth World, this game amazes.
At time of writing, this is an Early Access beta title with only the first city playable. There are a few broken side quests and a couple bugs, which you're warned about up front. They're putting the final polish on the rest of the title over the next ~7 months. Take negative reviews mentioning performance or bugs with a heaping pile of salt, because those are disclosed up front and won't be there on release.
Simply put, I can't wait.

Now this is one of those games that tear me apart. On one hand it is good yet on the other hand I feel like the developers should be publicly flogged for all those sins they committed when porting this to PC (I don't know if this was developed for PC side by side with the console versions, but feels like a generic console port).
Now this might contain some spoilers though I at least try to avoid them. You have been warned.
The story of the game was amazing. At first it seemed like yet another Call of Duty -ish (or Medal of Honor) game with all-American patriotic attitude and story ("Oh hey... relax. USA ie. The Good Guys are here to save the day from evil terrorists"). But then it just turned... strange. No longer the morals were black and white, but grey, grey and another shade of grey. The player is no longer necessary The One coming to save people from evil. Things go south and it is made clear to the player. Little by little the sanity of the main character is called into question.
Now... the console origin or target is clearly visible in this one. This is not the worst out there, but neither it is one of the best ones. I could bash the game for low quality textures and if I really want to please certain type of people in the internet, I could say things like "It doesn't even have tesselation or <insert new graphical fx here>", but frankly my dear... I don't give a damn about it if the game has decent story or fun mechanics. Yes, the graphics are not that great necessarily, but at least it is not like some ports are: subpar graphics AND requires lots of power to run well.
The level design is also quite boring. While some places and events do look quite nice, they do follow the modern military fps rulebook and are quite linear in design.
Here is the most infuriating thing I encountered. The controls. I get it, they aimed for consoles as well, but it is not a good enough excuse not to polish the PC controls and make them well customizable. It is not all right to bind several actions to a single key (ok... there are exceptions but generally one action per key). Many times I got really annoyed when I wanted to do something (like going into cover) but there was some interactable item near and game thought I wanted to use that item. In addition, I play some games with gamepad (there I said it though it is a curse word for most PC gamers) so I have gamepad connected most of the time. In Spec Ops this resulted in having all the tooltips (press X) showing gamepad controls though I was playing with keyboard and mouse.
The AI is also rather questionable. Enemies seem to be attracted to the player and pin him down while NPC allies are trembling in cover out of fear, only sometimes doing something actually useful. The allies also seem to be the accuracy of a storm trooper (and no, not the ones who attacked Uncle Lars' homestead but the latter ones who apparently also wore a red shirt under the white "armor").
In conclusion, can I recommend this game after this little rant with more negative than positive? Yes, I think I can. While the mechanics and the design is nothing special and the developers are guilty to all seven deadly sins of console porting (I might exaggerate this a little bit), the story and events themselves are enough to draw the game back to positive side. I really liked the story of this game and would like to see more like this.

When I was 18. 18 years old, I saw for the first time in my life. I saw an image of clarity. I saw a comic strip. a three panel comic strip that, though simple as it seemed, changed me. changed my being, changed who I am. Made me who I am. Enlightened me. The strip, Garfield, the comic strip was new. no more than maybe a month and a half since inception, since. since coming into existence. and there it was before me in print, I saw it. a comic strip. What was it called? Garfield. The story here is of a man, a plain man. He is Jon, but he is more than that. I will get to this later, but first let us say that he’s Jon, a plain man. And then there is a cat. Garfield. This is the nature of the world, here. When I see the world, the politics, the future, the. the satellites in space, and. the people who put them there. You can look at everything as a man and a cat. two beings, in harmony and at war. So, this strip I saw; this man, Jon, and the cat, Garfield, you see. Yes. hmm. It is about everything. This. little comic is, oh, lo and behold. not so little anymore. So yes, when I was 18, I saw this comic. and it hit me all at once, its power. I clipped it, and every day, I looked at it, and I said “Okay. let me look at this here. What is this doing to me? Why is this so powerful?” Jon Arbuckle, he sits here, legs crossed. comfortable in his home, and he reads his newspaper. The news of the world, perhaps. and then he extends his fingers lightly, delicately. he taps his fingers on an end table, and he feels for something. What is it? It is something he needs, but it is not there. And then he looks up, slightly cockeyed, and he thinks. His newspaper’s in his lap now, and he thinks this. Now where could my pipe be? This. I always come to this, because I was a young man. I’m older now, and I still don’t have the secrets, the answers, so this question still rings true, Jon looks up and he thinks. Now where could my pipe be? And then it happens.
You see it, you see. it’s almost like divine intervention, suddenly it is there, and it overpowers you. A cat is smoking a pipe. It is the man’s pipe, it’s Jon’s pipe, but the cat. this cat, Garfield, is smoking the pipe. and from afar, and someplace near, but not clear. near but not clear. The man calls out. Jon calls out, he is shocked. “Garfield!” he shouts. Garfield. The cat’s name. But, let’s take a step back. let us examine this from all sides, all perspectives. and when I first came across this comic strip, I was at my father’s house. a newspaper had arrived, and I picked it up for him, and brought it inside. I organized its sections for him and then, yes, the comic strip section fell out from somewhere in the middle, and landed on the kitchen floor. I picked up the paper pages and saw, up somewhere near the top of this strip. just like Jon, I was wearing an aquamarine shirt. So I thought, “Ah, interesting. I’ll have to see this later.” I snipped out the little comic, and held on to it. and five days later, I reexamined it. and it gripped me, I needed to find out more about this. The information I had was minimal, but enough. An orange cat named Garfield. Okay, that seemed to be the lynchpin of this whole operation, yes. Another clue. a signature in the bottom right corner, a man’s name. Jim Davis. Yes, I’m on to it for sure. So. one: Garfield, orange cat, and two: Jim Davis, the creator of this cat. And that curiously plain man. I did not know, at the time, that his name was Jon. This strip, you see, had no mention of this man’s name, and I’d never seen it before. But I had these clues; Jim Davis, Garfield. And then I saw more, I spotted the tiny copyright mark in the upper left corner. Copyright 1978 to. what is this? Copyright belongs to a. PAWS Incorporated. I use the local library and mail services to track down the information I was looking for.
Jim Davis, a cartoonist, had created a comic strip about a cat, Garfield. and a man, Jon Arbuckle. Well, from that point on, I made sure I read the Garfield comic strips, though as I read each one, as each day passed. the strips seemed to resonate with me less and less. I sent letters to PAWS Incorporated, long letters, pages upon pages. asking if Mister Jim Davis could somehow publish just the one comic, over and over again. “It would be meditative,” I wrote, “the strength of that.” Could you imagine? But. no response. The strips lost their power, and eventually I stopped reading, but. I did not want my perceptions diluted, so I vowed to read the pipe strip over and over again. That is what I call it, “The Pipe Strip.” The Pipe Strip. Everything about it is perfect. I can only describe it as a miracle creation, something came together. the elements aligned. It is like the comets, the cosmic orchestra that is up there over your head. The immense, enormous void is working all for one thing, to tell you one thing. Gas and rock, and purity, and nothing. I will say this. When I see the pipe strip. and I mean every single time I look at the lines, the colors, the shapes that make up the three panel comic. I see perfection. Do I find perfection in many things? Some things, I would say. Some things are perfect. and this is one of them. I can look at the little tuft of hair on Jon Arbuckle’s head. it is the perfect shade. The purple pipe in Garfield’s mouth. How could a mere mortal even MAKE this? I have a theory, about Jim Davis. After copious research and, yes, of course, now we have the internet, and this information is all readily available, but. Jim Davis, he used his life experiences to influence his comic. Like I mentioned before, none of them seem to have the weight of the pipe strip. But you have to wonder about the man who is able to even, just once, create the perfect form, a literally flawless execution of art, brilliance!
Just as in a ward. I think there is a spiritual element at work. I’ve seen my share of bad times and. when you have something. Well, it’s just. emotions, and neurons in your brain, but. something tells you that it’s the truth. Truth’s radiant light. Garfield, the cat? Neurons in my brain, it’s. it’s harmony, you see? It. Jon and Garfield, it’s truly harmony, like a. continuous, looping, everlasting harmony. The lavender chair, the brown end table, the salmon-colored wall, the fore’s green carpeting, Garfield is hunched, perched. perhaps with the pipe stuck firmly between his jowls. His tail curls around. It’s more than shapes too, because. I. Okay, stay with me. I’ve done this experiment several times. You take the strip. You trace only the basic elements. You can do anything, you can simplify the shapes down to just. blobs, just outlines, but it still makes sense. You can replace the blobs with magazine cutouts of other things, replace Jon Arbuckle with a. car parked in a driveway sideways, cut that out of a magazine, stick it in. Replace him there in the second panel with a. a food processor. Okay, and then we put a picture of the planet in the third panel over Garfield. It still works. These are universal proportions. I don’t know. how best to explain why it works, I’ve studied the pipe strip, and analyzed Jon and Garfield’s proportions against several universal mathematical constants. E, Pi, the Golden Ratio, the Feigenbaum Constants, and so on. and it’s surprising. scary even, how things align. You can take just. tiny pieces of the pipe strip, for instance, take Jon’s elbow from the second panel. and take that, and project it back over Jon’s entire shape in the second panel, and you’ll see a near perfect Fibonacci sequence emerge. It’s eerie to me. and it makes you wonder if you’re in the presence of a deity, if there is some larger hand at work. There’s no doubt in my mind that Jim Davis is a smart man. Jim Davis is capable of anything to me.
He is remarkable, but this is so far beyond that, I think we might see that. this work of art is revered and respected in years to come.

A good game bogged down by some poor design choices. First the pros.
This game is beautiful with a great color pallete and wonderfully designed characters that will harken back to a time of colorful mascot platformers. The roots of banjo kazooie stand out in this game and it looks as colorful and filled with character as banjo. The music is wonderful with the same composer coming back to work on it, and the movesets are satisfying and interesting. Each world is detailed and rich, each with its own unique sense of style.
And now on to the cons.
This is a 90s mascot platformer at it's core, warts and all. This means that the game has some severe camera issues, problems with annoying enemy types, and generally not telling the player what to do. In addition, the locations of collectables is not laid out in such a way as to show the player where to go, or give an idea of where things might be. They are randomly sprinkled throughout the levels. This is a problem as I am often wondering what I am supposed to do in this big bright colorful world I live in. Worlds can feel quite barren, with only a few enemies. In addition, whoever came up with the trivia sections should be fired. From a cannon.
Overall, a solid buy if you can get it on sale as it's problems keep me from getting it at full price. Again, this is not a bad game, but it has some issues that I hope get addressed somewhat in either patches, or Yooka 2.

When you lose everything...your love and your belongings...sometimes you just put a gun on your head and pull the trigger....sometimes you simply become selfish as hell...or sometimes you keep thinking about all your mistakes till you become mad...
Is this game real or not? Is it a true story or is just everything in your mind? Are you living your own real life or are you punishing yourself because you was unable to protect the ones you loved?....Play it and simply understand what you think it's the right one...
MadMax is an action game where you play the role of Max that♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off the wrong guy in the very beginning and you will find yourself with nothing but just your clothes.
Your final objective in this game is to escape from this hell...and leave nothing behind apart yourself and your V8 (the most DESIRED object from Max since the first minutes of the game).
Thing is that during your "escape" you will meet a lot of people that will change your life again...
The scenario is a doomed apocaliptic world where water ad gasoline are the new "gold". And people are very willing to kill each other to get them.
The map is nicely done and really huge, it's divided in several territories. Each of them is ruled by a specific characater that will help you during your adventure.
It is even filled with a lot of places to explore and items to collect (from old artifacts -pictures- to scraps -used to upgrade and build stuff- to camps -to conquer- a lot of stuff to blow up -scarecrow and sniper towers mostly- and RACES...yes...RACES)
There are plenty of upgrades for both you and your car.
The game is even filled with a lot of challenges; some of them are impossible to miss because they are story related. The rest will simply keep you busy and make you enjoy the game more and more.
Completing those challenges will give you some coins to spend to upgrade the specs of Max. Those ones gives you bonuses (like more health, resistance, bonus on water and gasoline etc...).
The gameplay is fun and it's very frenetic when it comes to combat because the most used weapons will be your fists.
You can play it both with mouse + keyboard or with a controller (much better)
Why you should buy this game?
- The story is really good and it's very emotional in some parts.
- Freeroaming....come on we all love it....
- Cars, customizations and demolition derby...here if you played FlatOut you will really love it...you can build your own customized car or use one of the standard ones (the Archangels)
- Graphics...yes is not an important thing but it's really good.
- Sounds, specially cars sounds.
Why you should NOT buy this game?
- The story....yeah it will grown up feelings inside you and it will throw away your heart....so if you are too much emotional beware
- Sounds...they are good but sometimes all the cars sounds the same...and if you love cars this could be a turn off
- Several minor glitches like be killed from a car while your are looking at a cutscene, don't get some achivements, find yourself floating in the air after a dialogue
- The challenges...sometimes they will run you mad.
- If you like weapons and items of mass destruction....here you will not find anything like this.
- If you don't like deserts...
Overall:
Graphic 9/10
Sounds 8/10
Longevity 8/10
Gameplay 8/10

At almost 100 hours clocked of this game, I still am not necessarily any better than I was at the start. Okay, not true. I can make it to cycle 140 now, whereas I couldn't get past cycle 30 before. Oxygen is still a nightmare to get, and if you run out of metal I haven't quite figured out how to get past that, and if my some miracle you figure out the power system (hooray, I did this, this week!) you start sending too much power through your wires and they start breaking!! There is so much to keep your eye on, so many options! This game doesn't seem to have just one way of doing something, it offers a few, but from my own games, it seems like you sort of end up trying to do everything! Though, not sure that's the best way...
It's not just oxygen you fight in this game, but the duplicates themselves. Sometimes they're infuriating, and sometimes wonderful and other times just plain stupid. Their stress responses, the kind of food they will and won't eat (that's another pain to add to the list), and their indidvidual decor expectations all add to up to issues you can easily forget about until suddenly Meep is DESTROYING EVERYTHING IN YOUR BASE. Dammit, Meep.
All in all, I throughouly love this infuriating management game. It keeps me distracted for HOURS on end. And by the end of it, when my duplicates inevitably die from lack of oxygen, food, or trapping their faces in the wall they're building, I am proud of how far I've managed to come, how much I've managed to learn, and how long I did survive on this asteriod.
Love this game, and will recommend it to everyone who likes management games, or is already a fan of Klei Entertainment.

My rating:

For a game where the MC's player model looks like he's constipated, it's pretty damn good for the time it was made. The shoot-em-up gameplay is really solid and fun for the most part, while not having much to it. It's constant grasp of having a 1st person perspective through all the events of the game really helps the psychological sections of the story. This game actually takes it's time to go through the psyche of Max. Almost like the sections are something out of Silent Hill. For the time, all the sound for the guns, especially the shotgun shells hitting the ground, is fantastic. All the bullet marks on the environment, the blood, bodies and even bullet shells stay present during the level. So after a big shootout you can look at all of the mess and get the feeling of your surroundings being more organic, like your actions have impact. Being able to replicate the lobby scene from The Matrix was fun too. There are other cultural references too, like a "blink and you'll miss it" mention of Microsoft. An actually satisfying revenge story (probably because you're playing it) unlike others in movies, it actually feels like it's all justified. But by the end I'm just thinking that Max should just put aside the crime fighting/shooting bad guys career and take up becoming an author, the guy talks about things like a bloody poet.

Some parts of the game are a bit of a slog like repeating Kartos' sections because you missed a gem by inches, and Rextro's arcade sections were a bit annoyed that you have to play them twice even if you did enough to high score them the first time.

I feel like most negative reviews of this game are people trying way too hard to compare it to banjo kazooie and trying to have it reinvigorate the same feelings they once felt as a child.
Regardless of how good a game is, this expectation will nearly always fall flat. Not because of the quality of the game is lacking, but because when you have so many expectations in a game, the game doesn't surprise you. It doesn't give you those special, unexpected, awe inspiring moments. You expected dumb humor, you expected collecting things, you expect that each unique part of every world is going to give you a jiggy (pagie). You expect there to be a hub world with a silly bad guy and you expect all of these moves that you are going to learn and how they will allow you to backtrack into previous worlds to get 100% collection. It's not just the high quality of expectations that I feel are dangerous, but the high quantity of expectations that result in the game being so much like what you expected that it no longer creates a new, unique experience that you had hoped for.
Onto the actual review...
Pros+
It is a collect-a-thon. That has to be a pro if you are going to buy this game.
It has some charm to it in terms of humor and character personalities.
A nice variety of ways to acquire the collectables in each world.
A few very hidden treasures makes for a few of those really cool moments.
Really nice game length, although some may say a bit short (15-20 hours for me and I got 100% with slight help from the internet).
Enjoyable bosses with just the right amount of difficulty.
Bright, colorful worlds with nice graphics for the style of the game.
Neutral=
I found the world expansion feature not very interesting, because once you start collecting almost all pagies available in the current world, you can immediately open AND expand the next world, pretty much eliminating the whole point of world expansion.
Although this is likely the same situation in previous games, it sometimes did feel like when you entered a new world that you were basically just going through a checklist of areas. It's very easy to spot pretty much every single pagie in a world just by looking around and saying "yea there's a door, there's an arcade, there's a mini game, there's a challenge", and it almost feels like you can see everything you have to do to get pagies, and then you go do it. It just doesn't create a huge sense of wonder when you can see everything so well, despite the worlds being very pretty. I'm not saying that going and collecting the pagies wasn't fun, but being able to see everything so well did not add to my enjoyment.
Cons-
The flying controls and camera are not the best, but they are absolutely not a reason to not buy this game.
No inter-world connectedness. All worlds are just independent from each other.
Overall, I really enjoyed this game. If you enjoy collecting things, then get this game. It's not very hard, and it's not supposed to be. It's supposed to be a fun, relaxing adventure as you complete various challenges and mini games while acquiring new moves to complete more challenges and mini-games. It plays that role very well.

I love the idea of this game more than the execution.
The style and feel of the game was built on nostalgia for older games like banjo-kazooie, however, it has a feel of emptiness to the whole game, combat feels unsatisfying and awkward at times and there are issues they took way too long to patch to problems that are actually really common place in many games now (skipping cutscenes/dialogue etc) especially considering how many people were irritated by the games voices.
There were other strange choices such as parts of the game requiring you to pass a quiz about the game (where was this picture taken etc) which were honestly awful, they destroyed any pacing the game had and relied a lot on locations/characters being memorable that actually weren't (one involved you naming one of four toilets from a level, each as forgettable as the last).
I truly appreciate what they tried to do, visually some parts of the game are pretty cool and I actually thought most of the music was quite pleasant but the game was bogged down with too much unnecessary filler, strange outdated decisions regarding the games design and bosses and frankly poor level design (I often got confused where the hell I was supposed to be going, including in the hub world) that no amount of nostalgia can save it from being merely an ok game.
I hope they get another chance to make a second game and really sort out the issues that arose from this one as I believe they could make something amazing.
I'd grab it on a reasonably low discount but anything above £20 just feels too much for what you get.
Sorry Playtonic, but like I said learn from what you did wrong with this installment and you'll have no issue making the next one amazing

I've spent almost 100 hours playing this game. I've made several bases and had many tasks to challenge. Through the 100 hours having playing this game, this is a really enjoyable survival,base builder, and probably the most intricate and interesting one yet. There are still features I haven't fully explored yet, and ideas and methods to use that could heavily improve my experience and make things easier and more fun.
The problem is finding those methods, and understanding them..
I'm going to start of with the positives to this game, this game looks great. It follows that classic Klei artstyle used in a couple of their great games, most notably, Don't Starve. The artstyle really works well in games like these, it makes it look quite nice and cute, but maintains a gritty look that is still quite nice to look at. The character models are well done as well, and are charming with their little animations they do throughout certain points of the game. The game runs relatively smoothly on my crappy laptop (which is really designed for work, and not gaming.)
There is so much to do in this game. There are alot of features that I've gone through and tried, but yet, there is still more for me to try out. The games new features it throws your way are always a suprise to come across, and even though only being around for two updates, I lookforward to the next one they present. The new Automation Update looks interesting, and I'm ready to explore what it can do (As I haven't discovered how they work yet, as it uses features such as gates and such) and the newer Tubular Update looks fantastic, and should prove to be really helpful in transportation situations.
Most of the features in the game are really well designed (Some, on the other hand, are not). You start out with nothing at first, just basic materials in one small biome that has 3 Water sources scattered around you. As you expand and improve, you learn alot from the hints that are shown and just by what you've experienced before as you go on later. You expand out to a full colony and see how far you can go, and whether you can explore the whole astroid. Every biome has something new to find, and something that can determine whether you can get out of a sticky situation or not. These situations come around alot, especially as you go on later in the game. I like how you can find other bases layed out in the game, and when first playing, it was always exciting finding one of these, as I hoped to find something or even someone in there. The supplys you can find in there can be really helpful, even though it's mostly sweaters and clothing, but you can still find food and left over wires and water if that's scarce.
The game is very fun, but can sometimes get a bit tiring and fustrating when you get in around 100-150 cycles, but, upon first starting the game, I spent around 5 hours playing and figuring out things for myself, everytime I'd explore more and do more research, It would add another hour or so of experminting with this and playing around with it and seeing what my duplicants would do and how it worked.
Right, time to move onto the negative sides of things:
As I just said, this game is fun, but after a week of playing consistantly, the game becomes a little repative, after restarting bases over bases, and starting again and again. Sometimes I would come back after a couple of weeks and find myself playing it again for another week. It would be nice to have something rare or different to find in certain seeds and biomes, I know you can find other bases scattered around, but there's mostly the same stuff in there, so something that could be quite benificial to find which could make a big difference to how you play would be quite nice, and possibly improve gameplay and make me play a little more.
(This part may be a bit bias and be a little more visual liking than gameplay enhancement ?) Decor is a really nice feature, but I find that there's not enough of things to really make the base look really nice and homely. Paintings are nice to have around (Really only when they're masterpieces) and I love having plant pots and statues around, but apart from that, there's not much decor specific items available in my opinion. I would love to have different painting frames that are shorter or longer in width and height, so that you can put them in better places, and things like hanging baskets or furniture. Decor reduces stress, so instead of having massage tables alone, it would be nice to have a living room with nice furniture and frames in there for the duplicants to relax in. Maybe even implament a social feature in the game, where duplicants can socialize and that can be shown in game, as I find the duplicants pretty emotionless and boring. Only in situations such as stress is really where you see some emotion from them. Once again, this part is probably a bias.
My last point(s) is alot. And I feel (If anyone bothers to read this whole thing) that some people might disagree with this point, but this game has ALOT to handle when it gets to the later cycles, and some features are not explained well and make the game VERY confusing and VERY fustrating. From around cycle 80-150 the game just seems to get harder and more of a pain to take on, (This is due to research, I know, Probably) But I think it all starts when one thing goes wrong and your focusing on something else. For example, I set my amount of duplicants to 6, and I think most people do, and they're fine until cycle 80 or so. Once I'm tackling a quite tough task (Getting Oil, More Metal or Trying to Collect more Water) the duplicants focus on that, but then food becomes scarce and so I have to go back and make some, but I don't have any water (I usually use microbe mushers as it's just easier and quicker than setting up a farm). I go get more water, but then I can't get more water because I don't have enough power from my source, and I can't expand that source due to how people are starving and there's not enough oxygen, and they can't provide power to the source I already have because there's no oxygen in there. I know this games whole point is management and everything and this is enforced in these times of games, and yes maybe I'm not good at it but good god, I found myself going in an infinite loop here, and I find it impossible getting out of these sticky situations.
I think electricity needs a bit of a revamp. Power overloading is confusing, and tedious to work with, and incredibly fustrating if you have no idea what you're doing. It would be nice to have a diagram for the player to use or get an idea from instead of being told the basic function of the Power Transformer which is still quite confusing in my eyes. It took me four(?) forum posts to figure out how to fix Power Overloading. I wanted to try and figure out the game on my own but I had to resort to other things. (This point is probably not very valid, and I can't think of many other features where it's not explained well, Maybe Automation? I haven't checked it out though so)
A small feature is how materials outside of your accessable area for some reason still display as usable, and whenever I ask the duplicants to do something, but can't because there's no materials that they can get to, is a little annoying, and would be nice to see something to tell the player this.
Finding easier and quicker methods to do things are quite hard without help from forums and such. It would be nice to have some sort of hint by the game.
So, Finally, I'd recommend this game Alot. If you enjoy games like survival base builders, and you're good at maintaining things then you'll really enjoy this. It's fun and interesting, and is really well designed.

I tend to avoid Open world games but this one I couldn't resist and while it do have some of the Open World design problems like a crap ton of things cluttering the map the content keeps it fun and engaging. The story is pretty weak in my opinion and the developers try to use an emotional beat late in the game that I don't think they earn. The pacing is really weird in my opinion and in order to achieve any impact they had to make it at least twice as long...if they could write it so its fun, engrossing and engaging which I doubt to be honest.
The game starts kind of slow and you have to play for about 2 hours until the game opens up and starts to become really fun. In the game you collect Scrap which is the currency used to buy physical upgrades for Max in the form of equipment upgrades to upgrades for the Magnum Opus (your car). Max himself can upgrade various abilites like health meter and so on by Griffa Tokens which you earn by completing various task in the game. You will get quite many just by playing the game so I never had to make a concentrated effort in order to get Griffa Tokens in order to upgrade Max.
Since the Scrap is quite scarce I would recommend you do the following in order to maximize your Scrap collecting:
1. When you get to a stronghold make sure to find and build the upgrades that collect scrap when you are offline (as in not playing the game) and the upgrade that collects scrap from demolished cars automatically so you dont have to stop and pick it up.
2. Use your Griffa Tokens to maximize Maxs Scrap Volition Ability. The more tokens you put here the more bonus scrap Max will get for every looting. Maxed out you get about 50% more scrap per looting which makes a difference.
3. Take over all the camps in every region and territory. First of all the Camps are probably one of the best part of the game. Every camps layout and design is unique and they are very varied which makes it a joy to explore them and take them over. When you have cleared a camp that camp will produce Scrap for you at set intervalls. I think it is about every 30 minutes. When you have taken over every camp in the game you get about 740 scrap every 30 minutes which also helps a lot.
As Open Worlds go this one is beautiful with a lot of varied enviroments. I think they have managed to squeeze in every type of desert that exist and some other wordly ones. There really are some stunning vistas in the game and it runs like butter. Its a very good and optimized port where you should be able to crank up the settings pretty high even on a modest set up. I personally have a I7 6700K@4.4GHz and a 980Ti OC and with everything maxed out I averaged about 180FPS!
The only thing I didn't like in the game is that in order to reduce the threat level in a territory you have to remove minefields. These minefields you have to use a special car that you can't fast travel with and it is a chore to clear these minefields. Its easy but timeconsuming. Granted its completely optional but if you want to reduce the threat level for a region to 0 in order to get some of the upgrades to Magnus Opus be prepared to devote some time for this. The upside is that the vehicle in question can drive full speed across almost every terrain so just take the birds eye route from minefield to minefield.
But other than that I really enjoyed the game and had a great time with it and I would like to finish with an anecdote that I experienced while taking on a convoy. Oh yeah forgot about that, there are convoys in the game which also are a blast to take on. Especially when your Magnus Opus is fully upgraded. Anyway, here comes the anecdote:
So I am taking on a convoy while listening to the Fury Road OST through the Steam Music Player. I manage to take out all but the lead car and 2 support cars before having to stop for repair while they drive off. As soon as the Magnus Opus is repaired I turn it around and drive against the convoy-route. My position is a bit more elevated so I can see part of the route in the distant to the right and the signature dustwind that follows the lead convoy vechile so I press full on ahead against a turn where we will collide. At this point I am listening to "Brothers in Arms" and the song is about to crescendo. About 100 meters from our imminent collision a huge duststorm starts mounting. The music hits the crescendo, the duststorm arrives and make a head on smash with one of the support vehicles turning it to a huge explosion. I quickly turn around and hits the nitro boost while debries is flying around to catch up with the 2 remaining vehicles. I pull out a thunderpoon and turn the second support vehicle to a huge fireball. The Music switches track and appropiately its the one which plays during the dust storm in Fury Road while I am battling out with the lead convoy vehicle. After a couple of good rammings I finally delivers the killing blow and it goes up in smitherins. At that moment it felt like I was being a part of Fury Road with all the thrills and excitement and it was Epic. I couldn't have directed it more perfectly if I had tried.
I can definitely recommend this game!

text:
When you lose everything...your love and your belongings...sometimes you just put a gun on your head and pull the trigger....sometimes you simply become selfish as hell...or sometimes you keep thinking about all your mistakes till you become mad...
Is this game real or not? Is it a true story or is just everything in your mind? Are you living your own real life or are you punishing yourself because you was unable to protect the ones you loved?....Play it and simply understand what you think it's the right one...
MadMax is an action game where you play the role of Max that♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off the wrong guy in the very beginning and you will find yourself with nothing but just your clothes.
Your final objective in this game is to escape from this hell...and leave nothing behind apart yourself and your V8 (the most DESIRED object from Max since the first minutes of the game).
Thing is that during your "escape" you will meet a lot of people that will change your life again...
The scenario is a doomed apocaliptic world where water ad gasoline are the new "gold". And people are very willing to kill each other to get them.
The map is nicely done and really huge, it's divided in several territories. Each of them is ruled by a specific characater that will help you during your adventure.
It is even filled with a lot of places to explore and items to collect (from old artifacts -pictures- to scraps -used to upgrade and build stuff- to camps -to conquer- a lot of stuff to blow up -scarecrow and sniper towers mostly- and RACES...yes...RACES)
There are plenty of upgrades for both you and your car.
The game is even filled with a lot of challenges; some of them are impossible to miss because they are story related. The rest will simply keep you busy and make you enjoy the game more and more.
Completing those challenges will give you some coins to spend to upgrade the specs of Max. Those ones gives you bonuses (like more health, resistance, bonus on water and gasoline etc...).
The gameplay is fun and it's very frenetic when it comes to combat because the most used weapons will be your fists.
You can play it both with mouse + keyboard or with a controller (much better)
Why you should buy this game?
- The story is really good and it's very emotional in some parts.
- Freeroaming....come on we all love it....
- Cars, customizations and demolition derby...here if you played FlatOut you will really love it...you can build your own customized car or use one of the standard ones (the Archangels)
- Graphics...yes is not an important thing but it's really good.
- Sounds, specially cars sounds.
Why you should NOT buy this game?
- The story....yeah it will grown up feelings inside you and it will throw away your heart....so if you are too much emotional beware
- Sounds...they are good but sometimes all the cars sounds the same...and if you love cars this could be a turn off
- Several minor glitches like be killed from a car while your are looking at a cutscene, don't get some achivements, find yourself floating in the air after a dialogue
- The challenges...sometimes they will run you mad.
- If you like weapons and items of mass destruction....here you will not find anything like this.
- If you don't like deserts...
Overall:
Graphic 9/10
Sounds 8/10
Longevity 8/10
Gameplay 8/10
The driving is fun and the combat is batmanish but overall a great experience, as well as a cheap price tag.

First of all, I DID like the game. But it was, at the same time, deceiving. I'd give it a 6/10, but if it were the right price, I'd give it a 8.5/10 for sure.
Let's start with the good things about it: it is a very enjoyable, nice and light game. Most dads are also charming, the art is great, too.
But on the other hand... routes are extremely, extremely short. Takes around 45 minutes to complete each route. Not only that, but the endings are very limited, only having 2 endings, so there's no room for replaying it to find the rest of the endings. I remember the Official Twitter promised multiple endings per dad. You don't get to know the characters, and most of the time, it doesn't really feel like you're flirting with them. I only got that impression with Damien. It's like you guys are obviously just friends until the end of the third date where you suddenly kiss and love each other. I was really excited to do Brian's route, but was very deceived to find that his route is just... being rivals and at the very end kissing. Nothing more. It felt empty and superficial, despite the cute shirtless moment or the final kiss and hug at Amanda's party. Didn't feel like a real developing relationship. I think that it wasn't only because of how short the route is, but because of how it was written as well. You could also have a short route where it does seem like they're flirting, like Damien's.
Your character also has a personality that can't be changed, which I've found a bit distracting when it came to dating other dads, because I felt there was no chemistry between my character and his love interest even if I really liked the dad I was trying to romance just because my character spoke for me. I don't know if this is normal for dating sims, though.
Next issue is how overpriced it is for such a short game. 15 dollars isn't what this game is worth, in my opinion. I'm mostly upset about having spent that amount of money on a game that isn't worth it. Had it been cheaper I would have been content because I paid for the content I was given. It is, still, a very nice enjoyable lighthearted game.
Another thing that bothered me was the voices. Grunts isn't voicing and it gets really annoying. I don't care about the Game Grumps, but it feels like they haven't done much for the game. Would have been better if they hadn't participated in this project at all.
And now, this is my personal opinion but... Amanda can get reaaaaally annoying. I know it's a Dad game and all that, but when you have to do several routes and hear her story once and once again it gets tiring and irritating.
But once again... this is a nice game. Cute, entertaining (except for the Amanda bits...) and with interesting characters, even though they don't really get to be fleshed out. I recommend it, but not for this price. I'd wait for a sale. I really, really hope more content is added later on, because despite my review looking negative, I really liked the game and some of the dads and I'm looking forward to some more dad dating.

Is this game too expensive for the amount of content it offers? Yes.
Is it still worth paying the full price? Yes, absolutely.
The true value of this game is in showing how a healthy romance should look like: you will not have a succesful date unless you know how to respect and appreciate your chosen dad. This silly little cartoon game does wonders to promote relationships in which no one is pushing the other side into anything for personal gratification, and in which both sides respect each other's needs and boundaries.
It is also a true gem in showing wonderful, heart-warming father-children relationships. You, as the player character, may not be the perfect dad, and Amanda may not be the perfect daughter, but the love and kindness they have for each other, and their will to work hard to understand and solve problems together, are very touching. It's worth noting, that the other dads are having parenting difficulties of their own which you can help them overcome.
Overall, Dream Daddy is one of the most warm, kind, uplifting and genuinely funny games I have ever played.

I'll start with what I liked, as that's polite and fair:
- The writing was really well done in terms of content, I was never particularly disinterested by what I hadn't read before.
- Dad puns were executed as advertised.
- There were some genuinely good jokes and good moments.
- The story's much better than I actually expected.
- Art is on point pretty much at all times.
- Music is fitting and not unbearable. Dig the wasp from that one loop.
- Dad tips at loading screens kept things a little better.
- Apparently MCR references everywhere but I haven't heard the group so I'm just taking others' word on it.
- It's Game Grumps. But I'm sure you already knew.
Here's the bad:
- The writing had a lot of basic errors, i.e. improper (or lack of) punctuation, "anymore" instead of "any more." This was okay until I noticed the first error. Then they kept coming up, and at some point I was no longer able to actually focus on the script because the errors stuck out like rats in a garden hose.
- I know I said the story's better than I expected. But that doesn't give the story a pass. After the first run, the skip button is pretty much essential in everything but the dates. The story isn't anything that takes much to understand and really only the first time through is interesting because it's new to you. It doesn't really resonate much.
- Music loops gets dull after pretty much two runs. I mean, there's some songs that are really well built, and some I wish weren't only in one scene (i.e. the song at the bar, the bragging battle one), but then you get to the storyline loops and you're just disappointed. The wasp I mentioned up above is panned all the way to the left, leaving the whole track just feeling awkward. I've done trashier games with stronger music games.
- After a couple sets of dates, I really just felt like I was to the point of achievement farming. I lost interest in the cardboard cutouts of universal archetypes which I am quite sure were pretty much pulled verbatim from TV Tropes. Hell, even the I-only-want-to-hook-up-guy's track (probably the one with anything akin to actual conflict) didn't sit right with me.
- It was really hard to get into the game after that very first run. I finished the first and was satisfied. The one and only other game of this sort of genre I've done (arguably a more serious one, I suppose) kept me interested in every ending I did in spite of its own main plot flaws.
- Fifteen dollars is a tad steep for this title really. I paid less for the aforementioned other title I've done of this sort of thing, and its price is still lower than this one's with no sales. I wish I had waited until a sale, because I could have gotten a large pizza and a couple 2-liter bottles of soda at this price.
- Seven dads but unless the endings don't set off achievements, misadvertisement on the endings per-Dad. I couldn't stay interested long enough to really test this theory. I felt like every run I pushed through led to the exact same ending really.
- #SmallTeamProblems all over the place. It very much feels like they're biting off way more than they can chew with this one, as demonstrated by the late release.
- If I record my grunts and hmmmms and ohs I can say my game is "voiced" too! It was sorta okay I guess, I understand they were strapped for time and grossly underestimated the amount of work it takes to get one of these things out. I'm at the very entrance of the rabbit hole and I still haven't heard the thing I dropped hit the ground.
- Loading screens? In a visual novel style game? The only other game of this sort I've ever done simply faded to black and had pretty much zero load times. I can understand for the minigames it may take a bit longer but I simply couldn't stand that there were honest to god loading screens in this game that would bring skipping to a screeching halt. I understand it's something minor and insignificant and dare I say petty, but jfc that really just made skipping harder.
- Did I mention you'll be learning to hold down the skip button? Did I also mention that you might even hold it down so hard you actually miss the few lines you've never seen before? Did I mention that if you skip certain lines or you scroll through em too fast, there's no way to backtrack and read through them again?
- Did I mention that these are all issues in a $15 game, not a freebie made by a couple people just wanting to get their names out there?
Another thing of note: This game is being released at a time where YouTube ad revenue is falling. That means that this game is pretty much a ploy to keep their earnings up while ad revenue is low. I don't necessarily think it's a particularly bad thing on its own, but I feel they eschewed quality to execute a more ideal business strategy.
So in conclusion, I can get that this is very much a game for quick thrill daddy lovin' but it really doesn't provide much more, leaving... quite a lot to be desired really. Even as a parody it really lacks the proper elements to make a satisfying mockery.

Anatola's work has always been a massive inspiration for be during my growth as an artist. When I heard that they had created a game which would utilize the elements of their art/animation style, I was estatic! I had been well aware of their talent for character design, their funky style of animation, and their incredible way of creating such beautiful, intricate, colorful backgrounds! For the longest time, I wasn't able to buy the game and kept myself from spoilers as much as I could. I kept my ground and pushed through, until I was finally able to purchase the game today!
Without a doubt, it was well worth the wait. For such a short, simple, little game, it brought me so much emotion and enjoyment. Each character, though given small interactions with Maggie, has their own diverse personality and uniqueness! I fell absolutely in love with these characters! They're all so varied in design, dialogue, story. It's pretty amazing! The background design is just as beautiful as I hoped it would be. All of the fractals of color within each background stuck out to me a lot! I love the care put into it all! I love the way each piece of the game fits together into something so humorous and charming. Figuring out each piece of the puzzle was so fun and honestly scary at times!! I felt so mant emotions for Maggie's struggle, as well as Beauty's....hell...even Dunc's! It was an incredible experience all around and I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys well written characters, story, and gorgeous artistry!
I'd also highly recommend this game to anyone who has experiences with trauma or abuse? As silly as it may seem, this game and its story provided a lot of comfort for me as someone who has been through many experiences with abuse/sexual harrassment/manipulation/or otherwise. It's a very comforting, loving story with so much care and so much humor, so much turmoil and so much struggle. I couldn't ask for a better game from 'Tola. Keep 'em coming, bud! Your stuff is one in a million!!
