I sit on the edge of a building looking down on some criminals on Christmas Eve trying to learn the whereabouts of the Black Mask. These guys don’t have much of a lead but they are up to no good so first I need to drop down and do a little training on a few faces.
Origins is the third game from the new Batman series but takes place before the last two. You are basically in the early years of being the bat. You’ll get to see some of the first encounters with some classic villains from the Batman stories we all love. Black Mask has put a $50 million bounty on Batman’s head and you now get the fun and excitement of dealing with all the villains who want that money. Not all is what it seems as you are soon to find out after a little progression and discovery.
The games graphics look about the same as AA & AC. Which is a good thing because I love the looks of the characters and environment. I did notice the lip syncing to be off sometimes but no problems there. Voices were all great like usual and I love the music specially the darker tone Christmas stuff.
Gameplay is what you expect from the last two games. Use your predator skills for silent takedowns which is always fun. Gadgets galore to use at your disposal. Like the new glue grenades to immobilize an attacker for a short time, or a gun which shoots a wire across to anchor points to be used as a zip line or tight rope. You can also use it to hook criminals to objects or each other.  Many fun times with that one. Other gadgets are your typical batarangs, grappling hook, explosive gel, and some others from the previous games.
There’s plenty to do in Gotham this time around with some side stories like Anarky, Deadshot and a few others. Small crimes you can solve which is now done with a cool feature were you can see a reenactment of the crime to discover what happen. A pretty cool feature and should be expanded on later down the line. Then there are the Riddler challenges again, which are just small packages you find throughout the city. Not as cool as the Riddler challenges from the previous game but it does give a little change.
Now the combat is what Rocksteady had perfected in the last two games and really made it exciting and fun to get into fist fights with your enemies. It was so fluid and fast and just beautiful to pull off some amazing moves. I’m not sure what happen but WB Montreal seem to screw up the system. Counters don’t seem to work many times and the fighting just did not feel as balanced as usual. It was disappointing and aggravating at times but I still had a blast playing.
Batman: Arkham Origins is a wonderful game to play and a great addition to the Batman franchise even despite its small flaws and some bugs I encountered. Like the red screen bug you get when entering the GCPD. Your screen turns red when you enter the rooftop door and then your PC restarts after like 10 seconds. An easy fix as you just have to put the game into windowed mode before entering and you can then go back full screen after that. Just be careful though because one downfall I got was after I beat the game and was almost finished with all side missions I forgot about this bug and got the red screen. When I restarted everything up again I had lost the last 7 hours of gameplay and all my completion stats. Luckily for me I had finished the game before this happened.
If the little issues don’t scare you away then pick this up and enjoy the great Batman story and fun.

SG2 is an RPG set in space and can be described as a poorly excecuted Freelancer clone.

In my personal opinion, this game may just be the best that has ever been made. From the people that brought you childhood favorites such as "Pajama Sam", "Freddi Fish", and The "Putt-Putt" Series comes an all new take on kart racers. Although many may draw similarities between Garfield Kart and Mario Kart, I can assure you that Garfield Kart is a much more intensely immersive experience than that of any Mario Kart game that you have ever played. A more accurate comparison would be to The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, as it compares not only in immersion, but in gameplay, graphics, storyline, and replayability. Once you begin your first race, you get sucked into the lasaga. Upgrading and stylizing your own playstyle is a very important part of Garfield Kart. This is the game that you will be saying "Where did all my time go", because as soon as you hit that juicy asphalt, the lasaga hits you and the mondays are forever behind you. There is a huge selection of unlockable characters that you can play as on your journey to becoming the king of the kart. The massive amount of racing tracks compares to games like Big Rigs: Over the Road Racing and Borderlands 2. When you drift along that sweet, sweet paving, you get the sense that you are actually the lasaga loving feline himself. Garfield Kart is easily my favorite game in my Steam library.

As one who has played Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie enough to develop Stockholm syndrome with those game, I think it's fair enough I know the pros and cons to Yooka-Laylee as a whole. You may agree with me or may not, but any independent though, positive or negative is appreciated. Aside from that, here's what I think.
In short.
Is Yooka-Laylee good: Yes
Is it absolutely flawless: No
Should you buy it: Eh... Let's just say $40 is at least a week’s worth of groceries.
In Long. (And I mean LONG, scroll down to the bottom for my final thoughts.)
I wasn't an adamant follower of this game's development, so I wasn't 100% aware of what to expect until it was about a week or two from launch. I still bought it, with a brand new 360 controller to play it with, to the dismay of my bank account. Regardless, I was able to pick it up quickly, and run it with my computer pretty darn smoothly. (after lowering the graphics settings to the lowest possible option, but my computer sucks so this is a moot point) I highly recommend playing this game with some form of controller, based on past experiences, 3D platformers don't do well with Keyboard and mouse. Controllers are a bit expensive, but you'll be thankful in the long run. (360 USB controller is recommended)
Out of all the games in my steam library, this has to be a unique gem. And, correct me if I'm wrong, there aren’t many games out there on Steam that are of the Collectathon Platformer genre. So it earns points in being a rare rose in a sea of flowers. It had been awhile since I played Banjo-Kazooie proper, so I thought I might have been a bit rusty picking this game up. Surprisingly though the game controls are smooth flowing and allow for quick corrections while platforming. The worlds themselves are pretty large. (somewhere between Tooie and Nuts n' Boltz size) but overtime you learn there layouts. A common complaint is that there empty, but I find that the speed of which you travel, and the moves you gain overtime make this a bit of a nitpick rather than a full on problem. The flaw comes with a ton of open space where you think there might be something, when there isn't (although it's mostly towards the edges of worlds). Each character is definitely memorable, though somewhat weirder than the norm. (I'm sure the Shopping Trollies in world 3 make sense to someone) It's hard to remember specifics and names when they have similar looks. (This doesn't mean anything, I'm just putting it here to see if you're actually reading this all) Hard to pick a favorite from them all when each has several lines that will at least get a smile out of you. The humor of the game is one thing that doesn't lose its touch and makes the transfer from Banjo unharmed. A combination witty British slang, 4th wall breaks, and jabs at modern gaming tropes, makes the whole script wrapped up nicely with a little charming bow. And on top of all that, we have the score of 2 music veterans of rare. Grant Kirkhope and David Wise. Both are on point with the music in this game, and after so long still have the magic touch. The only thing I think should be worked in is a bit more ambiance. (Those two are still legendary gods among music composers though)
So I've gone on long enough praising this game, it's only fair I bring up my criticisms for it. My biggest one is the move set. Each move is useful for traversing each world, but falls slightly in there uses. Most only have 1 or two obstacles that they apply to and not much else. And the amount of times they're used is not to often either. Another thing is the glowing outline around the contextual objects moves are used on. It kind of makes them stand out a bit, rather than making them blend into the environment. I find that its possible for objects to be obvious they need a move to be used on them, but not so much so that it's immediately clear which one it should be. My second biggest gripe is the enemy variety. In total there is 2 main enemies. One that gets a different skin each world, and a wasp like one. More enemies with different attacking patterns and different ways to defeat would do wonders. The bosses themselves are definitely humorous like previous games, but are lacking in much challenge. They all fall under the category of, dodge attacks then hit when vulnerable. That about wraps it up.
My final thoughts.
Overall, I had a lot of fun playing this game, and getting that old collectathon jumpstart. I can't leave it saying I think it's the most perfect thing in the world, but in my eyes it was worth the purchase. It's reasonable, even if you don't wanna go for 100%. Nothing is too challenging, and it was always enjoyable from start to finish. There's plenty of things this game doesn't have, but I had a blast with what was there. And with the spit n polish update coming later this year, there's definitely more reason to get it and play it. As a Returning Banjo fan, you'll feel right at home. And as a new fan, you'll learn to grow into it.
It might seem this game isn't as memorable as Banjo-Kazooie, but give it time, and it will sink in.
All in all, Solid game.
(And if by the power of all things collectable they're making a Sequel. I guarantee it will be all these great things and more.)
If you liked banjo kazooie you will enjoy playing this game... good ol' platformer fun! ..... worth it

I really love this game, the short game-length is about the only real issue for me. It is cheaper than most games, but still. There are only 5 worlds + the main hub, and it doesn't take long to get through the worlds and collect almost everything. Some puzzles can be a bit finicky, but that is the biggest challenge. Well, that and the final boss who is significantly harder than the rest of the game, and quite a long battle.
The game is easy overall, a bit too easy I think. The worlds are definitely small-ish too, I would have expected more. The worlds that do exist though, they are awesome visually and each has a unique theme to it, they are all very different from one another. My favorite is definitely world 4, as it feels like a game, within a game, and reminds us of just how silly these games were, with the only goal being fun. You won't get much story here past the most basic goal, but the dialogue is entertaining. Laylee will be the one that sticks, as she has the same cheeky personality Kazooie had.
In terms of platforming, it felt good. Camera angles were odd at times and about the main thing that could through you off and miss a landing. The controls were great though, but controlling the transformation in world 2 felt really frustrating. Combat is what you'd expect, these games were never about combat, rather collecting, adventuring, humor, and having fun. The bosses present somewhat of a challenging combat (you will probably die your first try figuring things out), but the minions on the maps were always meant to get in your way, not a challenge. This isn't a game meant for combat, if you play it for that, you are playing for the wrong reasons.
The last 2 major bits, music and collecting. The soundtrack and voices are perfect, they are all you could have hoped for and stay true to the past. The collecting is also fun, and there is no shortage of stuff, but many of the minigames are too simple. The quizzes also make a return of course, and the questions can be rough or super easy pending your luck.
I did not play multiplayer so no comment there.
Overall, I found this to be the perfect follow-up to Banjo-Kazooie and really miss those older games, they are so much better than most games these days. If you are a retro fan and wanted another Banjo-Kazooie, this is all you could hope for, minus how short it is. If you aren't familiar with such games, you probably won't appreciate many of the elements and touches as they are intentionally not modernized.
Hopefully more of these kind of games will come again (Devs, please do a larger game like DK64!).
Personal experience score: 9/10
Story: 6/10 - Not really much in the way of story beyond the obvious goal. The dialogue along the way is enjoyable though, lots of laughs and chat that you would expect from both Banjo and Kazooie.
Sound: 10/10 - The soundtrack is key and just perfect, the voicing as well. If you know Banjo-Kazooie games, this is exactly what you'd expect.
Graphics: 10/10 - Simply beautiful! Had to play 1 quality down from max, and every minute was a treat visually.
Controls: 6/10 - They are not ideal, mostly because of odd camera angles at parts, otherwise, they work just as you'd expect.
Game Length: 3/10 - This one was really disappointing. I expected 40 hours given some information about how it is supposed to be much larger, but it is 13 hours to cover most content and beat the game. Add +5 hours max to 100% it with collecting the remainders.

This game must have the worst leveling system EVER. You have a level, enemies have a level and a "threat level", missions have a level, but nothing makes sense.
At level 17 I did a level 14 main mission and almost got anihilated by the defense system of the prison I had to destroy.
At level 18 I tried doing the main mission which was level 16, and had to destroy a level "threat : impossible" battleship. Even with good and enhanced weapons I barely did any damage.
At level 19 I tried a level 17 assassination mission, just to get destroyed by 4 level 19 ships with "threat level : alarming". How is this a "level 17" mission ?
I tried hiring mercenaries but to no avail, they're just good at being destroyed instead of me.
People have complained about the leveling, the devs just said that each zone has its own level, and that a level 19 mission in a certain zone is not the same as a level 19 mission in another zone.
THEN WHY DON'T YOU INDICATE THE ZONE LEVEL IN THE GAME DAMNIT ?
They just link to a map with zone levels, outside of the game on their website, but this map doesn't exist anymore and the page says "404 not found".
It really just feels like the game has been abandoned at some point in development and they went and did Warlords instead, which is almost the same game, but even worse. On the forums they all act "we're the cool devs taking people's opinion into account" but in the end they just don't give a damn.
As an example, I found this license I could buy for 250K, allowing me to enter a certain zone with no fee. But I've never had to pay a fee before, so that was weird. I checked on the forums, found people reporting this "bug" and the answer was "yeah this feature is not implemented yet".
This was a post from 2014. Guess what ? The feature is still not in the game.
They're a small team in Croatia, I could forgive the bad voice acting, the badly written texts full of typos, the few bugs, the grinding. They did an awesome job with the design of the stations and ships, and space looks really good, it's not realistic and full of colors. I really wanted to explore the game and see all it has to offer.

Do you like playing Pool, but can't afford a real Pool table or can't find the space to fit one in your house? If so, then Pool Nation is a game you might enjoy.
Modes include free play (which lets you do whatever you want, recognizing no rules whatsoever), Eight Ball, and Nine Ball. The latter two are done in tournaments, where you face progressively more difficult opponents.
Each opponent has bonus criteria, which when met, net you more points but also some opponents have extra modes. These extra modes include bonus games (with varying rules) to earn new Pool cues, felt table skins, and ball designs. None of these really matter as far as the game itself is concerned, but it's nice to get something extra when you do better than average.
Sound and music are basic, although the music I found a little annoying. Take that with a grain of salt, as I often find music in games to be irritating. The sounds fit the game nicely, although they were nohing to write home about.
Graphics are amazing. I grew up in a house with a real Pool table and except for a few angles here and there, the table and balls all look incredibly realistic. You can also view the game from your character's POV or use a top-down view. I'd strongly recommend the latter.
The controls include mouse and keyboard or a controller. I used a wired Xbox 360 controller, as I found the analogue sticks to work better than relying on the digital input of the mouse or keyboard. Every once in a while it seemed like the game interpreted my stick movement as much weaker than I intended, but for the most part, it worked very well.
One thing that makes this game much, much easier than real Pool is the inclusion of guides. These guides show you where the ball will go when you hit it and adjust on the fly when you change anything about your shot. Some people might see this as cheating, so on higher difficutly levels the guides are reduced or removed entirely.
Multiplayer is available, although I have no idea how well it works. I've stuck entirely to single player against the AI. Considering the overall age of Pool Nation as well, there may not be many players left actively searching for games either.
I will warn potential buyers that Pool Nation's developer seems to have abandoned the game. If I'm wrong about that, I apologize. To be fair, Pool Nation is 100% done, so there really isn't much more to do other than fix a bug or two if/when they pop up.
Pool Nation is on sale a lot on Steam and through third-party stores, like Humble Bundle or Bundle Stars. so I'd suggest waiting for a sale to purchase it. That wait shouldn't be too long.
All in all, I'd recommend this game. It's entertaining, relaxing (for the most part), and doesn't require in-depth knowlege of sports or quick reaction times.

I bought Max Payne when it came out but I never finished it. However, I've recently played through the whole campaign after purchasing it once again on Steam and can say that it truly is a masterpiece. Although some of the character models look goofy by today's standards, the art direction of the campy comic book cutscenes and game itself hold up extremely well. Max Payne has some top notch level design, something that is missing from most modern games that seem like they're practically on rails, Some of my gripes were the platforming sections in the dream sequences and having to mess around to get it to work on Windows 8.1 properly. However, the platforming sections are brief and the work around didn't take too long. It plays surprisingly well with a gamepad, although you need a third party application for controller support. Also, I highly recommend the 16:9 mod and to enable VSR to downsample from a higher resolution to polish off those jaggies. All in all, Max Payne is a master class of third person action games with fun gamplay, a satisfying story, good voice acting and a rich noir atmosphere that demands your attention. It took me 10 hours to beat the game and I'm getting ready to hop into the sequel, Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne. If it's half as good as the first, I should be in for a treat.

There is a point in life where we look deep within our hearts and ponder on the finality of our very existence. Truly, there is no greater piece of fiction that analyses and depicts this than Garfield Kart. A deconstruction of the kart genre, Garfield Kart showcases with gripping sincerity, the internalised struggles of the kart racer through the title’s titular character, Garfield.
Garfield Kart is split into four main plot arcs known as cups, named Lasagna, Pizza, Hamburger, and Ice-Cream. Each individual cup in the game features four chapters known as courses where the plot unravels during the races.  The decision to accelerate and press onward is available, but the player can also make use of the reverse function in gameplay to reject the road ahead of them, or to undo mistakes when kart racing, at the cost of the precious time Garfield has left to live. Garfield Kart innovates in the use of the turning mechanic, in which players are not required to stick to the linear direction of Garfield, but can adjust their direction in accordance to their choices in life. When turning, karts can also employ the use of the complex drift mechanic, wherein a player commits to a turn they have taken in their path, which can either provide them with a boost of speed, or cause them to crash if their choice in life was poor. The boost mechanic from drifting is also employed in boost-pads and Lasagna, which can be used by the player to carve their own path in the race to break free from the pre-defined shackles and take their own path, saving time on the counter. Outside of Lasagna, items also include Pies, Springs, Diamonds, Pillows, Perfume, Wands, and UFOs, tools that serve as methods to channel the power of the individual kart racers against their opponents and impede their progress, both ahead of and behind the player.
Garfield and Jon Arbuckle are the playable characters during the main single-player story mode, however, different characters, such as Nermal, Arlene and Liz Wilson and different karts are also unlockable. Within the courses are puzzle pieces of Garfield’s lost broken memories to collect when racing, this side quest unlocks flashback scenes of Garfield’s past. The second side quest are time trial races, in which the player races against a UFO rather than a kart, a reflection of the inner darkness the player must attempt to outdo through their application of speed.
Garfield Kart’s greatest asset is the plot, with one particular scene truly reflecting the masterful writing of Garfield creator, Jim Davis. Garfield’s internal monologue of self-reflection prior to the rival race against the Lasagna corrupted Odie in Mally Market is perhaps the most poignant and well directed scene in videogame history. As Garfield questions if he races in his kart, or his kart races in him, he recalls the late Lyman’s words, “My old mentor Jim Davis told me once that, ‘Way down deep, we’re all motivated by the same urges. Cats have the courage to live by them.’ Remember that Garfield.”. Ultimately, this spurns Garfield to finally embrace Formula Zzzz and its power, despite the negative repercussions he will suffer as a result, as Garfield has accepted that he has to end Odie in order to save him. The tragic bond shared by Garfield and Odie is brought to its head within this scene, enhanced alongside the symbolism of Garfield finally accepting himself by becoming one with Formula Zzzz. The leitmotif that occurs throughout the game is used within the sad yet hopeful track “Ode to the Cat and Dog” within this scene, that creates a masterful atmosphere. Similarly, the endgame plot twist during the Ice-Cream Cup in Loopy Lagoon is shocking, yet perfectly foreshadowed. The ending of Garfield Kart is beautiful and bittersweet, a culmination of Garfield’s character arc, it must be seen to be believed, and shouldn’t be spoiled.
Garfield Kart, just like us all, is not perfect, it is still flawed. There is no local or online multiplayer present within the game, and the title lacks full controller support. Like real life, this is a journey we must take alone, as we attempt to control our movement despite the impairment of denied control and power.
Despite this, Garfield Kart is one of the most emotionally charged videogames I have ever experienced, intertwining gameplay and story to produce an outstanding work that is unparalleled to this day. Garfield Kart is a must-play title, I would recommend it.

This game is now one of my favourite games of all time. When I played it, I felt like a kid again, playing and exploring a completely new 3D Platformer that is not too easy, but not too hard at the same time.
Pros:
-Was made by ex-Rare employees who worked on classics like Banjo-Kazooie and Donkey Kong 64. (and the game definitively feels as good as those games)
- Has a ton of collectibles, and all of them has a use! (well, one of them doesn't until the update, but that's just a detail...)
- There may only be 5 worlds, but each one of them are extremly huge! (bigger than Banjo-Tooie's worlds, and they're pretty big worlds)
- The bosses are pretty cool and fun to fight (except for the 4th world's boss, but that's just because I hate Kartos...)
- The minigames are pretty fun to play (beating the high score is hard though...), and you can also play them with your friends!
Cons:
- Kartos's missions are the worst... They're extremly hard and annoying... I hate Kartos...
- The sudden camera changes are sometimes really disorienting and makes it a lot harder to play.
- There's no "Save" button, and the only way to save progress is either by collecting an important collectible (like a Pagie or an upgrage), or by going back to the entrance of the world and leaving, which is kinda annoying...
- Some transformations are only used for one mission, and that's a bit deceiving because the transformations are pretty cool...
Things I would recommand adding in an update or something like that:
- A mode that lets you refight the bosses (kinda like in DK64 and B-T)
- A "Save & Quit" button, or just a "Save" button in general.
- Fixing the camera problems.
- I'm actually surprised the Yooka-Laylee Rap is not actually in the game... Why's that?
If you like 3D Platformers like the ones in the N64-era, then you'll love this game! Oh and the game is also on PS4, Xbox One and (soon) Nintendo Switch, so you can buy it on consoles if you prefer consoles instead of PC...

Firstly since Black Ops 2 comes as 3 separate games on your Steam Games List when you buy it (Black Ops 2 - Campaign, Black Ops 2 Multiplayer & Black Ops 2 Zombies) i will be reviewing them all here split into thier own sections to make it easier to see which part of the game i will be reviewing.
The campaign to this game is really good in my opinion, i have thoroughly enjoyed pretty much every mission.  The story line is not too bad and links in with previous story lines from Treyarcs CoD games.  The graphics i run at maximun are not too bad either but there are parts of various missions in which there are most certainly texture issues or misplaced objects which you can see in my steam screenshots for this game.
The campaign is as with every other CoD just as explosive and violent with so much variety in the scenery or vehicles you can use etc.  One thing i do like in this campaign is being able to use an Access Kit during every mission, which allows access to various perks such as Drones, ASD's or CLAW's (Military Automated Units) and also things like Flak Jackets for reduced explosive damage and alternative Melee weapons.  Some parts are as with previous CoD's overly excessive with violence but it doesnt make the game any less fun in my opinion.
Also as with many previous CoD games there are Intel's to collect in each mission, however something i liked in this game is that there are two versions of Intel - One for missions based in the Past, and one version for the missions based in the Future. There are also Challenges for each mission which if completed allow access to more perks and more powerful weapons to use in the missions ahead or previous missions if you use the Replay Mission feature (after completing story).
The last feature i do like in this game was the ability to choose your weapons setup before starting a mission. You are able to choose both a primary and secondary weapon of your choosing with up to 3 attachments too.  Then you can also choose your grenades and perks too. Some grenades, weapons or perks are required to do the challenges in the game but sometimes those particular missions would also have the required weapon laying around nearby. Also challenges are not necessary to complete so its not super important if you dont take any particular weapon, grenade or perk.
- Achievements are also separate for each part of this game, the Achievements for the campaign part are all pretty straightforward, the most difficult being to complete every single challenge in every single mission including the StrikeForce missions.
The bad points i have picked up on having played this game are as follows:
-

For some unknown reason at some point in pretty much every single mission i had huge lag spikes where my FPS (Frames Per Second) would drop to like 2 FPS.  I have an absoloute beast of a computer and could run max graphics 100% of the time with no issues but these random lag spikes hit for like upto around 15 seconds where i can barely turn or anything because its going so slow.  Its not based on internet in this case as its purely singleplayer even if you disconnect internet and play its the same issue.  Fortunately this only happens about once on every map for no more than 15 seconds and may have not happened at all some times.  The only reason i say every mission is because i have played through each mission multiple times to get every challenge complete for the achievements.
-
This game has ALOT of cinematics, and they are very good and work well alongside the missions and quite often during the missions.  Therefore i have absoloutly no issue with the cinematics at all and this should not put the average player off at all.  However, if you are attempting to do EVERY SINGLE CHALLENGE in order to get EVERY SINGLE ACHIEVEMENT, you have to play through each mission multiple times and it takes a very long time watching the cinematics over and over again.  Some you can skip fairly quickly, sometimes you have to watch for like 30 seconds before it can be skipped and you can start the mission.  But the in-game cinematics 9 times out of 10 cant be skipped and takes forever to just continue with the mission to get your challenges or whatever.
Would be very nice to just have instantly skippable cinematics when using the Replay Mission feature after having completed the story at least once. Watching the same cinematic however many times it takes you to do some of the challenges is just not fun :P
-
The A.I. (Artificial Intelligence) units for this game are not too bad for the main campaign, you probably wont have a problem with them. However the A.I. in the StrikeForce Missions are absoloutly terrible and make them almost unplayable. I have completed all 5 StrikeForce missions in the Tactical View only for the Challenge required for the Achievement, and occasionally the A.I. just dont move ever, they get stuck and they stand until they die.  Having said that, the StrikeForce missions i have done in Tactical View were pretty straightforward and i did the challenge first time.
The mission 'Shpwrecked' even on Recruit difficulty seems to be impossible to do due to A.I. not doing anything at all, or dying almost instantly to enemy soldiers or ASD's. They don't attack enemies en route to waypoints, they just run straight past them, so they die.  You do seem to have to really work to get them to kill things and defend properly in this one mission.
I have completed this mission with very little difficulty having finally gotten around to it, at the time i completed it, i had quite a large force of soldiers, ASD's and a claw all fairly close to each other so they seemed to protect each other from dying so easily.  Once the Tactical View Challenge is done for all StrikeForce missions the rest of the challenges are a breeze.
One thing i will note to help others in completing challenges is that you do NOT need to successfully complete the mission so you can spend as long as you like 'running over soldiers with an ASD' for example until time runs out and you fail the mission if thats what it takes.

It could be fun. However a very clunky control scheme gets in the way. By that I mean the fact that to simply look around the ship, one has to press two keys to enter a "turret mode", then "targeting", and then the camera follows a target reticule, instead of a 1:1 mouse control. This is terrible in battles and travel alike.
In battles, the information on a hostile ship is tethered to its position in space. Therefore, to see any info like distance, health, danger, one must be looking at it. Without direct line of sight, all one gets is an arrow pointing to where it is. Trying to fly the ship, keep an eye on its vitals, whilst also trying to get a look at the enemy ship that is behind you is bloody tedious. I eneded up just not bothering, and stayed in the most intuative control mode, forcing me to simply circle around until the enemy came into view. This made the battle boring and devoid of tactics.
The game is beautiful and the ships look cool. One can even name their ship and have the name appear on the hull. There is also quite a bit of long distance travel to do. Combine those things and what happens? The player ends up wanting to look at the vistas and maybe get a nice cinematic view of the ship on a long and uneventful voyage. However, with this clunky camera it just doesn't happen. Firstly, because it simply sucks in the first place, being slow and restricted, with a million different modes and keys. Secondly, because once the destination is reached, one has to reverse all that crap and get into the proper control mode in order to be able to fight. Constant mode and targetting switching is just tedious and not worth the effort.
If they had just copied the controls of the countless 3rd person space games out there, at least the game would be playable. I could see myself playing it quite a bit. But when I can't even comfortably look at the freaking ship up close, from an angle I like whilst exploring then I just cannot reccomend or play it. In short, the ship is a chore to handle. I'm not saying the game is too hard, bwaaaah. I'm saying simple things take too many steps to perform and are badly implemented.
When a mod comes out to overhaul the camera, I will come back and recommend the game.

Starpoint Gemini 2 is a semi-free-roam Elite-like space game where you roam the local cluster of fighting, trading, bounty-claiming, and performing missions like mercenaries. With wide variety of ships from little gunboats all the way up to supercarriers, and a dozen factions to align with (and risk enraging other factions) as well as a lot of planets, stations, and more to visit, there are indeed a lot of variety to gameplay, but soon the game boggs down into the minutiae, which is when you start noticing the interface problems.
The story was typical: you're the son of a legendary captain and when you're sent to do a training mission, you came back only to find your father's ship blasted into space junk. You vowed to find out what happened, but with only a little gunboat at your disposal, it will be a lot of traveling, shooting, and upgrading before you can avenge your father, and deal with several crisis in the local cluster.
SPG2 managed to be a bit different by introducing boarding parties. You can recruit "marines" off stations, and you can use your transporters to board enemy ships (unless they have biometric shields that blocks transporters) and if you can send enough marines over you can capture the ship and tow it to station to be added to your fleet or stripped and sold off for a good windfall.
However, it is this strip and sell interface that becomes the problem. The interface only allow you to manage one ship at a time: yours. So in order to strip the other ship, you have to transfer your command to it, strip it, and transfer back. That is just tedious, esp. when the ship has several weapons.
In fact, the ships, despite the size differences, are not that different. Little gunboats have only 1 360 degree light weapon, while supercarriers and dreadnoughts have multiple front, rear, and side weapons, both light and heavy.  However, having more heavy weapons just means more reloads, not higher firing rates or bigger salvos. More light weapons, however, does result in larger salvos, albeit of the light weapons.
The light weapons comes in a couple archtypes, and within each archetype you have several models, each of which comes in different grades, from Mk I to Mk III (the best). The heavy weapons only comes in archtypes and models, not specific grades.
As you fight in the universe, you can come across blueprints that allow you build experimental components, including better weapons and other ship components.
Which brings us to cost. The ships and weapons in the game cost a LOT. A carrier can cost 35 million, and a top of the line plasma light turret can cost 2.5 million. A typical mission only pays about 50K or less. You pretty much have to supplement your income by capturing enemy ships when you can if you want to upgrade your ship in any way.  What's worse, the buy and sell prices are VASTLY different. A weapon that you buy for 2.5 million can only be sold back for less than 1/4 of that.  While some weapons can be captured (capture the enemy ship and strip off their weapons before selling off the ship) you will probably have to spend some money for the best.
There are a full list of ship components, like powerplant, engine, transporter, grappler (tractor beam), shields, and so on, but there are no alternate models you can buy unless you manage to build the alternate versions from accumulating enough blueprints, and those are quite rare. Instead, you have to buy 'enhancements', which are additional cost items that buffs the particular item in some way, like decrease reload time by 50%, or improve sensor radius by 15%, and so on. The more expensive the enhancement, the more buffs it can provide.
However, the interface is tiny on my 1080 p screen, even when down-res'ed somewhat to improve frame rate.
The actual combat sequence is rather meh, as the ship can be flown with mouse or keyboard, but otherwise, the game was as if it was designed to run with keyboard only,  Most of the commands were mapped to the keyboard, but one of the main functions was mapped to middle button toggling a context sensitive menu that does a LOT of things. You can almost play this as a shooter: just drive your ship around, lock on the the enemy ships, and let AI do most of the work (the turrets can handle themselves, you just steer)
You can carry up to 3 squadrons of fighters, and hire up to two mercenaries to accompany you as guards, of whatever size and level available at the station. I've hired dreadnought as escort before.
There are indeed a lot of things to do in SPG2. Capturing ships, salvaging derelicts, mine asteroids, smuggle things onto planet, run blockades with contraband, perform contracts, do side missions or primary story missions, the choice is yours.  The problem is they are all options... The actual mechanics of this game is random combat, where you fly from one place to another shoot down all hostiles (or run away), then repeat until level up, which enables more weapons, shields, etc... You get the idea.  But when all things are tried, the only sure way of making money is via combat, and capture of hostile ships and tow them back to station for the prize money.
The voice acting feels over the top and almost ridiculous, and the plot line barely comprehensible (only picks up later).
All in all, this is a "barely" recommend. I find Darkstar One more enjoyable, IMHO.

When I was 18... 18 years old, I saw for the first time in my life... I saw an image of clarity. I saw a comic strip... a three panel comic strip that, though simple as it seemed, changed me... changed my being, changed who I am... Made me who I am...
Enlightened me...
The strip, Garfield, the comic strip was new... no more than maybe a month and a half since inception, since... since coming into existence... and there it was before me in print, I saw it... a comic strip... What was it called?
Garfield.
The story here is of a man, a plain man. He is Jon, but he is more than that... I will get to this later, but first let us say that he's Jon, a plain man.
And then there is a cat... Garfield.
This is the nature of the world, here. When I see the world, the politics, the future, the... the satellites in space, and... the people who put them there...
You can look at everything as a man and a cat... two beings, in harmony and at war...
So, this strip I saw; this man, Jon, and the cat, Garfield, you see...
Yes... hmm...
It is about everything. This... little comic is, oh, lo and behold... not so little anymore.
So yes, when I was 18, I saw this comic... and it hit me all at once, its power. I clipped it, and every day, I looked at it, and I said "Okay... let me look at this here. What is this doing to me? Why is this so powerful?"
Jon Arbuckle, he sits here, legs crossed... comfortable in his home, and he reads his newspaper... The news of the world, perhaps... and then he extends his fingers lightly, delicately... he taps his fingers on an end table, and he feels for something...
What is it? It is something he needs, but it is not there.
And then he looks up, slightly cockeyed, and he thinks... His newspaper's in his lap now, and he thinks this...
Now where could my pipe be?
This... I always come to this, because I was a young man... I'm older now, and I still don't have the secrets, the answers, so this question still rings true, Jon looks up and he thinks...
Now where could my pipe be?
And then it happens... You see it, you see... it's almost like divine intervention, suddenly it is there, and it overpowers you...
A cat is smoking a pipe.
It is the man's pipe, it's Jon's pipe, but the cat... this cat, Garfield, is smoking the pipe... and from afar, and someplace near, but not clear... near but not clear... The man calls out... Jon calls out, he is shocked. "Garfield!" he shouts.
Garfield. The cat's name.
But, let's take a step back... let us examine this from all sides, all perspectives... and when I first came across this comic strip, I was at my father's house... a newspaper had arrived, and I picked it up for him, and brought it inside.
I organized its sections for him and then, yes, the comic strip section fell out from somewhere in the middle, and landed on the kitchen floor... I picked up the paper pages and saw, up somewhere near the top of this strip... just like Jon, I was wearing an aquamarine shirt.
So I thought, "Ah, interesting. I'll have to see this later." I snipped out the little comic, and held on to it... and five days later, I reexamined it... and it gripped me, I needed to find out more about this. The information I had was minimal, but enough...
An orange cat named Garfield...
Okay, that seemed to be the lynchpin of this whole operation, yes. Another clue... a signature in the bottom right corner, a man's name...
Jim Davis.
Yes, I'm on to it for sure.
So... one: Garfield, orange cat, and two: Jim Davis, the creator of this cat...
And that curiously plain man.
I did not know, at the time, that his name was Jon. This strip, you see, had no mention of this man's name, and I'd never seen it before.
But I had these clues; Jim Davis, Garfield.
And then I saw more, I spotted the tiny copyright mark in the upper left corner. Copyright 1978 to... what is this? Copyright belongs to a... PAWS Incorporated...
I used the local library and mail services to track down the information I was looking for...
Jim Davis, a cartoonist, had created a comic strip about a cat, Garfield... and a man, Jon Arbuckle. Well, from that point on, I made sure I read the Garfield comic strips, though as I read each one, as each day passed... the strips seemed to resonate with me less and less...
I sent letters to PAWS Incorporated, long letters, pages upon pages... asking if Mister Jim Davis could somehow publish just the one comic, over and over again... "It would be meditative," I wrote, "the strength of that."
Could you imagine?
But... no response... The strips lost their power, and eventually I stopped reading, but... I did not want my perceptions diluted, so I vowed to read the pipe strip over and over again... That is what I call it, "The Pipe Strip."
The Pipe Strip.
Everything about it is perfect. I can only describe it as a miracle creation, something came together... the elements aligned... It is like the comets, the cosmic orchestra that is up there over your head... The immense, enormous void is working all for one thing, to tell you one thing...
Gas and rock, and purity, and nothing.
I will say this... When I see the pipe strip... and I mean every single time I look at the lines, the colors, the shapes that make up the three panel comic...
I see perfection.
Do I find perfection in many things?
Some things, I would say... Some things are perfect... and this is one of them. I can look at the little tuft of hair on Jon Arbuckle's head... it is the perfect shade... The purple pipe in Garfield's mouth...
How could a mere mortal even MAKE this?
I have a theory, about Jim Davis...
After copious research and, yes, of course, now we have the internet, and this information is all readily available, but...
Jim Davis, he used his life experiences to influence his comic...
Like I mentioned before, none of them seem to have the weight of the pipe strip... But you have to wonder about the man who is able to even, just once, create the perfect form, a literally flawless execution of art, brilliance! Just as in a ward... I think there is a spiritual element at work...
I've seen my share of bad times and... when you have something... Well, it's just... emotions, and neurons in your brain, but... something tells you that it's the truth...
Truth's radiant light.
Garfield, the cat? Neurons in my brain, it's... it's harmony, you see? It... Jon and Garfield, it's truly harmony, like a... continuous, looping, everlasting harmony... The lavender chair, the brown end table, the salmon-colored wall, the fore's green carpeting, Garfield is hunched, perched... perhaps with the pipe stuck firmly between his jowls... His tail curls around. It's more than shapes too, because... I...
Okay, stay with me... I've done this experiment several times.
You take the strip. You trace only the basic elements. You can do anything, you can simplify the shapes down to just... blobs, just outlines, but it still makes sense...
You can replace the blobs with magazine cutouts of other things, replace Jon Arbuckle with a... car parked in a driveway sideways, cut that out of a magazine, stick it in... Replace him there in the second panel with a... a food processor... Okay, and then we put a picture of the planet in the third panel over Garfield...
It still works.
These are universal proportions. I don't know... how best to explain why it works, I've studied the pipe strip, and analyzed Jon and Garfield's proportions against several universal mathematical constants.
E, Pi, the Golden Ratio, the Feigenbaum Constants, and so on... and it's surprising... scary even, how things align. You can take just... tiny pieces of the pipe strip, for instance, take Jon's elbow from the second panel... and take that, and project it back over Jon's entire shape in the second panel, and you'll see a near perfect Fibonacci sequence emerge...

To put it plainly: this really isn't as good as a game as it's hyped up to be.
I'm not going to say I'm one of the more dedicated fans of this game, nor will I claim that I followed the game before this year. I'm one of the people who have spent time and effort into this game, hell I don't even have more than 100 hours put in and tha time was alloted just because I simply server hopped and idled a lot. But I can clearly see what many of the much more dug in players are saying without a doubt.
For starters: the dumbed down gunplay is 5 times worse than any other game I've ever played. Most of the time during gunplay I geniunely wouldn't even be aiming at the person, rather I would be aiming in their general direction but I would still end up killing them. Aiming itself is more or less just so you can find some sort of satisfaction with shooting. Bullets will just eventually go in random directions regardless of how long you spray down or tap. I could be aiming at a still target, never moving my mouse an inch and begin to fire off the B.A.R (Bolt Action Rifle) in small intrevals and still somehow see the bullets take different paths every 2 shots.
Next is the game progress: when I first began playing I was amazed to see that I was able to go from naked to already owning assault rifles and having a full sheet metal base playing solo. I assumed this was due to the fact I was on a lowly populated server and simply was being smiled upon by a higher power. But as I server hopped between multiple vanilla servers and went on playing, I saw that as long as the groups I join up with weren't raided or killed in the midst of farming and building that I would end up near end game status within 1-2 hours minimum. This seems like a long time but I assure you that is not the case as I've heard from much more experienced players it used to take longer. Once you hit that end game status you honestly have three choices: spend your time helping/recruiting others to work with you, begin raiding others solely for some sort of entertainment, or kill off random people. Another thing on raiding is that it's extremely easy to raid most people even without explosives and they don't even have to be online in order for you to do so. Hence why you see the term "offline raiding" come up a lot as it is seen as a problem in the community and tends to get you hazed for doing it.
While I'm on the the playerbase and its state; this game's community is
toxic. Even servers that say "Don't be toxic" simply mean don't sit there and spam in chat or go off looking for arguments (which still happens every second). People justify killing freshspawns every chance they get with the "It's a survival game and therefore you're idiotic for getting mad about it". I won't deny this is a survival game and sometimes the fittest will have to excert their strength in order to stay on top, but simply killing off people you can clearly tell don't have anything or you see spawn is just shooing off any new players who wish to get involved in the game; or seriously ticking off anyone trying to start up. Not to mention you'll get griefers who block off your doors and make it impossible to leave your base, people who seem to devote their time making monkey sounds into their mics whenever they down you or vice versa, or you'll come across people who's sole joy in life is to roof camp and make it impossible for anyone who gets close to pass by. To put it simply: this game's community is nowhere near welcoming to new players and you can easily see that reflected in the way the playerbase conducts itself all over steam.
My last pet peeve is the fact of how in the game's current state it's way too simple. After roughly 10 hours of playing and looking up some basic tutorials on YouTube, people would become surprised when I told them I had less than 100 hours in the game. This by itself is what can make the game very easy to pick up, but this also means that by the time you really get a feel for the game you end up with not a whole lot to learn. Building is tedious, combat is a joke, and surviving is really just eating food every once and awhile and making resources to keep furnaces and lanterns lit. And the events that do pose a threat get really boring and annoying after awhile just because of the fact that unless you're working with a large clan or a high populated server, you can benefit off of taking down the helicopter once or twice and catching one or two air drops. Obvious it's in early access which means the game will still make progress, but at the same time it's also been in early access for almost 4 years now. Of course this doesn't actually have any affect on how the game currently is but is just an observation as they can easily just drop it at any point or can just simply ignore making true progress and additions. That's what a few recent survival games have gone through.
To wrap this up simply: the game is fun for a short period of time, but you'll quickly grow tired of it. The learning curve is just way too simple despite what others are saying. The game can be fun if you know how to make it. For example, I've joined servers that award players with five times the amount of resources than you'd normally get and there are already modded gamemodes and edited rules and setups for others like having no guns available, your body doesn't appear as sleeping when you log off so you can't be looted, or you start off with guns and materials. Those servers are what can make this game a whole lot more intresting as they can put emphasis on certain aspects of the game that most people don't even focus on. But if you play solely of vanilla servers you can still enjoy it somewhat as people will create whole towns and shops, create local cultures and traditions, and even will make bounty hunter groups dedicated to only killing known bandits. Of course sadly, this isn't the case on most servers as you'll just get prepubescent children who technically have no business playing the game in the first place calling you the n-word killing you over and over and covering their base in Swastikas and male appendages until they get raided and quit playing forever.
If the current state of the game changes, then so will be my opinion as time can change anything but at the moment I honestly see it as just another overhyped, underdeveloped survival game to hit the market and for all we know could just fade away with the next year or so when something new comes out.

Buggy as heck and ultimately ruined my game experience.
While the atmosphere very much reminds me of X3/Freelancer/Privateer 2: The Darkening with a few rpg twists, much of the solar system is essentially empty. There are no unique discoveries of anomolies, enemies, stations that make you think "wow", just a slight rise in attention as you make note what can be bought where, that Spire has all the licenses for lawful people, and that a particularly useful officer or high level mercenary is there.
The controls and camera drive me crazy. You have to press tab to switch between camera modes, then space switches between controlling that camera mode and cursor mode. What happened to freelancer's easy one-two combo controls that seemlessly went from steering and shooting to cursor? The tutorial is very basic and doesn't explain many of the stats between power, batteries, launch delay, and on and on.
Combat is fairly lackluster. You could possibly dogfight and limit yourself to one camera mode that handicaps yours offensive capabilities. But most people will find it more efficient to just set autofire on and focus on having to use your heavy weapons. That mechanic in itself bugs me. You have light weapons with infinite ammo (railguns with no ammo?) and heavy weapons that have limites ammo, but in order to manually control all of them and focus one target you need three hands or waste your time changing the control scheme (the autofire makes no promises on what it will fire at).
What really ruined it for me was the barely mentioned bugs. Achievements are bugged, autopilot is bugged (flying in circles arround a planet), even combat is bugged with heavy weapons occasionally going through enemies. What really ruined it for me and made me stop wasting my time was a long trip collecting artifacts: I see a destroyer I wan't to capture and board while in a radiation field. I start traveling closer and am about 1800 m away when I see the radiation start eating my hull down to 3400/4000. No problem I think and pop a nanite repair for 25% hull. Suddenly my ship desides to instantly destruct without even the explosions that accompany the normal death. Nothing even near me, no planets, stations, anomolies. NOTHING, except that destroyer that was still 1800 m away.
This game feels like it wanted to capture the souls of all the games I formerly mentioned: Freelancer, X3, and Privateer. But it just feels like a horrible mix, like some kid decided since certain foods taste good, mix em together and they'd be even better. Many unimplemented features that still have notes and words in some of the menus (officers will always be apprentices) makes the game feel imcomplete. Mix that with the uninspired and monotone series of fly there, do rescue quest #478 then go to side mission #23 that feels exactly the same, then go do campign mission #whatever that STILL feels exactly the same and the game isn't fun. There is no climax, no differentiation, nothing to make me feel that my time was worth it.

First picture everything about Freelancer, then make it slightly worse in every aspect. Voila! You now have Starpoint Gemini 2!

I was a Kickstarter backer of Yooka-Laylee from the very beginning, having a huge amount of respect for the developers at Playtonic and their platforming legacy so I may be writing this review through some amount of nostalgia goggles.
Yooka-Laylee is overall exactly what was promised through their Kickstarter campaign and I'm glad I backed it. That being said there's some annoying parts to the game. Specifically some minigames that use questionable ball physics (such as golfing, ball navigating through pegs minigame, etc) that really are not fun and don't add anything to the game. There's also a few instances where the game has questionable floating controls especially with one of the later abilities where Laylee the bat can fly through the air and it's hard to control where she is going.
The platforming overall is very good, but I keep finding myself playing certain challenges that make me want to abandon the game due to frustration due to spotty controls and off physics. However, I would recommend this game to someone who enjoyed Banjo-Kazooie with the caveat that this game does not have as self-contained worlds and you need to find the good parts of the game yourself and ignore challenges which are an exercise in frustration.

**POTENTIAL SPOILER WARNING**
Just covering my bases.
Anyway, Yooka-Laylee recieved a lot of hype for nostalgic purposes. Which I won't deny be affected by. Made by Ex-Rare employees, but I feel this is common knowledge honestly. Its probably how or why you found out about the game to start with had you hopped on the kickstarter.
Yooka-Laylee attempts to reinvoke how platformers were on the N64, and to a degree is succeeded. But with anything it does have flaws, some worse than others.
I finished and 100%'d the game the other day, so I feel like I can give a truely informed opinion.
PROS:
*Genuinely Fun
I won't lie, I genuinely enjoyed most of my time with Yooka-Laylee. I enjoyed collecting things and collectathons in the past, so scoring a 100% for a world was really satisfying. Although sometimes it was just satisfying to know I was done with a world, but I'll go into that later.
*Capital B
I know a lot of folks seem to dislike him, but I really enjoyed his character. He was a ruthless but comical villain, and taunted you in ways similar to Gruntilda, except with business related insults. His design wasn't overly complicated, and I feel like his boss fight gave the game bonus points at the end ( which it really needed ).
*The Playtonics
Now a lot of people said these broke the game, I honestly didn't feel this. The one major tonic I used during the game was the one to help find secrets since some were either -very- cleverly hidden, or in some pretty asinine spots. Luckily not so much the latter. But while using them I never felt overpowered or like the experience suffered because of them. That bgeing said I wish the secret one didn't feel like it was as necessary as it came off to be.
*The Music
**Hivory Towers and Capital Cashino specifically**
The themes for these areas felt the most fitting. While the music overall was nice these two stood out. A lot of things I've read had people really hating on these areas, which I can understand, but to me they were the most well put together thematically. We'll go into -structurally- later.
*The Ghost Writers
It may be odd to go into a specific collectable, but I think they were done well. Similar to Jinjos, you have to collect 5 for a pagie. Unlike Jinjos though, you have to go about different means to collect each one, whether it be beating them up for feeding them etc. The audio cues, and the ability to figure out on your own how to go about each one on your own made them all the more satisfying.
Very specific pros yeah? Well, now its time for the nitty gritty, and its a bit more broad.
===================================
CONS:
*Level Design/Layout
Now before anyone gets the wrong idea, I generally did not find these levels to be empty. I always foudn sopmething to do *while there were collectables*. After that, the layout of said items turned most areas into a slog after a while. As someone who enjoys 100%ing these kinds of games, this turned and adventure into a chore after a while. Which is a shame, because some things were very clever. A lot though was also nonsense. Most also suffer from having too much clutter/scenery in a small area, and then large open areas of nothing. Moodymaze Marsh being the biggest offender of this. As a side separate note, Hivory Towers -did- suffer from being too large though. Traversing it even with the shortcuts felt like a slog, and the layout felt hard to navigate at times.
*Characters
Now I'm not talking about Yooka or Laylee, they were fine by me. Not good, not bad, very middle of the road. I mean moreso the NPCs and enemies. So many of the same NPCs appear over and over again, it just feels lazy and uninspired. Why do I have to keep encountering the pig knights or Kartos. The repetition just felt like they were generic NPCs after a while, versus inhabitants of those worlds. The enemies too, either get reused or are literally the same enemies with different models. They're not varied, it feels more like Corplets are just wearing thematically correct costumes for each world. Some normals enemies also take FAR too many hits. This is only a complaint because fighting enemies CAN be fun in a platformer, so I expected no less from Yooka-Laylee.
*Bosses
Same with the enemies, they just felt uninspired and boring.
-Rampo there was no oomph to it, music or attack wise.
-Brrreeze Blok is hard to describe, he just felt like he was there. Again too, no really boss impact.
-Trev the Tenteyecle had a really fun personality: a cockney swamp monster of whom we interrupted his watching of soap operas. Better boss than the others, but the way the phases were put together, it just lost any sense of dynamic it could have had.
-I.N.E.P.T. was probably the worst boss in the game. Now for clarity, he is more of a pattern boss versus one you openly attack. The killer is that with no healthbars on any of these bosses, it makes just planning out your actions a bit awkward. This boss as well, if you die, you start all the way back at phase 1 on this 3-4 phase fight. Under most circumstances this si fine, but this is a LONG fight and the pattern and objective just keeps changing enough where you might die a few times. Best world in the game got the worst boss.
-Planette has nothing that really stands out. She's just middle of the road nothing special.
-Capital B. is probably the best boss in the game, but that's not saying much. He also suffers from it not really having the oomph when you hit him or he loses health. His fight also just isn't very climatic as it should be. There's no satisfaction in beating him. Its just "oh, well that's done". Which is a shame because he's otherwise an absolutely wonderful character.
*The Music
***With the exception of Hivory Towers and Capital Cashino***
With how long it took to get all the cleectables in some of thes eareas, the music either droned on your was just otherwise unmemorable, which is a shame. There will be times where you might be missing only 1 quill, and in levels this large, it might take a long time to find. This might lead to hours potentially of the same track looping and with how either unfitting or just inunteresting they are, this makes what could still be an enjoyable scavenger hunt into a monotonous chore.
*Controls
***Specifically flying and using Yooka as a ball***
These two specific actions just felt very jenky, to the point trying to be precise ( like to collect butterflies to restore your power meter or a pagie ) became very annoying. Other than that, game controlled fine. I also had no issues with the camera.
*Jokes/dialogue
There was simply too much fourth-wall breaking. Its fine in doses, but the joke was getting grinded into the ground by the first quarter of the game. Pagies also felt like they talked way too much, and their jokes often felt forced. More clever and tongue-in-cheek dialogue would have been appreciated and benefitted the game more.
*Moves
I do not recall the game ever even giving hints about what you can do with some of these moves. The main one being that you can basically turn your body into a prism while invisible to refract lasers. I found this out completely through desperation.  This happened several times over.
=====================================
NIT-PICK ( this should not influence your purchase, this is just a personal grievance )
*Pagies in Cagies
Why are pages of a book locked in cages? Its not a logic argument here it just, it feels boring. Jiggies used to explode out of the ground, plunged out of a toilet, or get coughed out by a whole manner of things. In this game its just: Page in cage, solve puzzle, cage open, get page. I mean yes it rhymes but, there's no charm in it at all.
Overall, the game is fun, but feels unpolished. It lacks in a lot of subtle areas, but they add up.
I would wait for this game to go on sale before buying.
For what it is, its enjoyable. But I wouldn't pay more than $30 for it.

Ancient Space tries very hard to appeal to Homeworld fans, and i'd say it does a decently successful job. Instead of comparing this title to the 1st Homeworld, a better comparison would be Cataclysm or Homeworld 2 due to very strict unit caps.
This might seem like a horrible thing, but it actually is a saving grace for this game. Each and every single ship so far has some sort of special ability (sometimes two) which can be triggered at specific times for great effect. The more ships you add from the current values when having this variety in individual ships creates a micromanagement hell. It strikes an excellent balance between fleet size and interactivity of each type of ship.
This game has its problems for sure, but if you're looking for that Homeworld kick, you will find it here. Just don't expect it to come close to the gem that is its source material.

Possibly the best space RTS released in years. I enjoyed the diversity of units, the missions felt at the right pace and were varied enough to stay interesting. The unit types seemed well thought out and provide a variety of different ways of completing missions. Perhaps one of my favourite things is that the steam achievement system was put to good use, most achievements were rewarded for completing missions in a different way which made you play differently instead of always spamming the same ships.
My only potential gripe with the game is that the first mission is undoubtedly the hardest and then the difficulty curve drops rapidly. Other than that this was a game that kept me playing and I think I will play the campaign again on the hardest difficulty.

Finished the campaign on normal.
: Ancient Space feels somewhat like a single player party based MOBA game as oftentimes you'll be facing down waves of enemies with a relatively small number of ships. There are even structures on the map that spawn hostile "creeps". You need to use your ships' abilities and strengths to overcome the enemies' numerical superiority. Base building is minimalistic and reminiscent of tower defense games since you capture "building nodes" that allow you to construct turrets and support structures which can assist you in defeating enemy attacks. Missions consist of search & destroy, survival, protecting convoys and other objectives with a bit of stealth thrown in. You can scan anomalies to gain various bonuses and resources some of which can be used in between missions to upgrade your fleet and "hero" carrier.
Your carrier can alternate between a defensive and offensive variant which has to be chosen before mission starts. One small problem here is that the offensive carrier seems to be much better and even the missions' structure seems to favor it. After I unlocked the offensive variant I never went back to the other one. In addition you can bring three officers on every mission with each having their own activated global ability with capped, per-mission, uses. Some missions favor certain officers. Combat can be paused (unless using hardcore mode) which gives you time to consider your options and issue orders. Controls can be a bit hard to get used to but ultimately I simply zoomed out a bit, used wasd to move about and played it as more of a traditional 2D isometric or bird's eye view RTS despite the game being fully 3D. AS does feature a vertical axis and you can move your ships "up" or "down" but verticality is underutilized and there is little reason to engage with it.
: Visually, the best part of AS are the maps. Taking a fairly unique approach to its space-scape maps in AS often feature large rock formations or structures often giving them an enclosed or "indoor" feel which defies expectations one would have of a space game. Other than the interesting visual effect the only point of these obstacles is to serve as choke points or funnels. Ships have a very utilitarian, down to Earth appearance which some might find bland or boring though I'm personally happy with it. However the ships look pretty blurry and don't have much detail to them so don't expect a Homeworld-esque visual experience when it comes to observing battles. Due to the nature of the game you'll almost always be zoomed out taking a more strategic view of things so it doesn't matter much.
: Everything in this game has a subdued tone. There are no over the top emotional moments, no romance, no quirky comic relieft, no saving the human race or defeting some great ancient evil. Characters are professional, even under duress, and focused on their task which is also reflected in their voice acting. Again, some might find this boring but it's a refreshing change I think. The story gets a fair amount of exposition and a conclusion but also retains some mistery. Imagine if the first Alien or Predator movies never got a sequel. Music takes cues from Homeworld with some classical and middle eastern sounding tracks and can make for a compelling listen.
: While I do recommend Ancient Space I don't think it's a superlative game by any stretch of the imagination. Much could be said about how this game could be better like more variety in carrier upgrades/abilities, less linear, script driven mission structure, more satisfying ship/weapon visuals/effects, more playable factions, etc. but much of that is offset by its low price and Ancient Space, such as it is, is a full working package. Best way to approach it is to not base your expectations on Homeworld (even though AS does try to tug at that particular nostalgia) but go in with a blank slate and take it as it is. I would sooner compare it to the old Conquest: Frontier Wars in terms of gameplay (albeit more streamlined). AS's maps are even separated into sectors connected by wormholes which is something we could see in Conquest. If you're a fan of sci-fi and RTS, Ancient Space makes for a pretty good, and affordable, space adventure.

One of my all time favourite 4x4 real time strategy games is 'Sins of a Solar Empire' but sadly it was lacking a single player story.
Ancient Space is that and more. You take command of a fleet embarking on a scientific mission to chart undiscovered reaches of space and must overcome overwhelming odds. This game will keep you on your toes, and I found it to be frantic and fun!

The endless foe transforms every mission into a marathon effort just to protect a convoy or rescue some crew members, spiraling out of control into a dull, repetitive slog of a game, oozing wasted potential and a shoddy excuse for a story. You want to like Ancient Space, but it makes it terribly hard to do so.

100/10 Definitely one of my favorite games I've played. It's so well made, and as a gay trans boy, it's VERY nice to see an LGBT thing that isn't about coming out (and none of it feels forced, which makes this game even better). It has so many options for you as a player (like whether you were married to a man or a woman before, and whether you adopted/gave birth to Amanda, for example!) and so many different types of characters, all of which are pretty casual (in a good way) and very well done!! To me, all of the characters feel so developed and detailed like in any other game, despite this one being a dating sim. You can tell that everyone that worked on the game worked very hard and it turned out amazing!
As for the gameplay itself, I love it. It doesn't take too long to finish a game (1.5-2 hrs for me on my first game, but I messed up Robert's dates so thats probably why) but there are so many more ways to do things aside from choosing who you end up with, and theres like an actual story line. On your first playthrough you think, 'hey that wasn't so bad' but by your third, your thinking to yourself, 'why do I need a tutorial to complete a dating simulator, its a /dating simulator/??' and its an amazing feeling.
Also, the dad puns are great. I love them.

I felt like the scene in the beginning where you have all the dads in one location was the best one because all of them were together interacting with one another. I felt like while you did know about each dad in a sense, there could have been a lot more done to get to know them even better. The dates themselves seemed very lackluster in many of the different routes that you went to and to complete an entire dating route took little to no time at all.
While I did enjoy some of the mini-games that were added to the game, some of them seemed like they were either added last minute or didn't have someone properly try them out. The golf mini game, for instance, was one that I could absolutely see where it was going, but was difficult in some respects and especially since there wasn't a visible time limit. While I was able to get around half of the holes-in-one, many of my friends weren't able to get one. The design for that mini-game as well seemed very lack-lustered considering the vibrant theme that the game was implying for the area.
In terms of design, the character arts were all very lovely, if you were looking at the NPCs. The classing between your own dadsona and the characters was offputting at times and though the backgrounds for many of the areas looked cute, it could also be rather odd compared to the NPC. Not only that, but in some instances the backgrounds didn't change to reflect the time of day that you were in (I.E. Bayside at night, when it was clearly still the daytime)
The voices were rather glitchy at times and off putting, while some voices were fine at a certain volume, others would be too quiet or too loud. The quality of the voice lines were odd as well, in terms of how well they sounded more than anything. As well as that, it would have been nice to have had a sound slider within the game instead of just an option of turning streamer mode on and off. That way if someone wants to not listen to the voices , they have that option or if they prefer the music to be higher or lower that is an option as well. Yes I know that computers have a volume slider, but it would have been nice to be able to do that in game instead.
With the option of a gallery I thought it would have many of the same things as most dating sims or visual novels have, where there are multiple CG that you find in game either by saying something or doing something correctly to a character that you hope to date you. That isn't to say that I do not enjoy the art that we have, no they were all nice and I applaud the artists who took time into making them. Instead this is my wondering why there wasn't more that could have been added. Maybe at a later time they would allow for certain CG to be added, I know there were endings or certain events that I would have loved to have seen as a CG.
Edit: I realized while I was away one thing that bothered me the most was the save function. Rather than allow us to have our own save files that we can rename and pick where to save, we would have so many save files (If you saved constantly like I did) and it would take finding the one that you needed to be a bit more difficult than if we were allowed to simply have our own save files that we named whatever and our own save slots that we could pick from.
