Video version of this review:
Yooka-Laylee is a spiritual successor to the Banjo-Kazooie series. Playtonic was formed by a bunch of former Rareware employees, who decided to bring back the good old fashioned platforming style that Rareware used to make. I was really excited for this. So let’s see if this game lives up to our expectations.
From the start, our villain, Capital B, steals books from all over the world. But the book you have is special and Capital B wants it to rule the world, because that’s villains for ya. But the pages of the book fly out and scatter all over the place, and you have to find them. They’re actually called “Pagies”. Ain’t that cute?
You have to purchase your abilities from this snake dude named Trowzer. You buy your abilities with quills. Although in the hub world, you get some abilities for free. Being a collectathon, of course, you will have more things to collect than just quills. You need certain amounts of pages to unlock or expand different worlds. You also grab butterflies to refill your health and power bar.
Also, the soundtrack is composed by David Wise and Grant Kirkhope. Could you ask for a better combination than that for this particular game’s music?
There have been a lot of criticisms based around the camera, and I can certainly see why. This camera does like to get stuck every once in awhile, and also sometimes appears in different spots on its own when I’m standing against the wall and moving the camera. Some jumps are hard to make because I can’t line up the camera correctly.
The controls can be kinda troublesome too. When you release the button to stop walking, there’s a bit of a delay before you actually stop, and I’ve found myself stepping off the edge of platforms because of that. Jumping onto small platforms are a huge pain. I thought at first it was because of the keyboard controls. But then again, I played Psychonauts on PC. The platforming works perfectly fine with that game. I guess the game is to blame in this case.
I’ve only played two of the arcade games and they both suck. The racing one has the worst controls. You have to push the different buttons to move your car, but you can’t seem to use two buttons at the same time. So it’s really hard to dodge obstacles while moving forward at the same time. The flag-capturing one lasts way too long. You have to hold onto a flag as long as possible without getting hit by enemies. But sometimes, when I want to attack, I don’t, or I just won’t hit them, even though it looks like I should be close enough. But either way, I can never survive long enough to actually win.
The loading screens seem to take forever. Seriously, I don’t think I’ve ever played a game that takes so long to load.
When you play this on PC, they don’t seem to show the PC controls when it gives you a selection of choices. Why didn’t they change that? They show the keyboard controls in the characters’ dialogue, but every other time, they just show Xbox controls. I don’t even know what key on my keyboard is the equivalent of the Xbox’s “B” button. After I’m done buying my abilities I push “Esc”. While that does pause the game, at least it gets me out of the store menu, and so far, it seems to be the only way to do it.
The first level has some small crevices where it’s harder to get a good view of where I’m going, because the walls bring the camera too close to me.
You have to solve puzzles to get some of the pages. Some are easy, and some are more challenging. But some are next to impossible to get because of my constant battles with the controls and camera.
I wanted to talk about the second world, but there was a "problem posting this review". I figured it was probably a character limit, so I shortened it. So everything I said about the second world is in the video above.
Now if I could only get out of this “Yes, No” selection screen. Why can’t I get out of that? When Rextro asked me if I wanted to play his arcade game, I pressed Esc, and it got me out of there, but it won’t work for this. I’m pressing every key on my keyboard, but not a single key equals the B button for Xbox. The only way I can get out of this is returning to the hubworld. The PC version needs to be fixed, really badly. Fine, I’ll go to the hubworld, because screw it.
For the first couple of hours of this game, I kept on talking about how I loved it. But I never thought I’d get so frustrated that I’d end up wanting to quit the game. Probably the first time I did that in a 3D platform game. This was not worth $45. So for the last time, screw it.

With my nostalgia goggles on, this game is absolutely amazing. I love it. The music, the characters, the gameplay, the doofy dialogue. It's great.
But if I take my nostalgia goggles off... What do I see?
I see problems plaguing the game that will likely turn people away from this masterpiece. At it's core, it really is a Banjo-Kazooie successor. The first game, not a Tooie successor. The elements from the first Banjo-Kazooie that made it into Yooka-Laylee are both great and bad. The elements from Tooie that they pulled are also both great and bad. There's things missing from this game that made Kazooie and Tooie special.
The most obvious flaw for me is the extreme lack of enemy variety. Literally all of the ground minions are reskins of the Corplets you fight in the hub world. The Bee enemies are annoying, the underwater enemies are lacking and the big minion is a bit OP until you figure out to just consistently Buddy Slam him.
Trowzer felt lazy to me. Lazy as in they didn't feel like spreading him throughout the maps to find your moves and pay for them. Instead, you find him in his pre-determined spot and pay a sad amount of Quills to become what I will essentially call a god. Some of the moves Trowzer gives you aren't always needed as well. I distinctly recall glitching my way to Pagies in World 1 just because I had the ability to.
The worldbuilding is bloody fantastic and beautiful. I love it, but there's a problem when you don't simply add giant mountain walls around the edges of your map. You get people walking all along them when they probably shouldn't. There needs to be invisible walls in out of bound areas or something, stop letting me repeatedly exploit the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of your game.
Rextro. Bloody. Rextro. I hate him, don't add him to the second game. If you do, I'll buy a disc of the game and snap it in two. I hate his mini-games, I hate more that I have to play them -twice-. Why should I have to beat his hi-score if I did so during my first playthrough of his arcade? It should have been, beat simple score, beat hi-score. If beat hi-score, collect both pagies at once. God. I hate Rextro.
Kartos. Alright, I dislike Kartos. I don't hate him though, I can see the appeal of a minecart minigame. I'm just not meant for those types of things. I would not be opposed to seeing him again, but man are his challenges annoying. Half of the time I felt like he didn't even respond to my controls. The cooldowns are abominable.
The Bosses! I love 'em all. I want to fight all of them again. The only boss I disliked was the World 4 boss and that's because [REDACTED].
The Muuuusic. It's brilliant. The composers did an astounding job on this game's soundtrack. It's just like the olden games they're meant to represent and WOO-HOO BOY do I love it. It's pretty catchy, but not quite as catchy as BK or BT.
Level Design. Alright so I kind of touched on this but the level design in this game is pretty brilliant. I love a lot of it. I just dislike all of the exploits I can take advantage of in this game, it feels like I'm killing it. However, there were other issues as well. Some areas just have no context to them and are genuinely confusing. They have nothing or do nothing. Some areas that have things to them, are also confusing sometimes. Sometimes things are hidden from you, despite being right in front of you. It's really hard to look past stuff like that.
The Hub World. It's very reminiscent of Gruntilda's Lair from Banjo-Kazooie and I believe that's what they were probably trying to go for here. If that's the case, they did a spot on job.
Amount of Worlds + Expansion. This is the bit I'm stuck on mostly. On one hand, your game only has 5 Worlds whereas previous games such as Kazooie and Tooie had at least 9 of varying quality and environment. On the other hand, your worlds -expand- into even larger worlds. This idea was beautiful to me. It almost makes the game 10 worlds, but it's still only 5. I think part of me is upset that there aren't a couple more worlds to traverse before finally getting to Capital B. Where's the fire or desert world man?
Collect-a-thon. This type of stuff is my jam, however there are things about collect-a-thons that are also just irritating that Tooie managed to fix up real well. In here and Kazooie, you collect your Quills and Notes individually, 200 Quills or 100 Notes. Individually picking up all of these items is a hassle and sometimes leads to you having to backtrack the entire level when you've missed one note or quill and can't seem to find it. Tooie fixes this by bundling the notes into nests and placing them in all of the areas the player should definitely be going through.
Overall. The game is a mixed bag without my nostalgia goggles on. Do I recommend you get it? Yes. Do I recommend you get it right away? No. You should probably wait for a sale or something, it's a nice successor, but it drops the ball in some places. I still love this game and am sad I've already 100%'d it.

Yooka-Laylee could have been the perfect game. All of the pieces were ripe and ready to fall into place. And yet somehow the product is of lesser value than the sum of its parts. How can this possibly be? Allow me to break it down:
I would like to quickly and concisely address the camera right from the get go. It can be incredibly annoying at certain points ( I recall it violently shaking during some sliding segments) but it is fine more the most part, at least in the big wide open areas (which is every area).
To get more obvious points out of the way that people love to harp on: yes, the game has a very "empty" feel to it. Very large worlds with not much to fill them. It can be easy to find yourself lost once in a while.
I'm already getting bored writing this review, I'm ready to put this game behind me and get it out of my brain. I won't call it utter garbage, but it really felt like a chore to finish as I was approaching my 100th pagie.
And wait, I almost forgot to mention the final boss. The combat in this game is lackluster at best (I'm used to INCREDIBLY FLASHY combat I play fighting games) so you already know that the boss fights are going to be weird. Just spin your tail around a lot, mash that junk like you're playing Kingdom Hearts or something. There's a pool of acid hanging around during the final phases of the boss (this boss has too many phases) and during one of the shifts Capital B (spoilers) fell into the acid and the game soft locked. It was total BS! I was sad because I had to start the whole fight over again after that.
My biggest pet peeve about the game is this: Yooka is still "active" while cutscenes are running. So for example, a cutscene is playing during an underwater sequence BUT YOU ARE STILL RUNNING OUT OF AIR EVEN THOUGH YOU HAVE NO CONTROL OF YOUR CHARACTER. So I'm watching a giant ice key unlock an underwater door and at the same time watching my character drown with no options as to what I can do to save him. I experienced the same kind of thing during the later phases of the final boss as well. He was switching from phase 3 to 4 so I had no control of Yooka but one of the boss's shockwaves was still in play and hit me so I lost a little butterfly for that. THIS IS TERRIBLE GAME DESIGN. I should not be taking damage during cutscenes. Period.
I think forcing myself to slog through until the end of this game has made me insane. I am literally insane now. Thanks for reading my review.

Before I start I just want to say that if you are going to buy this game make sure you have a controller. If you only have keyboard and mouse don't get it (at least not yet, at least to me the controls are super bad for keyboard and mouse).
Pros:
* funny characters
* few invisible walls and surfaces that you will slide off. You can basicly walk on any surface that isn't a 90° wall without slidig off it. Not even on some of the NPCs. (I love this design choice so much since it allows us to get to almost anywhere on the maps)
* beautiful graphics
* fun puzzles and minigames
Cons:
* autofixating camera (it can cause motion sickness and there is no way to turn it off)
* no rebindable controlls (not a huge issue but it is still a litle anoying)
* the tutorials are X-box controller only with no option to change as far as I know (there are also a few controlls they don't tell you, mainly slow/fast sliding and the aim mode for shooting projectiles)
* the save  system (the only way to save is auto save after entering/exiting a world or when collecting a pagie. There is no way to manualy save)
Other thoughts:
Everything else about this game comes down to weither you enjoy this kind of game. The music and voices can be anoying for some people (I don't mind them myself, but I can see why some people would).
This game also gave me over 14h worth of content before I even got to the final boss, but a lot of it was exploring the worlds trying to find every collectible (I still havn't 100% so I still have more things to do in the game).

This is the best Star Wars game I've played, other than KOTOR. (Although honestly I haven't played KOTOR II or any of the other Jedi Knight games.)
•The combat system is the best I've seen in a Star Wars game.
•The missions are fun and challenging, even on the regular difficulty.
•The main game is long enough without being too long(unless you're as bad as I am).
•There is a nice amount of character customization, but the species choices are a bit lacking.
•The graphics still hold up well for a game that was made over a decade ago.
•And there is still online multiplayer that is pretty fun.
Now, for the bad stuff (which isn't a lot)
•First off, the vehicle controls are really broken and wonky. Fortunately, you only use a vehicle twice in the game, and it's optional one of those times.
•As I mentioned earlier, the character customization felt a little restricted. For some odd reason, the genders are tied onto the species, which means you can't have a male Zabrak(Darth Maul's species) or a female Keldor(Plo Koon's species).
•The lip-sync is pretty bad, and so is Luke's voice actor, but these were only minor annoyances.
I highly recommend this game, and I guarantee you'll love it. That is unless you hate Star Wars...

I am a space sim junkie that has been keeping tabs on the StarPoint series for a while.  I got this game for free during a give away.  I was curious about warlords and how this whole series plays out, so was anxious to try this game.  Being that a newer version is out, and I just didn't like this take on a space sim, I can't recommend this title unless you specifically like StarPoint and want to play this story...which isn't that great to begin with.
While the graphics are nice, and the space combat is 3d, the size and scale of the system you are in seems unrealistic to me.  I couldn't immerse myself into this game because everything feels artificial, even the planets, asteroids, and gas clouds.  Most everything in the system is on a 2D ecliptic, but one that is static.  Solar systems usually keep most of its debris on the solar ecliptic, but it's obvious this system was made to be a 2D game world drawn on a map.  Most everything is pretty close together too.  It won't take too long to hyper drive across the system.  So my space immersion experience was C grade at best.
Then there's combat.  It's just not exciting.  I can't even see what I am shooting at half the time because the enemies are zipping around and my turrets are auto engaging within their field of view, not the view from my cockpit.  I also didn't like the static camera views.  I wanted to be able to zoom out and look around tactically.  So combat is a C grade, and camera is a D grade.
The powers system, it makes the game feel more like an RPG, not a space sim.  So, it felt sort of like playing a watered down Space MMO.  It was interesting for a time, but I just got bored of driving from nav point to nav point.  When you get to a higher level, I can see that if you specialize your power, you can be quite deadly, but it seems unrealistic to me.  It's gamey, not immersive, just my preference.
Story is 'meh'.  A cliche daddy did secret squirrel hero stuff in the past and I somehow inherit the load when he inevitably dies.  What's worse, I am with him for a time and have absolutely no idea what's going on until I go through a bunch of fetch quests and everyone says, "OH, You are the spiting image of your father, haha".  I just can't get into the role of a kid who doesn't know who is father is and wants to fill his shoes.  It's JRPG F grade material.  A father that actually wants a protege will keep said protege in the loop, else said protege will simply move on to greener pastures.  The main character obviously acts like a pompous brat, so he should have at least been educated by his noble father on what the hell is going on, and not expected to pick up the pieces after daddy's death.
There is a free mode, but I am not interested in trying it.  X3 suits my tastes better.

This game gets so much right about what makes a Hitman game great and then proceeds to crap all over it. I've been a fan of Hitman since the very first game and played (and purchased on different platforms) more hours of Blood Money than I could even guess. I was really hoping that this game would be a return to form for the franchise, and from some of the things I've seen and done in the game I honestly believe that it could have been.
I don't absolutely hate the episodic release, I wish it would have been a full form Hitman game but this gives me some incentive to really flesh out and explore each level. Honestly there seems to be a lot to do in the main Paris mission that we have available, and that really bodes well for each subsequent level we get next.
Now on to why I wouldn't recommend this game in it's current form. I've got a pretty beefy PC rig that should be absolutely able to run this game at 60fps on at least high settings. The entire first "tutorial" mission was initially unplayable due to what seemed to be a problem with shadow mapping, causing the screen to be almost completely blacked out by blown out shadows. After resetting the game multiple times it finally randomly decided to start working. After getting through the tutorial stage I was able to get into the real meat of the game in the Paris level. This time a lighting issue (that I still haven't been able to fix, regardless of what settings are changed) made the game look like absolute garbage with flickering lights and overblown shadows. As long as I wasn't in an exterior environment it seemed to function fine.
Finally to put a stellar cherry on top of this turd sunday I was just about to complete my first Silent Assassin run of the Paris mission when I get this text popup onscreen stating that I was disconnected from the server. In some bizarre choice of DRM the game needs to be online, I assume for the leaderboard to function correctly. One would think that the best option in that situation would be for your game to go into "offline" mode, nope it just kicks you back to the main menu. I will add that the game has an offline mode that I will now be utilizing.
There is great potential here, and honestly it seems like there's many things that IO Interactive could fix. I think this speaks to a larger issue with games in the last five to ten years, the mentality that "hey we could just patch it" if things aren't working. I understand the idea behind releasing patches for obscure bugs/glitches that weren't picked up during testing, but for the game to be nearly unplayable at times is (to me) unnacceptable. For many developers patching seems to have become a crutch. In short, I would wait until a few episodes have been released along with (hopefully) a few patches as well. If you're a fan of Hitman I know you'll recognize the potential this game has, but I still couldn't recommend it as it currently stands. I give it 3 crow suits out of 600 rubber duckies (review scores are pointless).

I was quite disappointed with this game. I was expecting it to be more or less like Blood Money, but with the Absolution style game mechancis and graphics. However, in it's current state, there are a lot of problems and I wouldn't recommend buying it at all.
Cons(-):
- Always Online
- If your machine was just good enough that you could run Absolution on Ultra high settings, you can run this with everything on minimum and it will still lag
- The "Modular" release format leaves this game with a serious lack of content at the time of release; this is pretty much the same thing that happened with 'Elite Dangerous' (i.e. it was released to meet a deadline, when it was obviously not developed enough to be ready for release)
- It feels like the game was based off of the blood money rather than absolution as it's backbone; clues to be found in some glitches from blood money like how sometimes dragging a body would not work
- Running the same mission over and over in different ways is very repetitive; at the moment, there is no variety in missions (there are literally just the tutorials, and one single map! Is this a joke?). Blood money had a lot more content than this. So did all the other hitman games. I would rather play the old ones than this.
Pros(+):
- Honestly, I have no pros to post. As a huge fan of the hitman series up until this point, I am seriously disappointed.
Conclusion:
If you have a machine that can run this on max settings, and you want a good game at similar price point, get 'The Division' instead. Unless they release like 10 more levels in the upcoming patches, this is not worth it at all.
EDIT: Updating my review for the release of the Sapienza portion of the game. IMO if they genuinely only plan to release one more map after this, then that's an absolutely disgusting lack of content. Having been a fan of all previous hitman games, this one is just bad.
However performance-wise, the game performs better on this level than on Paris for some reason. Playable FPS is possible on semi-decent machines if you overclock the GPU (still, you shouldn't have to) but it's still doesn't have the look or feel of absolution. Yes, they spent lots of time making the maps big. But 3 maps does not a good game make and playing the same map over and over in 100 different fashions is just not good. Waiting for the 3rd release, but after the first elusive target and Sapienza, I would still DEFINITELY not recommend this game to anyone under any cirucumstance.

Having played this game for over thirty hours at the time of writing this review I feel confident enough to review it now.
I picked up the Euro Truck Simulator 2 Deluxe Bundle at the recommendation of a friend. I paid about £30 something at the time and got a bunch of rubbish games with it that I played for about seven seconds before uninstalling. However this game was worth the £30 alone.
Euro Truck Simulator is a super basic game. You drive a truck from point A to point B, that's really all there is to it. But don't let that put you off. You still need think about how to turn corners without crushing your cargo, when to indicate, etc. It's pretty realistic. Also, if you go too fast you can tip your truck which I have done a couple of times...
It has full controller and racing wheel support and soon I plan on getting a racing wheel to enjoy this game to the fullest.
The unintended side-effect of this game is how relaxing it is. Cruising down the motorway in a truck, listening to the real radio stations provided to you in-game. It's a great game to unwind with. But be warned. Longer journeys can take a very long time to complete and there is a real genuine risk of falling asleep and having your truck crash during the few seconds your eyes were closed. My tip? Don't bother with the long distance hauls unless you're very very awake and alert.
Apart from that though, I give this an easy 10/10. Especially with all the DLC currently available.

Max Payne is a 3rd person shooter based around mobsters, drug addicts & drug dealers that run rampant in the streets of New York City & you as Max Payne the cities "Ex Cop" which put most of them away for their crimes.
A rather large & compelling story with major plot twists around each corner. You'll need a lot of clarity in your head to grasp the reality of this well written and planned out story that is "Max Payne".
Max Payne's story is set around the player Max Payne who is a Police Officer in the New York Police Department, you're 1 of the biggest cops in the department because of how many cases you've solved and how many criminals you've put away, of course with all the popularity from the good guys the bad guys also see it fit to use you as their scapegoat for a very chilling & deep story.
Max Payne is stuck centered in a mob hit which has his Wife & Baby murdered in cold blood, this leaves Max with a bad case of depression & drug abuse, While Max is on his first job back at the force, Max ends up once again getting stuck in another situation that has his partner killed & him being framed as the gunman, this causes him to lose his job at the police force & leaves him on the run as a wanted criminal.
With major twists around every corner and a very dark and unnerving story you're going to need to experience every second of it to understand truely how the protaganist feels.
Max Payne's gameplay is set around shooting, shooting and more shooting, there's not much sections in the game that don't rely on you killing someone or something. But of course if you were in Max's situation you'd be out for revenge for who set you up & murdered your family too.
The gunplay in Max Payne is very iffy & doesn't feel the best, at times the guns feel too useless & you spend more time retrying sections till you get them right! This gets really frustrating & will often have you quit every half an hour or so.
The use of Bullet Time in this game is one of the cooler features in the franchise.
This game is where "Bullet Time" started for the gaming community only after the Matrix movies started it for the movies. (Props to Remedy for bringing this awesome feature to reality).
Max Payne is one of the few games that doesn't use Quick Saves & Checkpoints so make sure you save frequently or you're going to be starting from the beginning of the game quite a lot!
Max Payne 1 it self is not a bad game, it's quite the opposite, Remedy is one of the best companies i've ever seen when it comes to story telling gameplay, from Max Payne to Alan Wake they're flawless in story with very little to no plot holes & they also have very solid gameplay to boot.
The problem i have with Max Payne 1 is that it's quite frustrating that the weapons feel useless & the NPC enemies will generally rush at you in order to kill you rather than duck behind cover & wait for you to come to them. It feels a bit cheap and because you have no defence when they get in close to you, well you often die fast.
The controls for Max Payne are really REALLY clunky, movement is restricted to only running so don't try to take your time because you can't walk, this was an issue on the Playstation 2 version as well so it's not just PC.
Combat is very nice with Bullet Time but without Bullet Time it can be quite hard to kill the enemies so make sure you save it for when you need it.
Hang onto as many "Pain Pills" as you can because they're your source of health & they're quite scarce and of course without them expect to die alot.
Max Payne is such a great game from it's seriously dark and grim story to it's fantastic Bullet Time & Character Development to the enemies having very interesting and creative dialogue, nothing in this game feels like it's out of place.
My main gripe is the weapons being weak and the enemies being cheap.
I have to give Max Payne a 6/10, it would be higher if there wasn't so many down points for the clunky controls & the weak guns.
The Story & the strong character development is what makes this review stay strong & without these key elements being 100% top notch this game would be one i would warn people to steer clear from, however i just can't say that to such a great franchise,
If you don't like Max Payne 1 for the reasons i mentioned then you MUST play Max Payne 2: Fall of Max Payne because everything bad in this game has been fixed in that game!

Max Payne is a very interesting game. It looks like it was made on a budget of 10 $5 footlongs and a cheap toaster. Max has a permanent constipated look on his face, the textures are really low-res, and the voice acting is sub-par. Those things though are part of what makes this such a charming game. Max's metaphors and similies are like poetry, and the game plays like a dream. The story is gripping, I had no problems getting through it, which I credit to the way it's delivered. The game's cutscenes are almost all in a graphic novel format. You get 4-5 pages of 2 - 3 panels each at the start and end of each segment, 6 - 7 pages of 2 - 3 panels at the end of each chapter, and 1 - 2 pages during gameplay. The shortness of these cutscenes means you're out of them and back in the game in a heartbeat, ready to shoot more mooks in slow motion. Max Payne plays very much like an arcade shooter, with short, frequent encounters and occasional bosses. It's only downfall in my eyes are the dream sequences at the start of each chapter. This is not a platforming game at all, so there's no reason for me to be walking narrow pathways over insta-death pits except padding. Luckily, there are only two of them, and the second one breaks the fourth wall in an amusing way.
tl;dr, buy Max Payne. It's a great value at any price, and a very memorable game.

I'd give this game about 60% good 40% bad. It's not as good as I hoped. I'm no stranger to this style of platformer and I admit that I went into this game with huge hype. I played Banjo Kazooie/Tooie and too many Donkey Kongs to list. I beat it 100% (all collectables, mini games, achievements included at launch) in only 20 hours. My Steam time is higher for the game only because it spent time sitting paused.
The controls are so inconsistent between forms/ground types that they range from awesome to terrible. Running and jumping (the staples of a platformer) work just fine. Some later moves like tongue grappling are great too. More exotic moves like flying and swimming are awkward mostly because of a straight-from-the-90s bad camera.
Levels are too big and not interesting enough. They are visually pretty but the puzzles aren't dense enough so most of the space feels wasted. Art style is fine as long as there's content. I'd have preferred a greater number of smaller worlds instead.
The worst part is that the game doesn't really feel like I'm gonna replay it in the future. I've played Banjo and DK repeatedly because they are amazing platformers. This one just fell short.
It is a definite challenge and while cute, it's not a kids game. This is for 90s kids. We had pre-order tickets to the hype train and we're riding it all the way to its death.

well it's been six hours, probably time to review it...
Lets address the elephant in the room first. Why is everyone so freaked out about JT getting cut from the cast? What this game has is not voice acting. It's the sort of noises I would make when I was 7 years old to irritate my siblings when I was bored. I would probably like this game a lot more if the characters were completely silent when the dialogue was being printed to the screen, the noises they make instead of actual freaking voice acting are pretty annoying.
so what do I like about the game?
It looks amazing! That pre rendered trailer from the kick starter campaign did not disappoint. The controls are fluid and responsive, even relying on my desktops sub par bluetooth card for connectivity. My dualshock worked without any messing about with ds4drv, rumble and everything, so that was nice. The game's humour is 25 carat gold. There is no forth wall, characters frequently address the player. The pun's might wear on some people, but there was not a single joke I did not laugh at so far. The worlds are absolutely huge. If they were any bigger, you could call the game open world. And the 200 feathers per level are no joke to find. It will probably take me forever. The music sounded great, although I think I have already made my views on the voice acting abundantly clear.
Is there anything I don't like?
As state previously, the voice acting is annoying. So too are those quizzes that break up the levels. Yes, nostalgia for that quiz at the end of banjo-kazooie. I hated that as well. Those quizzes are not fun. They are monotonous. If you wanted to make me hate Dr. Quack, then kudos, but I am mad at you too playtonic! Performance is probably worth mentioning. I use Gentoo (linux), and graphics drivers and kernel versions so new, they make the recommended software specs of most games look depreciated. So naturally I expect funny things to happen. Since nothing worthy of an exorcism has happened, I guess the game is stable. Hardware wise I have an AMD fx6300 cpu, an nvidia GTX 950 graphics card and 32 gigs of ram. Far in excess of the minimum requirements to be sure. Most of the time, on the penultimate preset, with some generous overclocking, I get 60 fps. However, in one room of the ice castle, the framerate dropped to like 10. Quite annoying. I was also disappointed to learn that this game does not utilise vulkan, though considering that it's still a beta technology, I should not be so surprised. Finally, capital B rarely ever rhymes. He is still absolutely gas, but I miss that from grunty. Still a better villain though.
Is the game brilliant? yes. Is it flawed? yes. Can those quizzes be removed in a patch? yes please!
Would I recommend the game? HELL YES!

This is a very nicely presented pool game, with everything that a fan of the game would want. It has nine-ball pool (pot the balls in sequence and whoever pots the last ball is the winner), eight-ball pool (the stripes and solids version), trick shots and online play.

Every match in the campaign mode has extra challenges that make each game different and help to ramp up the difficulty. For example, a challenge might be to get a four-ball streak, perform a kick shot, etc. There’s also a few bonus rounds with different modes of play.

Tutorials are excellent. It guides you through each step of the shot and makes it very easy to perform impressive stuff like kick shots, jump shots, combo shots, swerve shots and more. There's a surprisingly large amount of ways to hit a ball.

You can unlock different designs for the tables, cues and balls. You also unlock different locations to play pool in. These are purely cosmetic, but they look great and add to the overall experience.

If the idea of playing pool appeals to you - definitely get this. I personally have very minimal interest in pool, but it’s all so well done that I'm enjoying it anyway.

Strengths:
- Lovely (non-protagonist) sprites.
- Excellent writing throughout, witty dialogue and plenty of pop culture references that feel natural but not overbearing.
- Varied characterization, making it likely to find at least one character you care for.
- What little voice acting there is is fairly nice.
- Auto-save feature is highly convenient.
- While more on the lighthearted and wacky side, the serious moments are still handled very well.
Neutral:
- Music is fairly catchy, but once a file is reloaded in-game, the scene you load to lacks any music. This fixes itself once you trigger a different track to be played.
- Lack of log/rewind/backward button that you can look at without just reloading a save.
Cons:
- The protagonist Dad clashes awfully with the rest of the art onscreen at any time, and at the point of this review, there are graphical errors that make light pixels from the background bleed through the character sprite.
- If you're not invested in every dad, the game may feel fairly short. You basically have three main scenes per dad, which are fairly lengthy but may feel lacking to some.
- Awful bugs, such as a scene that duplicates itself and seems to affect how no one can access one particular good ending. Hugo and Damien's lines are noticeably breathy and a different quality than the rest of the characters. These will assumedly be fixed but does affect my current overall enjoyment of the game.
- There's a lack of consistency to the dialogue. For example, Joseph can ask you if you were ever propositioned by Robert, and your player character can confirm that he did, even if it doesn't necessarily happen in that playthrough. There are other inconsistencies brought up, such as Amanda's mom being referred to as her dad even if you select otherwise, etc.
It's about 8 hours in total if you're only going for the good routes, which in combination with the writing, feels like a fair enough price once all these inconsistencies and bugs are fixed. I plan to replay it later, just due to the enjoyability of the stories.

My totally uncensored (maybe spoiling) review of Dream Daddy: A Dad Dating Simulator will start with the positives:
This is a totally awesome game if you're into a short-lived, maybe 45 minute game at most. There are bright colors and the scenes are well created. The dialogue is also to die for, detailed and informative. It really gets into building character. Also, a lot of My Chemical Romance references if you're into that. Also, all the dads are cute, and have cute voices, so that's a major plus.
Yet, I think I need to note the problems with the game, which I'm saying lightly as I understand this game was created in a short amount of time and by only a handful of people.
It is a short game, and the ending is highly expected. You meet dads, choose your dad of choice, you end up with dad after three dates, your daughter goes through some teenage angst, yada yada, your daughter goes to college, everyone lives happily ever after. It would totally be awesome if there was an actual problem in the game, something you needed to solve, maybe more minigames. Yet, there are only a few minigames, and everything is as expected.
And the dad creator. You get to create your dad, yes, but you don't get a lot of options. And the EYES. None of the eyes look good, none of them are suitable! And not to mention, you don't really get a choice as to your characters personality. He's kinda a loser, very lame, very lazy, sleeps a lot. He's very chill.
All in all, the game is probably worth $5, if any. I've played better free games before. It was short-lived and I think if I ever play it again, it would only to be to collect images for the gallery.
But thanks for the short game, it was a nice and relaxed 45 minutes. I just wish there was more to it. More customization, maybe your character gets a voice, /something/ to spice it up a little so it isn't just a dialogue game you follow along with.
Thanks for reading this far if you did, it's just my opinion and I mean nothing bad about it.
Be proud of the game, there have definitely been worse but there are definitely better, is all I have to say.

On the one hand, you're going to hear a lot of things about this game being a lazy sequel and a shameless clone of Arkham City, and most of them are probably true.  The city covers the same districts, uses the same gadgets and combat tactics, and even some of the same buildings that you've already seen in the last game.
On the other hand, even the worst Arkham game is still better than most other games. The freeflow combat system is back in all of its glory, except that now enemies will attack you much more frequently and with less warning. Part of me is grateful for the realism and added challenge of thugs not just idly standing around waiting for Batman to palm strike them, yet another part of me is frustrated in not possessing the same dominion in mob suppression and crowd control with carefully linked combos that made the previous game fights so enthralling. It was less about Batman trying not to have his clock cleaned, but more about keeping everybody whipped with seamless variety and finesse. Arkham Origins still does this, but you will have to work a lot harder to get it.
The predator system hasn't really changed at all, and at this point is starting to feel tiresome. There aren't really any new takedowns for Batman to use, except one related to a particular new gadget. The levels are also dull and poorly laid out, presenting very few opportunities to set well-placed traps in strategic locations. The explosive gel in particular has taken a big  hit. The gel takedown apparently only works when it feels like it. Half the time the explosion will knock the guys on the ground with stars over their heads for a few seconds before they get back up, with the whole room now aware of your presence. And once you get the proximity upgrade, that stuff goes off whether you want it to or not, even if a guard casually strolls by while you are still spraying it.
Collectibles have again returned courtesy of the Riddler, or "Enigma" as he is currently known, although his distinguished Riddler Trophies have been replaced with generic glowing green squares. These "data packs," which contain extortion data on some of Gotham's highest criminals, are encrypted and dispersed throughout the city and must be unlocked by solving simple gadget puzzles. He has also installed wireless network relay devices scattered at street level in plain view, which Batman must destroy by, brace yourselves,
Well played, Edward.
Except Batman isn't looking to use Enigma's data to expose corruption the city -- he's actually trying to
from doing so because apparently it's morally wrong when Edward does it, or that whistle-blowing on dirty cops, mobsters, and politicians will bring more harm than it alleviates.  Don't ask me how, this is never explained.
This should now bring us to the game's sketchy story. Batman is in his early years, his existence just shy of a mythic folk tale. Corruption runs thicker than blood all the way through the police force, all of whom are dressed in SWAT gear and for some reason carry no side arms.  Gotham City is under a lockdown on Christmas Eve due to a winter storm, but maybe it's more likely a ruse for the Gotham police to easily arrest the gangs. Or maybe the GCPD are so corrupt that they wish to collude with them uninhibited.
The setting looks to be a total reboot to the series, so if you're expecting a prequel or a prelude to the events in Arkham Asylum and Arkham City, you can put those expectations to rest. You start off with most of the same gadgets and upgrades you acquired in Arkham City, despite being about 8 years in the past. Your detective vision is as state-of-the-art as ever, so much that it can run a virtual forensics software that reconstructs murder scenes based on a few scuff marks and blood stains. I did like the CSI: Gotham portions of the game as a new detective-style concept, but most of it is done by simply "Press A to Think."
The pre-Arkham city is somehow less alive and more packed with criminals despite not being a sanctioned inmate internment camp. At least the prison had political prisoners, helicopters, and other non combatants. In this city there are so many criminals that you can leap anywhere off a clock tower and land knuckle first on a class-A felon.  Most of the enemies you will fight are either in
gang, or police officers who are so corrupt that they are, for all intents in purposes, criminals themselves and therefore fair game for Batman (although he does show them more restraint). The police fight with the same AI and weapons as their street thug counterparts. There is nobody else on the street: no innocent bystanders, no homeless people, no emergency vehicles, and no snow plows? All of this makes a once expansive and versatile game engine feel claustrophobic and narrow in scope.
The combat scenarios are fun but get very repetitive. The enemies fight you in groups no smaller than 5, and are so densely populated that you can't help but alert the NEXT group of bad guys on the other side of the fence before the fight ends. The rooftops are no safe haven either, as more gang members patrol listlessly with their assault rifles, waiting to be stealthily subdued in a full nelson under Batman's mighty armpit. Funny how the guard patrols never notice you until you land right in front of them, but two guys talking to each other on street level will spot you instantly.
Just in case you didn't have enough excuse to indiscriminitely beat people senseless, you can now respond to APBs for crimes on the street, just to give you more excuses to snap limbs. What's strange about this is sometimes the perpetrators are in fact fellow Gotham police officers. I have to say it's an inspiring display of integrity of a notoriously dirty police force to report their
crimes, but if there are no citizens out and about, then who's calling 911? And who do the dispatchers expect is going to respond?
The villains in the story are well represented and true to their archetypes from the comic and film universes. Bane, for example, is as tenacious and cunning as he is brutishly strong, with the former mirroring his film adaptation and the latter from the comics. The Mad Hatter makes another completely random appearance, this time taking Batman into Wonderland. It's creative and pretty, but too short and too much a novelty to count.
The Joker, however, completely stands out as the truly definitive version of himself. Standing in for Mark Hamill who retired from Arkham City, Troy Baker is a phenomenal second choice. He is a dead ringer for Hamill's joker, and most untrained ears (and even many trained ones) would not be able to tell them apart. The script and dialog are much better as well. The Joker that we saw in the previous Arkham games was essentially the reckless cartoon villain that we've seen in the animated series. While he was ostensibly dangerous in Arkham Asylum and City and had a significant body count to his name, he seemed too much of a goofball to be a criminal mastermind. The writers kept using little anecdotes to remind us that he was a psychopath and therefore capable of real harm. In Arkham Origins, the Joker lets his actions speak for themselves, and really knows how to get things done. He's meaner, more theatrical and razor-witted, and his carefree disregard for the lives of anyone including his own makes him all the more chaotic and downright frightening.
What you should take from this is a recommendation if you love the Arkham games and need your Batman fix. If you're looking for something fresh and new, wait for Rocksteady's Arkham Knight.

I've been a fan of the Batman: Arkham series since it's inception. I've eagerly awaited each release, bought each DLC, and played countless hours in the first two games. They were nothing short of spectacular.
Where the first (Arkham Assylum) established what playing as the Bat should feel like, the second (Arkham City) created a fantastic story complete with some of the best voice acting done in a game to date.
This latest installment, Arkham Origins, undoes both the gameplay of the first (by having frequent glitches and crashes) and the story of the second (in that this one feels rushed, uninspired, and pushes the limits of credibility). Origins represents a large step backwards in the series, and a collasal disappointment.
Saddest of all, perhaps, is that this game is meant to mark the last performance of Kevin Conroy (voice of Batman since the pivotal animated series in the 90's).
I can only hope that Rocksteady -- the developers of the first two -- will retake the reigns for the next installment and bring a return to form which makes us forget about this mistep.

I must say that i have no idea where all the negative reviews for this game come from, as i find it to be exactly what it is advertised to be, a return to the collectathon 3D platforners of the N64s heyday.
In other words exactly what i and certanly many others have been looking for on PC for a loooong long time.
The graphics are beautiful, the controls are smooth and very easy to understand if you have ever played a game of this type before, and I have certainly enjoyed my time with it immensely thus far.
It certainly isn´t a game for everyone, but then again, no game ever is. I spoke to a couple of friends about this just yesterday as all of us tend to like different games and different genres best, and among us i certainly am the target audience for this game, the rest of them much less so.
So ask yourself if this is a genre you like, if so, i believe you will enjoy your time with this game immensely.
As for the complaints, well, yes there is no voice acting, no one said there would be, and quite frankly i see absolutely no reason for it, on the contrary the grunts and squeaks are exactly what i expect from a game like this and therefore don´t detract from the experience, they add to it. Quite frankly i find the kind of voice acting one tends to find in games like this annoying at best most of the time as most of the time the so called funny voices wear out their welcome extremely quickly.
As for the camera beeing a bit problematic here and there, well, it´s not as if that is anything not present in any other game of this kind, and in some way it wouldn´t really be a faithful adaptation of the classics of old without it. Of course i wouldn´t mind not having them, but i expected what i got, and thus it may not be a plus for the game, it isn´t really a negative either.
As for it requiring a controller to play properly, well, let me put it this way: get a freaking controller already, we are way, way past the point were it is uncommon for PC users to have one of these lying around, and i find complaints about games not beeing optimized for mouse and keyboard when they are in a genre that is clearly best played with a controller annoying at best and downright aggravating the rest if the time, as these comments seem to be trollish to me by now.
As for it beeing a ripoff of the classics? What the hell did you expect from a game that is advertised as an hommage to the games you compare it to? It is supposed to feel like them.
And lastly, it becoming stale and boring, what can i say, hasnßt happend to me yet, and if this is what you experienced, sucks for you, but in the end, thats the one thing that is different for all of us, some games just click, others just dont, no matter if you normally like or dislike similar games, this one is always up in the air as everybodys tastes are simply different.

I've been playing through without a guide and I'm loving every second of it. The worlds and characters are beautifully rendered, the writing often made me laugh out loud, and the gameplay feels really solid.
I've seen people complain about the camera, but honestly, besides a few forced camera angle transitions, it was never an issue for me. I've also seen people complain about boring levels / puzzles / gameplay and, you know, that's their opinion and all, but I've found it to be the complete opposite. There are some tough bosses, but they're a challenge and never unfair.
I guess I'm being ageist, but I do think people who grew up with these types of games will probably 'get' it and have a lot of fun with it.
It's a great game and definitely worth adding to your collection.

I think the most damning criticism I can give for this game is that I was sitting at 101 pagies and I thought to myself, "Hm... do I want to even bother with level 5?".
Something has clearly gone terribly, terribly wrong when the drive to collect the things in a collectathon sputters out. It was probably unwise to design the five levels to hold 25 pagies each yet still have them feel utterly barren, all the while only needing 100 out of 145 pagies to tackle the final boss. People more eloquent than me have probably tread these points into dust so my succinct and witty take on this game is that it skews closer to Banjo-Tooie than Banjo-Kazooie and that is ultimately a bad thing.
Not to say Yooka-Laylee was all bad; I did enjoy myself for a good half of the playtime, exploring and getting the things. But soon the attrition and fatigue of the more Tooie-ish design ethos started to wear me down and I ended up only skimming the unexpanded Galaxy Galleon (or whatever it's called) for three pagies and Trowzer's moves so I could move on to the final boss.
Ultimately the game is fine. It's okay. It's not fantastic, nor is it horrible. People who instinctively bop their heads to Grant Kirkhope's Danny Elfman-esque tunes or make up Gruntilda couplets for fun will have a great time as they're already beyond help. Everyone else will either get too annoyed by all the little niggling flaws or end up rushing the endgame as the game can't really stop you from brute forcing most of the platforming challenges with the flying move. It's definitely worth playing at some point if you had any kind of nostalgia for the salad days of Rareware's 3d platforming collectathons  and Rareware in general before Microsoft eroded them into a pile of sad pencil shavings but I also wouldn't blame you for waiting for a sale.
For now, I give it a 5/10. For reference, Banjo-Kazooie is an 8/10, Banjo-Tooie is a 3/10, Grunty's Revenge is a 2/10, DK64 is a 1/10, and Star Fox Adventures is a -23/10. Better luck next time, lads.

When Yooka-Laylee's Kickstarter was still going, I wasn't particularly interested, but having played the game now, I wish I had backed it while I could.
Overall the game was great in my opinion. I feel because of my lack of investment, financially and otherwise, I didn't have built up expectations which could greatly affect or even ruin an otherwise fine game experience, which is what I suspect at least a small portion of players may have had.
The gameplay is solid for the most part, with only minor kinks that don't usually affect the game. The collision detection on the environment is much more precise than a lot of platformers bother to do (ledges and bumps on most walls can be stood on, for example), which encourages exploration.
The difficulty isn't overly easy, but there aren't that many difficult objectives either, a small amount can feel borderline tedious due to their length, but those are thankfully few in number. I was glad to see that the majority of the collectables weren't placed in overly esoteric locations which could have been annoying to look for, which was a problem I was afraid of encountering.
I initally doubted the game's length, thinking it was much shorter than it turned out to be, but having spent 30 hours on it, I'd say it's plenty long.
The music is great enough that I felt getting the Digital Deluxe edition was worth it for the soundtrack alone. I've found myself listening to certain tracks a lot.
Platformers used to be my number one favorite genre by far and this game helped me remember why, I definitely recommend getting this for any avid lover of platforming adventure games. It made me want to replay some of the old platformers, which I just might do.

Yooka-Laylee isn't quite as good as the classic Banjo games or Mario 64/Sunshine but it's still a ton of fun and likely the best game of its type on steam, I look forward to whatever Playtonic do next.

Undertale, is one of my favourite games to date. It ranks in my top 10 if not then my top 5.
Visuals - 8/10: Undertale is a retro style game that looks like it belongs on the SNES. With great art for every monster and
area in the underground. Although some of the art can be kind of crude (The main character sprite is an example) this is the only problem i could find with the art as everything else nears perfect for this kind of game.
Audio - 9/10: The music of undertale is by far one of it's best elements. A lot of the soundtrack is up-beat and chill songs to give joy to the areas such as "Snow" and " Can You Really Call This A Hotel I Didn't Receive A Mint On My Pillow". They just add so much atmosphere. Along side these tracks are the boss themes which include "Spider dance" and "Hopes and Dreams", this game's boss themes are incredible in fact "Hopes and Dreams" is one of my favourite songs in general. They really add to the tension of the fights and in some cases may even bring out varied emotion. You will definitely want to download this soundtrack to your phone or Mp3 player. The only reason it's not 10/10 is because a few of the songs are reused in other songs but still mixed well into a different variation.
Gameplay / Characters - 10/10: The gameplay is generic RPG gameplay with a loveable twist. You don't have to kill or hurt anything. The way you pass through the game is entirely up to you. The battle mechanics are also great. Smooth and clean, when you fight you become a small heart that reprisents your soul. I don't want to spoil too much but I wouldn't give this 10/10 for no reason. Characters are loveable too. You're able to get a very clear understanding of who and what they are upon meating them and you will get attached very quickly, even to side characters like the Snowdin residents or just generic monsters scattered around.
Overall I adore this game and even though the fanbase can be quite "cringe" at times. The good side heavily out-weighs the bad. This game gets a 9.5/10 and a strong recomendation.

Garfield Minus Garfield (also known as Jon Arbuckle) is a webcomic created by Dan Walsh, a technology manager from Dublin, Ireland,[1] which received considerable attention during 2008. Each strip consists of a reprint of a past episode from the comic strip Garfield, from which all the characters except Garfield's owner Jon Arbuckle have been removed through photo manipulation.[2][3] Though Walsh admits that he was not the first to come up with this idea,[4] he was the first to "champion and popularize" it.
Paws, Inc. publishes an identically named and themed strip on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.[5]

Content[edit]
Without the presence of Garfield, the resulting strips consist mostly of Garfield's owner, Jon Arbuckle, interacting with himself, rather than with his pet cat. The strip's website characterizes this result as "a journey deep into the mind of an isolated young everyman as he fights a losing battle against loneliness and depression in a quiet American suburb."[6]
Reception[edit]
Garfield creator and artist Jim Davis has commented on the webcomic, stating that he is an occasional reader and finds it "fascinating"[1] and an "inspired thing to do".[7]
Publication[edit]
On October 28, 2008, Ballantine Books released a Garfield Minus Garfield book in full color, with the original comics alongside the "minused" ones.[8] It is credited to Jim Davis (who officially sanctioned its publication), with a foreword written by Dan Walsh. Inside the book, however, most of the content is devoted to a section with "Garfield Minus Garfield Strips by Dan", followed in the end by "A word from Jim Davis" and a small section of Davis' own attempts at making Garfield Minus Garfield strips.[9]
Paws, Inc. published its own Garfield Minus Garfield from November 3, 2008 to July 21, 2010, and resumed publishing on April 25, 2012. Unlike Walsh's version, it also includes the original Garfield strip underneath.[5]

Strengths:
- Lovely (non-protagonist) sprites.
- Excellent writing throughout, witty dialogue and plenty of pop culture references that feel natural but not overbearing.
- Varied characterization, making it likely to find at least one character you care for.
- What little voice acting there is is fairly nice.
- Auto-save feature is highly convenient.
- While more on the lighthearted and wacky side, the serious moments are still handled very well.
Neutral:
- Music is fairly catchy, but once a file is reloaded in-game, the scene you load to lacks any music. This fixes itself once you trigger a different track to be played.
- Lack of log/rewind/backward button that you can look at without just reloading a save.
Cons:
- The protagonist Dad clashes awfully with the rest of the art onscreen at any time, and at the point of this review, there are graphical errors that make light pixels from the background bleed through the character sprite.
- If you're not invested in every dad, the game may feel fairly short. You basically have three main scenes per dad, which are fairly lengthy but may feel lacking to some.
- Awful bugs, such as a scene that duplicates itself and seems to affect how no one can access one particular good ending. Hugo and Damien's lines are noticeably breathy and a different quality than the rest of the characters. These will assumedly be fixed but does affect my current overall enjoyment of the game.
- There's a lack of consistency to the dialogue. For example, Joseph can ask you if you were ever propositioned by Robert, and your player character can confirm that he did, even if it doesn't necessarily happen in that playthrough. There are other inconsistencies brought up, such as Amanda's mom being referred to as her dad even if you select otherwise, etc.
It's about 8 hours in total if you're only going for the good routes, which in combination with the writing, feels like a fair enough price once all these inconsistencies and bugs are fixed. I plan to replay it later, just due to the enjoyability of the stories.

My totally uncensored (maybe spoiling) review of Dream Daddy: A Dad Dating Simulator will start with the positives:
This is a totally awesome game if you're into a short-lived, maybe 45 minute game at most. There are bright colors and the scenes are well created. The dialogue is also to die for, detailed and informative. It really gets into building character. Also, a lot of My Chemical Romance references if you're into that. Also, all the dads are cute, and have cute voices, so that's a major plus.
Yet, I think I need to note the problems with the game, which I'm saying lightly as I understand this game was created in a short amount of time and by only a handful of people.
It is a short game, and the ending is highly expected. You meet dads, choose your dad of choice, you end up with dad after three dates, your daughter goes through some teenage angst, yada yada, your daughter goes to college, everyone lives happily ever after. It would totally be awesome if there was an actual problem in the game, something you needed to solve, maybe more minigames. Yet, there are only a few minigames, and everything is as expected.
And the dad creator. You get to create your dad, yes, but you don't get a lot of options. And the EYES. None of the eyes look good, none of them are suitable! And not to mention, you don't really get a choice as to your characters personality. He's kinda a loser, very lame, very lazy, sleeps a lot. He's very chill.
All in all, the game is probably worth $5, if any. I've played better free games before. It was short-lived and I think if I ever play it again, it would only to be to collect images for the gallery.
But thanks for the short game, it was a nice and relaxed 45 minutes. I just wish there was more to it. More customization, maybe your character gets a voice, /something/ to spice it up a little so it isn't just a dialogue game you follow along with.
Thanks for reading this far if you did, it's just my opinion and I mean nothing bad about it.

I have been looking forward to this game since I heard about it around two months ago. This very morning,  the moment I heard it had released, I literally fell out of bed, smashed my power button and bought a copy of the game for me and my best friend.
I won't lie, I was very worried about this game when I had heard that the premise of it came about as a joke.
But my gods, I was not dissappointed.
The artstyle is clean, crisp and gorgeous. As far as the writing goes, it is incredibly witty, heartfelt and genuine. Dad jokes aside (which are gold, might I add) The character interactions have a certain feel that takes them beyond simply making choices in a dating simulator. They feel far closer to real interactions with real people. Also, your precocious daughter is best kid ever and I will defend her to my dying breath.
The cast of characters are plucky, fun and witty all in their own ways. Trust me when I say that even if there are more than a few dads who don't strike your fancy, take a chance. Go for it. I, personally, was not a fan of Damien or Joseph at first, but they grew on me as I traversed their routes. I'm five out of seven on dads right now.  Please send help.
Musical composure is very important to a game as well, and the soundtrack for Dream Daddy is beautiful and conveys the mood that each song is for perfectly.
I will say what really makes this game a winner for me is the warmth and love than has very clearly been put into this game's development. The inclusion of trans- and bi- characters and the INTENSE lack of fetishization of homosexual relationships- one thing I personally was worried the most about- is a refreshing breath of air from what we see a lot of in today's media and other sources. I seriously cannot tell you how happy I am to see that this game revolved around GETTING TO KNOW PEOPLE, NOT GETTING INTO THEIR PANTS.  Vernon and DDADDS Dev team, if you're reading this, you ♥♥♥♥ing rock. I hope to see more of this from you in the future.

Combat time. Right. I just turn on the auto attack on. Ship moves close, the enemy is destroyed. The enemy that I cant even see against the background. Cant see. Zero player input needed. Dont care. Moving ON

And from the exciting battle to the planet, there is nothing to do. Nothing. MOVING ON
This surely cant be the top speed. Surely there are better way to travel the galaxy than this. Lemme look it up while my ship gets there Ignore window mode. I look on my browser. I wait out the 3 minutes of travel. I land on the planet. Ok. What is the planet going to look like. Huh? Lets see it...And its just a static concept art of a street level view. Amazing. Spared no expense.
Right. I am here to pick up a cargo. Some message about a cargo flashes. Where do  go do it? Do I do anything? Or is it done? Am I meant to buy something? huh? What? Maybe I am done. Lets undock from the planet and see if it continues with the next part.

Another ingame cutscene. Right. Some emergeancy. By this point, i dont care what the story is. I just want to freeroam and i can only do that once i finish this tutorial. I press escape. Nothing. Umm..."S" for Skip? Nothing. Space? No. Backspace. No. Mouseclick? No. I run my hand across the keyboard? Nothing. I cant skip this cutscene. Cant pause it, cant look at the menu. Great.
Cutscene basically tells me to hurry back. Nice. I, AGAIN, make my 25m/s tedious journey back.
When I get there. Cutscene. Again. Unskippable. Something about the hero's resolve for vegeance. Cant skip
Cutscene ends.
At this point, the game asks you if you want to continute as normal campaign or freeroam. I choose freeroam.
Thats it. That was apparently all the tutorials one could ever want. Just movement and auto attacking. No trade system. No upgrade system. No mining, no indepth combat mechanics. Just go from A to B. Shot something.
Furiously smash that Alt + F4 button
Cool off. Reopen the game. Freeroam
Right. Gonna recheck.
Check again. Movement Mousescroll. Right. Confirm that there is ZERO momentum to these ships. Things have mass. Things in this game do not.
Ok. Read more of the tutorial and things on steam. There is apparently like a Boost mode. Right. Is it SHIFT? No. Is it Space? No. Of course. It's B for BOOST. HOW STUPID OF ME. If I want to sprint next time I am in a FPS, I should press B for BOOST. No. Not shift. Shift should do nothing. Thats the only logical thing to do. Shift does nothing. B BOOSTS.
Oh. and of course, coming out of boost, you stop on a dime again.
Pressing Tab. What would that do? Stats? Inventory? Menu? Navigation? OF COURSE NOT. It changes the camera mode.
Pressing Spacebar. What would that do? Jump? BOOST(we already established the answer is NO)? Act like a handbreak(we've already established that these ships can stop on a dime)? NO YOU DIMWIT. It changes the way you point your ship. You toggle whether or not you want orientate your ship to the mouse movement. Right. That is so crucial that it needed the spacebar. I would think that once you choose a camera mode to play with, you stick with it and not change so often that you reserve the spacebar for it.
Right. Lets land and see what this space station offers....And what it offers is again shown to me in this tiny popup box that is only 1/9th of the whole available space. Why. There is all these empty space around it, doing nothing. The worst offender of this is in the ship color customisation. your ship displays within that 1/9 space as a tiny 3d model, not much bigger than a standard RTS vehicle unit such as a Battlecruiser from Starcraft 2. Except, in this, the model is not properly lit and thus you can barely see what you are changing. Great. Other games have a full model view and sometimes in a fully modeled drydock. Again, this game spared no expense.
The real cherry on top is that when you pick a color for customisation, it doesnt show. You have to confirm the color, the popup menu for colorpicking closes and then the changes are displayed. So if you arent happy with the colors, you reopen the color menu again and change and reconfirm so the model updates. Marvelous. Ive seen better color picking on a Warcraft 3 model viewer.

I found Call of Duty Black Ops II to be my favorite in the series to date. The single player campaign is okay but has what you'd expect from a normal Call of Duty campaign on rails, cut scenes, etc. I found multiplayer to be fun and enjoyalbe despite very few changes from previous Call of Duty's multiplayer modes. The "Pick 10" system is my favorite addition. Instead of requiring the player to have a grenade for instance they can remove it and spend a point on another category. Wild cards also add additional customization to the multiplayer loadout by allowing the player to have two primary weapons or two perks in the same category. Of course the players are required to sacrifice something else in return to use the wildcards so it maintains balance. On the zombies side of things I found the zombies to be just as fun as the multiplayer. Each of the base maps were very well made for long rounds of survival with each map requiring different strategies. The DLC maps are definitely worth a look at too. They add a story to these maps and make new challenges for the players. For instance the DLC map "Die Rise" has perks randomly dispersed among elevators throughout the map instead of having them in stationary places. Overall if you are buying this for multiplayer, zombies, or both it is definitely worth it. If you are buying this for the single player campaign only, I would find a better way to spend your way. But for those players who want multiplayer and zombies, this game gives you a good value for your money!

My older brother got me this, remembering I played Banjo-Kazooie and -Tooie growing up, so I got this game for free, and I STILL don't think it's worth it.  I don't want to sound like an♥♥♥♥♥ but I honestly feel like *I* wasted HIS money.  This game makes me want to re-fire up Banjo Kazooie and its sequel, not play Yooka-Laylee.
There's promise here.  I actually would have backed this game when the news of its creation came out, had I had any bloody money to spare in that dark, dystopian age of 2015.  I waited years to get my hands on this and kept up on it as it developed. I was really, really hopeful, but the finished product here is just....  It's flat.  It's missing a lot of the heart and soul of what it's trying to succeed (between this and Tides of Numenara, what the Hell, 2017?  I was mad hype).
It's hard not to sound like a jilted fanboy, and you can't prove to everyone that you're not one.  Just let it be known I can temper my love of the original when it comes to newcomers.  I AM a slavering DOOM fanboy, since I was six, lemme tell ya, but I didn't♥♥♥♥♥♥all over 2016's DOOM, which a lot of the old "purists" did.  So I'd like to set that as precedent.
Anyway:
I made it through three worlds before I just gave up.  The hub world is boring and unintuitively laid out; I usually ended up stumbling into new worlds after running about, confused, for 20 minutes, which is generally the opposite of what you want when you're trying to connect game worlds with a sprawling medium.  Things are never where you expect them to be, and a lot of the new paths you go down after learning new abilities either lead you to a ♥♥♥♥-off Pagie (this game's Jiggies), a dead-end, or a shortcut back to earlier worlds.  I'm not really sure why THOSE are there, because as yet (again, I only made it through 3 of the 5 worlds), I didn't see any Pagies or collectibles I needed moves from a later world to get during my first run of a given world.
The enemies are perhaps the gripe I have most.  I can think of.... four?  Standard Gremlins, fliers which essentially amount to Zingers from DKC, jellyfish, and eyeballs that jump onto props in the level and rush at you.  The Gremlin monsters all have unique skins world to world, but they're rarely more than palette-swaps.  They see you, they scream, they rush.  Dudes with Commissar hats take two hits.  The impact of your spin attack is limp, the enemy model rotates as it flies a foot or two, and poofs away.  Jellyfish have only been in the Ice world, Zingers are everywhere with little-to-no variation between appearances, and the eyes just jump on different objects. Barrels in world 1, snowmen in world 2, jack-o'-lanterns in world 3, etc.  NONE of them are a challenge.  Spin into them, sonar THEN spin into them if you're feeling froggy.  It's really disappointing and completely unrewarding.
The moves are pretty okay.  I like the way the characters animate.  Your move-provider in this game is a snake by the name of "Trowzer" (okay, I snickered at that one).  You give him quills (this game's coins in most games, notes in B-K), he gives you a new move.  They're rarely anything spectacular, and almost all of them are environmental, by which I mean you need a fireflower or a box of cannonballs around to make use of them.  They're NEAT, certainly, but it doesn't really feel like you're increasing your verb-set.
I'd like to say I enjoy this game's approach to sequence-breaking, but if you're a fan of Yahtzee and have seen his review, I have to reaffirm what he mentions.  At first it's neat to jump up on a wall or exposed outcropping to grab an item that the game (ostensibly) expects you to get a new super jump or glide to grab, but later on, you're doing it all the time, and it becomes clear that it's due to laziness.  This is only solidified by later on, when the game gets wise to its own flaws, and insulting invisible walls are set up in your path.  Rather than going through and smoothing out the level construction, keeping you from abusing level geometry, the developers put invisible walls in specific areas that they wanted to herd you through, and it feels really inorganic and cheap.  The biggest♥♥♥♥♥♥of this was in world 2, where there was a fence my new super jump (that I had earned IN THAT VERY LEVEL) was enough to jump OVER, but I couldn't PASS. A fence that was slightly too high for my standard jump.  Thinking I had re-equipped myself to surpass the little fence, I super jump clear over it, only to see my characters float in vain against a barrier I can't see and  have no indication of being there.  It makes you feel cheated.
On that note, yes, the worlds are large, but they are barren as all Hell.  There's no real conveyance, and you'll do little more than roam what are (admittedly, very colorful) wastelands, stomping an effortless enemy every five minutes or so, trying desperately to find a trail of collectibles you haven't already found. The music is okay, but I don't find myself humming any of it like I do with Click Clock Wood or Jolly Roger Bay, or even E1M1, to keep the analogies consistent.
The sound is..... Unimpressive.  Like I said, impacts are limp, and the character voice clips are weirdly annoying. I heard someone say Yooka sounds like a closet molester in his sound clips and I can't unhear it.  Laylee is charming, but her dialogue makes her out to be a profoundly unpleasant person.  Never has a kind word to say about anyone, and rather than how Kazooie was a little scathing toward people you ended up fighting, and traded spirited blows with Bottles (WHO GAVE HER SOME BACK; VERY IMPORTANT), Laylee just ♥♥♥♥♥ on everyone you talk to, and only perks up when talk of payment comes around.  I get what they were going for, but it's missing something; Kazooie makes me laugh, Laylee's just a prick.
Oh, on the note of writing, the game really thinks it will get more credit than it does by acknowledging it's a game.  Seriously, every fifth dialogue (or third time the Big Bad comes up to♥♥♥♥♥♥talk you while you're in the hub), the game lets you know it's a game.  Laylee's responds to a tutorial with, "we know, it means more obstacles and more annoying characters to help" (lol; edgy, right guys?), or Capital B (said Big Bad)'s "I need to outsource the next boss fight!" make it seem like the dev team is nudging you in the ribs going "right?  Right??"  It was charming the first time, but when it's one of approximately three moves somebody has to show you, it'll get old way before the 20-ish hours this game takes to finish are up.
To add to that, the quizzes in this game can ♥♥♥♥ right off.  If you played B-K, you remember Grunty's quiz at the end of the game.  Having to do that more than once would suck, right?  Well, here, you do.  And many of the questions are obtuse to the point of sadism; the game tries to capitalize on that by outright having the character tell you "there are guides online, you know", thinking that by calling attention to its blatant padding, you don't curse it, but drawing attention to your flaws self-consciously doens't absolve you of your flaws.  Especially when they're deliberately caustic, trying to make the ♥♥♥♥♥iness of the mechanic the joke doesn't make a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic any less ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Come on, guys.
The biggest pro I can say?  I like eating butterflies to regain health.  It's a way of gaining health that is more engaging (since perhaps Super Punch-Out!!) than usual, and is just cute to watch, especially the yelp the butterflies let out.  That is literally my favorite part of the game.
TL;DR version:  It doesn't SUCK, but it IS on the ♥♥♥♥♥ier side of mediocre.  If you get this specifically to revive your love of Rare's 64 3D-Platformers, I can't advise it, but if you're new to the genre and have some extra cash and time, get it on sale. BIG sale.  It's bad, it's a letdown, and it left me more DISAPPOINTED than anything else.  Not ANGRY, disappointed. Get a 64 emulator and play B-K 1&2.
I don't have much at all to say.  I was really looking forward to it, and it is very well-made in some ways, but it is really not fun.
